title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs across Text and Audio Modalities for Accessible Disaster Assistance
summary: This research evaluates the performance of multimodal large language models (LLMs) across text and audio modalities to improve accessible disaster assistance. The goal is to address the communication needs of individuals with diverse functional requirements during emergencies.

title: When Uncertainty Isn't Enough: An Empirical Study of Self-Correction in Code Generation
summary: This empirical study investigates the effectiveness of self-correction mechanisms in large language models (LLMs) for code generation, particularly when uncertainty estimation methods are applied. It explores whether these signals can improve code generation reliability.

title: Position: AI Agents in Scientific Teams Should Be Studied as Human-Agent Systems
summary: This position paper argues that large language model (LLM)-based agents used in scientific discovery should be studied as human-agent systems, rather than solely focusing on their autonomous capabilities. It emphasizes the importance of understanding the social dynamics of human-AI collaboration.

title: Beyond Correctness: Toward Automated Novelty Verification with Lean 4
summary: This article introduces AViD Journal, a new pipeline designed for automated novelty verification of AI-generated mathematical theorems within the Lean 4 proof assistant. It aims to address the challenge of distinguishing novel results from already known ones in formal mathematics.

title: Auditing an AI-Generated Mathematical Proof: A Correction to a Greedy Conditioning Lemma in Quantum Parallel Repetition
summary: This paper details an audit of an AI-generated mathematical proof from OpenAI, specifically identifying and correcting a greedy conditioning lemma within its discussion of quantum parallel repetition. The correction addresses a flaw in the original proof's argument.

title: When Agentic Executions Fail: Detecting and Localizing Runtime Faults from Telemetry
summary: This work introduces AGENTCHAOSBENCH, a new benchmark designed to detect and localize runtime faults in LLM-based agentic systems by analyzing telemetry data. It focuses on evaluating the reliability of agentic executions beyond just final task outcomes.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Wireless Foundation Models for AI-Native 6G Networks
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive survey of wireless foundation models designed for AI-native sixth-generation (6G) networks. It discusses how these models enable scalable, transferable, and data-efficient intelligence across various communication tasks.

title: Synchronized Logit Steering: Real-world Steganography
summary: This research introduces "Synchronized Logit Steering," a new method for real-world steganography in large language models (LLMs). It enables embedding hidden messages within natural-sounding text, addressing the limitations of prior methods that require shared prompt contexts.

title: Semantic Uncertainty-Guided Orchestration in Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems
summary: This paper explores semantic uncertainty-guided orchestration as a method for coordinating agents in hierarchical multi-agent systems built with large language models (LLMs). It addresses the challenge of managing uncertainty in increasingly capable multi-agent architectures.

title: Beyond Pass@k: Measuring Reliability and Security of Agentic Code Generation
summary: This research critically examines existing benchmarks for AI coding agents, highlighting misapplications of the pass@k estimator and its impact on reliability and security measurements. It aims to improve evaluation methodologies for agentic code generation.

title: Agentic Data Cleaning Without a Clean Reference: An Experimental Study of Capabilities and Trade-offs
summary: This experimental study investigates the capabilities and trade-offs of agentic data cleaning in scenarios lacking a trusted clean reference. It proposes an evidence-grounded framework to understand how different agent capabilities affect reference-free data cleaning.

title: From Errors to Proofs: Minimal-Core-Guided Repair for Neuro-Symbolic Constraint Solving
summary: This research introduces a "Minimal-Core-Guided Repair" method to enhance the reliability of neuro-symbolic constraint solving with language models. It addresses challenges arising from unfaithful problem translations by LLMs, which can lead to incorrect solver outputs.

title: CEDAR-GRPO: Process-Aware Reinforcement Learning for General Abductive Reasoning in LLMs
summary: This paper introduces CEDAR-GRPO, a process-aware reinforcement learning method to improve general abductive reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs). It aims to enhance LLMs' ability to infer the best explanations, a core aspect of problem-solving.

title: Individual Disempowerment through an Advice Channel: Control Loss when Influence is Endogenous
summary: This paper explores the safety implications of AI advice channels, arguing that even if humans can ignore AI suggestions, endogenous influence can lead to individual disempowerment and control loss. It addresses a long-suspected weak point in AI safety premises.

title: Generated Context versus Governed State: Functional Conditions for Accountable Longitudinal Clinical Reasoning
summary: This paper argues that Large Language Models (LLMs) in clinical AI lack explicit, persistent, and governed representation of patient states, proposing functional conditions for accountable longitudinal clinical reasoning. It highlights the need for AI systems to maintain and recall information about patient history.

title: Do LLMs Know What to Ask and When? Evaluating Multi-Turn Information Seeking
summary: This research evaluates Large Language Models' (LLMs) ability to perform multi-turn information seeking by recognizing underspecified user questions, identifying missing information, and actively asking for clarification. It formalizes this process to assess LLM interaction capabilities.

title: MINT: Min-Selection Preference Distillation for Balanced Multi-Objective Alignment
summary: This paper introduces MINT (Min-Selection Preference Distillation), a new method for balanced multi-objective alignment of language agents, addressing the challenge of preventing optimization from collapsing onto the easiest objective. It aims to improve preference-based training for agents.

title: What the Reranker Sees: Multi-Aspect Page Annotation for Long-Document Multimodal Question Answering
summary: This research investigates the effectiveness of rerankers in long-document multimodal question answering, proposing multi-aspect page annotation to improve evidence selection within retrieve-then-read pipelines. It analyzes the bottleneck shift from retrieval recall to reranker-side evidence selection.

title: Discovering High-Quality Chess Puzzles with Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research applies offline reinforcement learning to discover high-quality chess puzzles, aiming to automate the generation of effective pedagogical materials for skill mastery. It addresses the challenge of creating domain-specific educational content.

title: JarvisBench: Always-on Intelligence Between Humans and Agents
summary: This paper introduces JarvisBench, a framework designed to address the bidirectional coordination problem between long-horizon AI agents and humans, where agents operate continuously while human attention is intermittent. It focuses on ensuring always-on intelligence and seamless interaction.

title: Personalized Auto-Research: Towards a True AI Co-Scientist
summary: This paper explores the development of "AI co-scientists" that can generate hypotheses, design experiments, and draft papers, moving towards personalized auto-research. It focuses on creating advanced agentic systems to assist and collaborate in scientific discovery.

title: Frontier AI Forecasting Has a Measurement Problem: An Audit of Progress Evidence
summary: This paper audits the public measurement record used for forecasting frontier AI progress, identifying a measurement problem regarding the connections between dated targets and trends in benchmark scores or training compute. It questions the reliability of current AI progress evidence.

title: LLMs Can Predict Failure Risk, But Struggle to Predict Which Collaboration Protocol Pays Off: Cost-Aware Protocol Routing Across Reasoning Tasks
summary: This research investigates how multi-agent Large Language Model (LLM) systems can improve reasoning, focusing on cost-aware protocol routing to determine when additional collaboration is beneficial. It explores the challenges of predicting the payoff of different collaboration protocols for agents.

title: Small Models Scout Bottleneck Order for Large-Model Data Control
summary: This paper proposes using small proxy models to scout the order of skill bottlenecks for larger models, aiming to optimize data control and training trajectories. It introduces a method for first-passage skill training.

title: Trust Is Not Enough: Influence Calibration for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Agentic RL
summary: This research introduces influence calibration for on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) in agentic reinforcement learning, arguing that teacher trust alone is insufficient for effective token-level supervision in language agents. It aims to improve how agents learn from self-teachers.

title: RETRACE: Resilience-Guided Trait-Conditioned Craving Estimation from Wearable Physiology in Opioid Use Disorder
summary: This research introduces RETRACE, a system for resilience-guided and trait-conditioned estimation of opioid craving using wearable physiological signals to support proactive interventions for individuals with opioid use disorder (OUD). It focuses on detecting subjective craving despite evaluation challenges.

title: T-LLM Compiler: Trusted LLM-based Code Optimization and Verification Framework
summary: This paper introduces the T-LLM Compiler, a trusted framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) for code optimization and verification, aiming to overcome LLMs' current limitations in applying extensive code transformations. It provides a structured approach for enhancing code quality.

title: Does a Tool Result Carry More Authority Than Plain Text? Three Prospective Studies of False-Claim Adoption in a Synthetic Assignment Task with Claude Opus 5
summary: This research investigates whether claims presented as "tool results" or "retrieved" carry more authority than plain text for language models, using Claude Opus 5 in synthetic tasks. It examines how this influences the model's adoption of false claims.

title: Forward Pass Domain Adaptation (Without Cross-Layer Backpropagation)
summary: This paper introduces Forward-Pass-Only (FPO) MLP training, a novel domain adaptation method for large language models that operates without cross-layer backpropagation. This technique achieves substantial throughput and memory efficiency improvements during fine-tuning.

title: Coarse-to-Fine Multi-Resolution Diffusion Models for Trajectory Generation in Urban Systems
summary: This research proposes coarse-to-fine multi-resolution diffusion models for generating human trajectories in urban systems, addressing privacy concerns and limited availability of large-scale mobility data. It offers a new method for understanding urban dynamics.

title: Geometry Is Not Robustness: A Trajectory-Level Study of PGD Evaluation
summary: This paper conducts a trajectory-level study of Projected Gradient Descent (PGD) evaluation for adversarial robustness, arguing that final accuracy is insufficient and proposing deeper diagnostics of model behavior during attacks. It critiques and refines methods for measuring model resilience.

title: DumpsterCluster: From Dumpster Diving to Serving LLaMA-70B on $60 GPUs

title: Calibrated Trust, Not Sharper Prediction: An Empirical Test of Uncertainty Fusion
summary: This paper proposes and empirically tests methods for fusing different uncertainty tools to improve case-outcome prediction in legal AI, using 1,000 real European Court of Human Rights cases. The goal is calibrated trust rather than just sharper prediction.

title: PIKFNO: An Interpretable Neural Operator Based on Physics Informed Kernel Function
summary: This work introduces PIKFNO, a new interpretable neural operator framework that integrates physics-informed kernel functions derived from governing equations into its architecture. It aims to improve model interpretability and physical consistency.

title: Explaining Reinforcement Learning Decisions in Self-adaptive Systems
summary: This paper addresses the lack of transparency in Reinforcement Learning (RL) policies, particularly deep RL, which hinders user trust and verification in autonomous and self-adaptive systems. It highlights the challenges in understanding these AI decisions.

title: Metaplasticity as adaptive gradient preconditioning for incremental learning
summary: This research explores metaplasticity, a biological mechanism preventing catastrophic forgetting, as a potential method for adaptive gradient preconditioning to improve incremental learning in artificial intelligence systems. It draws inspiration from biological intelligence.

title: Fractional Optimizers Meet Fractal Activation Functions: An Empirical Study of Multi-Scale Optimization in Neural Network
summary: This empirical study investigates the combination of fractional optimization methods and fractal activation functions to enhance neural network training through multi-scale optimization. It examines these two independent approaches for performance improvement.

title: Early Cycle Charge Trajectory Generative Prediction and Full Life Cycle Health Management of Iron-Chromium Flow Batteries Based on FlowBD-E1

title: Randomly initialized autoencoders: fixed points and edge-of-chaos

title: Valid Per-Field Selective Risk Control for Document Extraction: Three Failure Modes, a Validity Ladder, and When Conditioning Pays
summary: This paper examines valid per-field selective risk control for document extraction systems, identifying three failure modes and proposing a "validity ladder" to ensure the error rate among accepted fields is properly controlled. It analyzes when conditioning improves performance.

title: BDIP-Net: Dual-Interaction Graph Learning for Property Prediction of Bilayer Materials
summary: This work introduces BDIP-Net, a dual-interaction graph learning method designed for predicting the properties of stacked bilayer materials. It addresses the challenge of accurate structure generation and property prediction for these materials.

title: Training and Evaluating Ethical Reinforcement Learning Agents on Per-Episode Distributions
summary: This paper investigates the challenge of training ethical Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents, addressing how they exploit gaps between designed rewards and intended behaviors. It proposes methods for training and evaluating these agents based on per-episode distributions.

title: DUET: Dual-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Same-Weight Disagreement for Prohibition Compliance
summary: This paper presents DUET, a dual-teacher on-policy distillation method using same-weight disagreement to enhance Large Language Model (LLM) compliance with runtime-injected prohibitions like enterprise policies or PII redlines. It addresses limitations of conventional post-training methods.

title: iFuzz-Meta: An Interpretable Fuzzy Learning Framework Bridging Top-Down and Bottom-Up Knowledge Integration
summary: This paper introduces iFuzz-Meta, an interpretable fuzzy rule-based learning framework that integrates top-down and bottom-up knowledge. It aims to achieve both high performance and human-understandable explanations in neural computation.

title: SMOPD: Selective Token-Entropy Masking for Dirty-History Multi-Turn On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: This paper proposes SMOPD, a method utilizing selective token-entropy masking for dirty-history multi-turn on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). It aims to mitigate the brittleness of OPSD when a student model emits erroneous intermediate replies, focusing corrective signal more effectively.

title: Discrete Diffusion Language Models Are Training-Free Multi-Label Classifiers
summary: This paper introduces dLLM-SetScore, a training-free method that leverages discrete masked-diffusion language models for multi-label text classification. It operates by posing yes/no questions for each candidate label and comparing answer token probabilities.

title: Paired Exact-Reset Evaluation of a Prediction-Derived Medium-to-Full World-Model Cascade
summary: This research evaluates a prediction-derived medium-to-full world-model cascade, examining whether a cheaper "Medium"-derived interface can accurately predict when to switch to a separately frozen "Full" prediction model for additional computation. It uses paired exact-reset physical outcomes for evaluation.

title: Pushing the Limits of High-Resolution Weather Forecasting through Data Scaling
summary: This paper addresses the limitations of developing 0.1$^{\circ}$ global weather forecasting models using machine learning due to scarce high-resolution data. It explores approaches to push these limits through data scaling strategies.

title: Do Uncertainty Signals Help? A Systematic Study of Uncertainty-Aware Decoding with Rollback Mechanisms
summary: This systematic study investigates whether uncertainty signals improve code generation in large language models by evaluating uncertainty-aware decoding with rollback mechanisms. It quantifies the utility of prediction uncertainty for enhancing model performance.

title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Perception-Decision Misalignment in Omni-LLMs via Modality Subspace Activation
summary: This paper diagnoses and proposes mitigation strategies for Perception-Decision Misalignment (PDM) in Omni-Large Language Models (Omni-LLMs), where decisions do not faithfully reflect multi-modal perceptions. It suggests using modality subspace activation to address this issue.

title: P2E-VQ: ECG-linked representation augmentation for PPG via discrete patch retrieval
summary: This work introduces P2E-VQ, a method for enhancing Photoplethysmography (PPG) representations by augmenting them with Electrocardiography (ECG) data through discrete patch retrieval. This improves the prediction of cardiac conditions despite PPG's limitations.

title: LUNG-KGMM: Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Learning for Lung Cancer Incidence Prediction
summary: This paper proposes LUNG-KGMM, a knowledge-guided multimodal framework for predicting lung cancer incidence. It aims for early risk identification by leveraging structured clinical knowledge and multiple data modalities, overcoming limitations of current models.

title: pico-type: A 1.5M-Parameter Byte-Level Multi-Head Content Classifier
summary: Introduces pico-type, a 1.5M-parameter byte-level multi-head content classifier that predicts seven content properties from raw UTF-8 bytes in a single forward pass without tokenization.

title: Ring-based Spatial Transformer: Learning Non-linear Spatial Interactions between Building Distribution and Pedestrian Flow
summary: This study proposes a ring-based SpatialTransformer to learn non-linear spatial interactions between building distribution and pedestrian flow, using concentric ring buffers around railway stations in Tokyo.

title: In-Context Learning to Assess Built Environment Impacts on Perceived Neighborhood Walkability Among Mobility-impaired Older Adults
summary: This study investigates the utility of in-context learning (ICL) to assess how built environment factors impact perceived neighborhood walkability for mobility-impaired older adults.

title: Quantifying Depth Sufficiency in Residual Neural Networks: A First-Order Criterion
summary: This paper proposes a first-order criterion to quantify depth sufficiency in residual neural networks, studying it under a function-preserving residual-growth protocol.

title: When Does the Best Sampling Temperature Rise with the Budget? Sufficient Conditions for Pass@k
summary: This paper investigates why the optimal sampling temperature for `pass@k` often rises with the sampling budget, providing sufficient conditions for this phenomenon observed in multi-sample inference studies.

title: ARGUS: Attention-Guided Transformers for Scalable Person Identification Using Wi-Fi Telemetry
summary: This paper introduces Argus, a passive Wi-Fi sensing system that uses attention-guided transformers for scalable, device-free person identification.

title: Take it Personally: The Limits of General SSL Representations for Real-Life PPG Emotion Detection
summary: This work evaluates the efficacy and limits of general Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) representations derived from photoplethysmography (PPG) for real-life, subjective emotion detection.

title: RouteTS: Frequency-Time Routing for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Introduces RouteTS, a frequency-time routing method for time series forecasting that addresses the limitations of existing approaches by disentangling global periodic structures and localized non-stationary variations.

title: One Score, Two Decisions: Selective Prediction on the Rare-Disease Tail
summary: This paper proposes a method for selective prediction in diagnostic systems, enabling them to decide when to endorse a prediction or defer it for review, especially for rare diseases.

title: Mitigating Rubric Interference in LLM Judges via On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: This paper proposes mitigating rubric interference in LLM judges via on-policy self-distillation, aiming to improve efficiency and accuracy when evaluating responses against multiple fine-grained rubrics.

title: Rethinking Reverse KL as Adaptive Entropy Distillation
summary: This paper rethinks Reverse KL divergence as adaptive entropy distillation, proposing an improved knowledge distillation objective for transferring capabilities from large language models to smaller student models.

title: A Reproducibility Study of Partial Residual Ablations in Pre-LN Transformers
summary: This paper presents a reproducibility study of partial residual ablations in Pre-LN GPT-style transformers to better understand the independent roles of attention and feed-forward residual pathways.

title: The Quantum Shortcut: Complex Phase-State Dynamics Reduce the Optimization Steps of Sequence Models
summary: This paper explores how complex phase-state dynamics, driven by the number system (substrate) used in sequence models, can reduce their optimization steps.

title: Tail-Aware Top-$k$ On-Policy Distillation
summary: This paper introduces Tail-Aware Top-$k$ On-Policy Distillation, a method for transferring knowledge between language models by training a student to align its next-token distribution with the teacher's.

title: A Novel Fourier Feature Network for Solving Partial Differential Equations
summary: This paper proposes Fourier Feature Networks (FENs), a novel single-hidden-layer neural network architecture that incorporates Fourier features to solve Partial Differential Equations.

title: Unraveling the Size Determination Mechanism of Nanocrystal Synthesis via Interpretable Neural Networks
summary: This study develops the Nanocrystal Equation Learner (NanoEQL), an interpretable neural network, to unravel the size determination mechanism of nanocrystal synthesis and provide insights into underlying synthetic mechanisms.

title: Generative Learning of Separatrices
summary: This paper explores generative learning for identifying and reconstructing separatrices, which are boundaries separating basins of attraction in multistable, multidimensional dynamical systems.

title: Iterative Refinement Diffusion for Super-Resolved Data Assimilation of Multiscale Physical Systems
summary: This paper proposes an Iterative Refinement Diffusion method for super-resolved data assimilation, aimed at recovering high-resolution states from sparse, low-resolution observations in multiscale physical systems.

title: WANDR: A Benchmark for Wide and Deep Research
summary: WANDR is introduced as a benchmark comprising 500 realistic data-collection tasks designed to evaluate the wide and deep research capabilities of AI agents.

title: Real-Time State-of-Health Estimation and Online Degradation Prognosis from Partial Battery Discharge Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: This work proposes a physics-informed deep learning approach using neural networks for real-time State-of-Health estimation and online degradation prognosis of lithium-ion batteries from partial discharge data.

title: ER-KANs: Efficient and Robust Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Data-Scarce Scientific Machine Learning
summary: This paper introduces ER-KANs (Efficient and Robust Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks), a new variant designed for data-scarce scientific machine learning. It benchmarks various KAN architectures to evaluate their performance on noisy data.

title: p-Spin Glass Network Efficient Single-Batch Continual Learning
summary: This research introduces the p-Spin Glass Network, a novel architecture designed to improve sample efficiency and continual learning. It aims to overcome limitations of modern sequence models regarding memory footprints and large-batch stochastic optimization.

title: Is Grokking a Loss of Normal Hyperbolicity of the Interpolation Manifold?
summary: This paper investigates the grokking phenomenon in neural networks, reframing its post-memorization phase as a constrained optimization problem. It explores the dynamics of models along the zero-loss manifold.

title: Disentangling Homophily and Rarity: Explaining Failure in Graph Neural Networks
summary: This research aims to disentangle whether classification failures in Graph Neural Networks for heterophilic nodes are due to heterophily or rarity. It frames this as a subgroup generalization problem.

title: Can Neural Networks Learn by Experimenting on Themselves? Self-Interventional Learning from Functional Consequences to Predictive Self-Knowledge
summary: This work introduces Self-Interventional Learning (SIL), a novel approach where a neural system learns by perturbing its own functional structure and observing the consequences. This enables the system to gain predictive self-knowledge.

title: Degeneracy Counting Quantum Algorithm using Decoherence
summary: This paper presents the CTPQsd# algorithm, a quantum method using decoherence to count the global optima of classical optimization problems. It aims to address the #P-hard task of degeneracy counting.

title: PathFinder: Joint Decompositions of Linked Multimodal Datasets
summary: This paper introduces PathFinder, a method for joint low-rank decompositions designed to uncover patterns and structure in linked multimodal datasets. It extends existing decomposition techniques to enable discovery of commonalities.

title: LLM-based Framework for Generating and Verifying Parallel DEVS Statecharts
summary: This research introduces an agentic PDEVS-LLM framework designed to assist human modelers in generating and verifying parallel DEVS statecharts. It leverages large language models for modeling and simulation.

title: Command-Space Counterfactual Explanations for Pareto-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper proposes command-space counterfactual explanations for Pareto Conditioned Networks (PCNs) in multi-objective reinforcement learning. The method aims to make the local mapping from command and state to action more transparent.

title: Auxiliary uncertainty signals for LLM-assisted systematic review screening: a benchmark across eight Cohen drug-class reviews
summary: This research demonstrates how an auxiliary BERT+GCN classifier can supply structured uncertainty signals to improve the efficiency of LLM-assisted systematic review screening. It presents a benchmark across eight drug-class reviews.

title: HarmProfile: Characterizing Harmful Distributions in Frontier LLMs
summary: This paper introduces HarmProfile, a method for characterizing harmful distributions in frontier large language models (LLMs). It aims to analyze harmful outputs produced during model misbehavior, rather than just treating them as attack outcomes.

title: Multi-Modal Generative Fuzzy System: Fuzzy Inference Guided Large Model Interactive Question Answering Framework
summary: This paper proposes a Multi-Modal Generative Fuzzy System, a framework guided by fuzzy inference for interactive multimodal question answering. It aims to improve joint encoding and integration of heterogeneous information from various modalities.

title: Wiola 13M, a Gated Spiral Attention Architecture for Parameter Efficient Small Language Models
summary: This paper introduces Wiola 13M, a decoder-only small language model featuring a Gated Spiral Attention Architecture designed for parameter efficiency. It targets on-device inference and rapid experimentation for small-scale language models.

title: AutoMem: A Text-Gradient Recursive Self-Improvement Framework for Automated Memory Architectures Search
summary: This paper introduces AutoMem, a text-gradient recursive self-improvement framework for automated memory architecture search in LLM agents. It constructs a discrete search space to optimize memory design, storage, retrieval, and management.

title: LLM Safety Alignment in Low-Resource Languages: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: This paper presents a systematic literature review of LLM safety alignment, specifically focusing on challenges and progress in low-resource and multilingual settings. It highlights that safety guarantees remain weaker in these contexts compared to high-resource languages.

title: Inference-Time Mitigation of Adversarial Political Bias in Large Language Models
summary: This research addresses the critical need to ensure large language models (LLMs) are non-partisan and invulnerable to political bias. It proposes methods for inference-time mitigation of adversarial political bias in LLMs to enhance trustworthiness.

title: Characterizing Rhetorical Misalignment in Decision-Making with Language Models
summary: This research characterizes rhetorical misalignment in human-AI decision-making, exploring how large language models (LLMs) might amplify cognitive biases. It investigates the influence of LLMs on human decision-making processes.

title: DeMTS: Denoising Trajectories as Multivariate Time Series for Hallucination Detection in Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper introduces DeMTS, a method that denoises trajectories as multivariate time series for detecting hallucinations in Diffusion Large Language Models (D-LLMs). It aims to address the issue of factually incorrect or unsupported content generated by D-LLMs.

title: Automatic or Controlled? Repetition Priming Reveals Divergent Processing in Base LLMs, Instruct LLMs, and Humans
summary: This research uses repetition priming to investigate whether language models reactivate prior representations or re-evaluate repeated words afresh. It compares processing in base LLMs, instruct LLMs, and humans to reveal divergent mechanisms.

title: Domain Agnostic Text Redaction from Natural Language Rules using Instruction Tuning
summary: This paper proposes a method for domain-agnostic text redaction from natural language rules using instruction tuning. It aims to provide an automatic sanitization solution for textual data to enhance data privacy and compliance.

title: Which Question Is Your Attention Metric Answering? Attention Rows as Compositional Data
summary: This paper analyzes the composition of attention rows in transformer models, treating each row as a probability distribution over tokens to understand what attention metrics reveal. It investigates how standard comparison tools apply to these distributions.

title: Class Imbalance and Batch Effects in LLM-Based Screening for Systematic Reviews
summary: This study analyzes the performance of LLMs in imbalanced binary classification tasks, specifically for study screening in systematic reviews. It experimentally compares individual and batch processing, with and without prevalence metadata, to understand their influence.

title: Prompting is not enough: supervised baselines and leakage control for measuring shared decision-making with LLMs in pediatric encounters
summary: This research investigates whether zero-shot prompting of LLMs is sufficient to detect shared decision-making behaviors in real pediatric clinical encounters. It also assesses the added value of supervised learning for this application.

title: Beyond Tokens: A Survey on Decoding Methods for Large Language and Vision-Language Models
summary: This survey explores various decoding methods for Large Language Models and Vision-Language Models, focusing on inference-time approaches to ensure outputs align with user intent. It discusses challenges in controlling generative capabilities beyond the training stage.

title: Beyond the pale: Assessing prevalence and contents of extremist speech in LLM training data
summary: This work assesses the prevalence and content of extremist speech within the text corpora used for pre- and post-training of large language models. It addresses a gap in research concerning the composition of LLM training data with respect to trustworthy and safe AI.

title: Writing Style Similarity Reflects Academic Genealogy
summary: This paper examines the limitations of authorship attribution systems, particularly those detecting AI-generated papers, by showing how academic genealogy can lead to inherited writing styles. It highlights how these systems' errors can wrongly accuse legitimate authors.

title: What to Forget in Unlearning? Forget Set Curation for Language Models
summary: This research explores "forget set curation" for machine unlearning in language models, a technique that aims to remove targeted data or behaviors from trained models without retraining. It addresses the challenge of identifying what information models should forget in realistic deployments.

title: Where Does Retrieval Fail? Evaluating RAG Architectures for Agricultural Advisory
summary: This study investigates where retrieval fails in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures, evaluating their performance for agricultural advisory in Bengali. It highlights that aggregate scores can obscure significant differences across various query types and language conditions.

title: Interpretable Cross-Lingual Alignment in Small Language Models: Probing Cultural and Pragmatic Reasoning in Japanese-English Bilingual LLMs
summary: This research probes interpretable cross-lingual alignment in Japanese-English bilingual small language models, investigating their cultural and pragmatic reasoning. It addresses the challenge of understanding LLM behavior in languages typologically distant from English.

title: How Do Agents Fail on AutoResearch: End-to-End Diagnostic Evaluation on 100 Real-World Frontier Research Tasks
summary: This paper presents an end-to-end diagnostic evaluation of AI agents on 100 real-world frontier research tasks within the "AutoResearch" paradigm. It investigates how these agentic systems fail when attempting whole-stage scientific research.

title: Training Leaves Traces: Centered Residual Signatures for Language Model Lineage Verification
summary: This research introduces "Centered Residual Signatures" for language model lineage verification, studying whether model weights alone can reveal shared ancestry between compatible open-weight checkpoints. It addresses the undocumented provenance of fine-tuned, quantized, pruned, and merged models.

title: DA-RAC: Distance-Aware Calibration of LLM Judges for Trustworthy AI Auditing
summary: This paper introduces DA-RAC, a Distance-Aware Calibration method for LLM judges, aimed at improving trustworthy AI auditing. It addresses the issue of miscalibration in context-free LLM scoring, which can lead to false confidence in generative AI system evaluations.

title: RamseyGadgets: A Graph Construction Dataset for LLMs
summary: This paper introduces "RamseyGadgets," a graph construction dataset designed for large language models. The dataset aims to test LLMs' ability to generate special graphs, an important task in graph theory and computer science.

title: Harness the Memory: A Holistic Evaluation of Memory Substrates in Memory Agents
summary: This research provides a holistic evaluation of memory substrates in memory agents, investigating the underlying mediums for how memory is represented and stored. It offers guidance on selecting appropriate memory substrates for long-horizon LLM agents.

title: Handoff-H1: An Orchestrated Vision-Agent System for Material Quantity Takeoff from Construction Blueprints
summary: This paper introduces Handoff-H1, an orchestrated vision-agent system designed for material quantity takeoff from construction blueprints. The system integrates visual perception, reasoning, and construction knowledge to interpret architectural drawings.

title: RecurrentGPT: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation in Transformers
summary: This paper introduces RecurrentGPT, a transformer architecture that uses recurrent modulation to achieve expressive depth while maintaining memory efficiency. It addresses the tension between functional specialization and memory footprint in scaling transformer language models.

title: A Pilot Study of Autocompleting Tokenizers
summary: This pilot study investigates the concept of autocompleting tokenizers to compress transformer inputs, inspired by autocomplete-assisted writing systems. It explores whether information can be omitted and recovered from local context in byte-level tokenization.

title: Why Vision Fails as a Universal Bridge: Rectifying Modality Asynchrony in Multilingual MLLMs
summary: This research investigates why vision fails as a universal bridge in multilingual MLLMs, attributing performance degradation in non-English visual reasoning to modality asynchrony. It analyzes the underlying mechanisms in these models.

title: A Declarative-Procedural Perspective on Expert Routing in Bilingual Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
summary: This paper investigates expert routing in bilingual Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models from a Declarative-Procedural perspective. It analyzes lexical, grammatical, and syntactic processing during English-German bilingual language acquisition in a decoder-only MoE Transformer.

title: Left-Branching Transformers Excel at Right-Branching Languages: Data Shapes Word Order Preferences in Language Models
summary: This study systematically compares word order preferences in decoder-only language models across 192 artificial and diverse natural languages. It finds that models exhibit a left-branching preference in artificial languages, regardless of natural language universals.

title: TRACE-BN: Transferring Bangla-English Tutoring Behavior to a Sub-1B Offline Language Model
summary: Introduces TRACE-BN, a curriculum-guided dataset for training a sub-1B offline language model to perform Bangla-English tutoring, including grammar explanations and error awareness.

title: Time as Structure: Temporal Dependency Graphs for Verifiable Deadline Computation over Legal Documents
summary: Proposes using temporal dependency graphs and language models to accurately compute legal filing deadlines, which are often complex due to various triggering events and suspensions.

title: When Do Concepts Become Functionally Sufficient During Language-Model Training?
summary: Investigates when internal structures and concepts within language models become functional during training by analyzing concept dynamics at different layers and checkpoints.

title: Logical Embeddings for Argument Analysis
summary: Proposes a new framework for machine learning-oriented argument analysis that uses logical embeddings, an alternative encoding exploiting argumentation structures, instead of traditional word embeddings.

title: When AI Rewrites, Classifiers Relax: Uncertainty-Aware Sentiment Analysis on Sarcastic and AI-Paraphrased Social Text
summary: Presents an empirical study on the behavior of sentiment classifiers when processing sarcastic or AI-paraphrased social media content, highlighting challenges in these distributional regimes.

title: The Machine's Internal Clock: Do LLMs Share Human Temporal Illusions?
summary: Explores whether large language models exhibit temporal illusions similar to humans, whose perception of time relies on context and relational cues rather than direct elapsed time tracking.

title: Gated Against One Model, Open to the Next: Option-Only Solvability in Legal Multiple-Choice Benchmarks
summary: Examines how to accurately measure if a model truly "needs" a question to answer multiple-choice benchmarks, proposing methods to assess option-only solvability in legal contexts.

title: Language models suffer from a curse of ambiguity
summary: Identifies a "curse of ambiguity" in large language models, explaining how sampling-driven improvement makes the fidelity of their learned distributions critical and some distributions harder to learn.

title: Do Language Models Consistently Encode the Current Year?
summary: Investigates how language models represent the current time by proposing two tasks that probe the current year using associative reasoning and verb tenses.

title: Why Summaries Turn Neutral: Policy Attribution for Sentiment Drift in Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
summary: Diagnoses why Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF) causes sentiment drift, leading to overly neutral LLM summaries, and introduces Policy Attribution to explain this phenomenon.

title: L3Cube-IndicQuest v2: A Large-Scale Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Factual Knowledge of Large Language Models Across Indic Languages
summary: Introduces L3Cube-IndicQuest v2, a large-scale multilingual question-answering benchmark with 3,471 English question-answer pairs for evaluating the factual knowledge of LLMs in Indic languages.

title: BengaliMCQ: Automatic Generation and Answer Prediction of Academic Multiple-Choice Questions in a Low-Resource Language
summary: Proposes a structure-aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework to improve automatic generation and answer prediction of multiple-choice questions from Bengali textbooks, particularly for low-resource languages.

title: When Stories Evolve: Benchmarking LLM Storytelling Across Agent Architectures in Open-Ended World Simulations
summary: Introduces WSE-bench, a new benchmark for evaluating LLM storytelling capabilities in open-ended world simulations and AI-native games, focusing on maintaining facts and causal dependencies as narratives evolve.

title: BERTopic-Virality Prioritisation: A Scalable Framework for Thematic and Comparative Analysis of COVID-19 and Monkeypox Misinformation on Twitter
summary: Presents BERTopic-Virality Prioritisation, a scalable framework for thematic and comparative analysis of health misinformation on Twitter, particularly for COVID-19 and Monkeypox.

title: TaoLive Digital Avatar Agent Technical Report: Training Agents to Evolve with Their Harness
summary: Describes the development and training of AI-powered digital avatar agents for live e-commerce, focusing on their ability to adapt rapidly to changing business strategies and provide factual replies.

title: Using the Mimi codec for metalinguistic representations
summary: Analyzes the Mimi neural codec within the Moshi language model's semantic token codebook, investigating its effectiveness in capturing mappings between semantic tokens and phone realizations.

title: Hallucination Span Detection with Input-Side Evidence Alignment
summary: Proposes a new method for detecting specific hallucinated spans within text generated by large language models by aligning the output with input-side evidence.

title: QuantumPhaseNet: A Gauge-Covariant Geometric and Quantum-Spectral Theory of Semantic Concept Hierarchies with Prototype Validation of a Classical Quantum-Inspired Model
summary: Presents QuantumPhaseNet, a new quantum-inspired model that extends Transformer representations using a gauge-covariant geometric and quantum-spectral theory for semantic concept hierarchies.

title: MicroVerse: An Instrument for Measuring Self-Authored Identity Drift in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Language-Model Simulations
summary: An instrument called MicroVerse is introduced for measuring identity drift in persona-conditioned agents within long-horizon multi-agent language model simulations.

title: When Less Is Enough: Context Selection and Prompting Strategies for Bengali News Headline Generation
summary: A study investigates effective context selection and prompting strategies to improve large language model performance for Bengali news headline generation.

title: PLSQLBench: Benchmarking LLM Systems for Executable Procedural Database Programming
summary: PLSQLBench is presented as the first benchmark to evaluate large language models' ability to write executable PL/SQL programs, assessed via execution-based tests.

title: Token Distribution versus Data Volume: Domain Balancing in Multi-Domain Meeting Summarisation
summary: Research disentangles whether token distribution or data volume is more crucial for performance gains when fine-tuning LLMs on multi-domain meeting summarization tasks.

title: Aborted but Not Forgotten: KV-Cache Retention Breaks Rollback Consistency in Language Agents
summary: A study shows that KV-cache retention in serving sessions can cause language agents to break rollback consistency, leading models to attend to discarded content.

title: The Null Token Knows: Reducing Message-Free Hallucination in ASR and NMT
summary: A method is proposed to reduce message-free hallucination in ASR and NMT systems by using the abstention signal from the models' reserved null tokens.

title: SEER: Long-Context Reasoning via Selective Visual-Text Compression
summary: SEER is introduced as a new method to enable long-context reasoning for large language models through selective visual-text compression, reducing computational cost.

title: LLMs Get Smarter from Targeted Synthetic Multilingual Data
summary: Research indicates that large language models improve their language-specific competency when trained with targeted synthetic multilingual data.

title: Xemo-Talker: Unlock Emotions Explicitly for Audio-Driven Talking Portrait Synthesis
summary: Xemo-Talker is a new system designed to achieve precise and explicit emotion control for audio-driven talking portrait synthesis, overcoming limitations of implicit regulation.

title: Periocular Soft Biometrics: A Survey and Applications to Multimedia Forensics and Disinformation Detection
summary: A survey explores periocular soft biometrics, discussing their applications in multimedia forensics, identity verification, and the detection of synthetic media.

title: On Cross-Validation for Hyperparameter Optimization of Deep Learning Image Classifiers
summary: Research investigates cross-validation methods for hyperparameter optimization in deep learning image classifiers, especially for small sample sizes in medical imaging.

title: Equilibrium Forcing: Adaptive Video Generation Without Noise Conditioning
summary: Equilibrium Forcing (EqF) is presented as a simplified framework for adaptive video generation and denoising that operates without relying on noise conditioning.

title: PE-CSNet: An equivariant network architecture with learnable patch-based sparse representation
summary: PE-CSNet is a new equivariant network architecture that utilizes a learnable patch-based sparse representation, applicable to compressive sensing in fields like medical imaging.

title: Path2ST: Hierarchical Cell-Tissue Grounded Cross-Modal Translation for Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Path2ST is introduced as a hierarchical cross-modal translation method for predicting spatial gene expression from H&E-stained images in spatial transcriptomics.

title: VideoGAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants on Agentic Video Understanding
summary: VideoGAIA is a new benchmark created to evaluate the agentic video understanding capabilities of general AI assistants and multimodal large language models.

title: AeroGround: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Aerial-Ground Collaborative Reasoning
summary: AeroGround is a comprehensive new benchmark designed to assess the performance of vision-language models in aerial-ground collaborative reasoning tasks for unmanned aerial vehicles.

title: Braided Vision Transformer for Stroke Detection in Multi-view Retinal Fundus Imaging
summary: A new Braided Vision Transformer architecture is developed for accurate stroke detection using multi-view retinal fundus imaging.

title: A Vision Transformer for ECG-Based Detection of Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction Across Multiple Clinical Sites
summary: A Vision Transformer-based method is developed for detecting Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction from electrocardiograms across various clinical sites.

title: Privacy-Preserving Dataset Curation for Kuala Lumpur Urban Traffic: Grounded Vision-Language Detection with Spatial Vehicle-Context Filtering
summary: A method for privacy-preserving dataset curation for urban traffic in Kuala Lumpur is presented, using grounded vision-language detection and spatial vehicle-context filtering for autonomous driving applications.

title: Spatial Attention Noise Masking for Causally Sufficient Interpretability
summary: A novel causal approach to interpretability for computer vision models is proposed, which dynamically masks input images prior to classification.

title: Low Cost Two-Stage Fabric Defect Detection at the Edge
summary: This paper proposes a low-cost, two-stage computer vision system for detecting fabric defects at the edge, aiming to make AI-powered inspection accessible to smaller garment manufacturers. It uses anomaly detection to screen for defects in production.

title: Do CNNs Internally Represent Real and Fake Images Differently? A Hidden-Layer Analysis
summary: This research investigates whether Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) process real and fake images differently internally, analyzing their hidden-layer representations. It aims to understand how CNNs distinguish between authentic and synthetic visual content.

title: IP Protection in the Era of Visual Generative AI: A Survey
summary: This survey explores the intellectual property risks introduced by visual generative AI, such as unauthorized data use and reproduction, and reviews technical defenses to mitigate these challenges. It addresses the legal and technical landscape of IP protection in the generative AI era.

title: Emergence of Transfer Learning towards Specific Identification of Alzheimer's Disease A Prospective Approach
summary: This paper investigates the use of transfer learning with deep learning and machine learning models for the specific identification of Alzheimer's Disease. It explores a prospective approach to applying AI for medical diagnosis of dementia.

title: From Dense Prediction to Visual Editing: Structured Supervision for Unified Image and Video Creation
summary: This work proposes a structured supervision method for unified image and video creation, enabling models to follow diverse instructions while maintaining identity, geometry, and temporal structure. It aims to improve precise visual editing capabilities.

title: PolyComp: A Polycube-based Benchmark for Compositional 3D Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Models
summary: PolyComp is introduced as a new procedurally generated benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models' compositional 3D spatial reasoning and visual recognition capabilities. It challenges models to combine polycube components to form a target solid.

title: Beyond Boundary Noise: Aggregated Aleatoric Uncertainty Fails to Capture Presence Ambiguity in 3D Lung Nodule Segmentation
summary: This research finds that aggregated aleatoric uncertainty measures, commonly used in deep learning for 3D lung nodule segmentation, often fail to capture clinically meaningful ambiguity. It challenges current methods for uncertainty estimation in medical AI.

title: NARRATE: A Multimodal Real-World Australian Driving Dataset for Human-Centred Explanations in Automated Driving
summary: NARRATE is a new multimodal real-world Australian driving dataset created to develop human-centered explanations for automated driving systems. It aims to help automated vehicles communicate their decisions in an understandable way to passengers.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Tool for Combating Child Labour: A Real-Time Edge Vision Pipeline for Child Detection and Age Estimation
summary: This research presents a real-time edge computer vision pipeline that uses AI for child detection and age estimation as a tool to combat child labor. The system aims to improve monitoring and identification in affected sectors.

title: AMPLIFAI: A Multiphase CT Dataset for Benchmarking Clinical Reasoning in LI-RADS Assessment of Liver Lesions
summary: AMPLIFAI is a multiphase CT dataset developed for benchmarking AI models' clinical reasoning capabilities in LI-RADS assessment of liver lesions and hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis. It provides a foundation for automating HCC diagnosis.

title: MegaParts: Scaling Part-Aware 3D Object Generation to 300 Parts via Token-Efficient Autoregressive Modeling
summary: MegaParts introduces a method for scaling part-aware 3D object generation to highly complex objects with up to 300 parts using token-efficient autoregressive modeling. This advances generative AI capabilities for graphics applications.

title: Qwen-Video-Edit: Instruction-Based Video Editing by Repurposing an Image Editing Model
summary: Qwen-Video-Edit introduces a new approach to instruction-based video editing by repurposing an existing image editing model, offering a cost-effective alternative to video-pretrained generative backbones. It demonstrates a new capability for video manipulation.

title: Zero-Shot Adaptation of Medical Vision Foundation Models for High-Frequency Micro-Ultrasound Prostate Segmentation
summary: This research focuses on the zero-shot adaptation of medical vision foundation models for high-frequency micro-ultrasound prostate segmentation. This method aims to improve early detection of prostate cancer by precisely outlining the gland boundary.

title: OvDSGG: End-to-End Open-Vocabulary Dynamic Scene Graph Generation
summary: OvDSGG introduces an end-to-end open-vocabulary approach for dynamic scene graph generation, capturing spatio-temporal interactions in videos as triplets. This method underpins various downstream tasks like video captioning and action analysis.

title: Zero-MELO: Test-Time Evidence Calibration with Multimodal LLMs for Zero-Shot Micro-Gesture Recognition
summary: Zero-MELO proposes a Test-Time Evidence Calibration method using Multimodal LLMs for zero-shot micro-gesture recognition, addressing their limitations in fine-grained and motion-centric video understanding tasks. It enhances MLLM capabilities for subtle human interaction analysis.

title: Beam-Wise Statistical Background Subtraction for Static Roadside LiDAR: A Cross-Sensor Benchmark Study
summary: This study proposes beam-wise statistical background subtraction for static roadside LiDAR, and presents a cross-sensor benchmark study for efficiently isolating dynamic traffic participants. It addresses the lack of systematic evaluations for this type of LiDAR perception.

title: SpIn-ViT: Designing a Sparsity-Induced Vision Transformer That Is Mechanistically Interpretable
summary: SpIn-ViT is a newly designed sparsity-induced Vision Transformer explicitly built to be mechanistically interpretable. It aims to provide greater insight into the internal representations of AI models, addressing a core concern in AI ethics and safety.

title: PaSTel: Anchoring Histology in Spatial Transcriptomics via Multi-Scale Hierarchical Bio-Prior Contrastive Pretraining
summary: PaSTel introduces a novel multi-scale hierarchical bio-prior contrastive pretraining method to anchor histology images in spatial transcriptomics. This AI approach aims to align tissue morphology with molecular programs for biological discovery.

title: Benchmarking Frontier Text-to-Image Models on Image-Description Prompts
summary: This work benchmarks frontier text-to-image models using image-description prompts that require compositionally demanding requests. It aims to evaluate model performance on precise object counts, multi-object attribute binding, and explicit spatial constraints.

title: Risk-Adaptive Edge--Cloud Visual Reasoning for Communication-Efficient Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper presents a risk-adaptive edge-cloud architecture for visual reasoning in autonomous driving, optimizing communication efficiency by dynamically balancing cloud-hosted and onboard AI models. It enhances contextual reasoning for tactical decisions in self-driving vehicles.

title: FZ-VLM: A Two Stage Florence-Zephyr Vision Language Model Framework for Pulmonary Nodule Characterization and Clinical Decision Making
summary: This paper introduces FZ-VLM, a two-stage vision-language model framework designed for characterizing pulmonary nodules in CT scans and aiding clinical decision-making for lung cancer.

title: MetaReason: Precise Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning via Editing Meta Information for Solving Geometry Problems
summary: MetaReason proposes a method for precise interleaved multimodal reasoning by editing meta-information to enhance vision-language models' ability to solve complex geometry problems.

title: DualMiT-Net: Local-Global Transformer-Convolutional Fusion for Breast Mass Segmentation in Mammographic Regions of Interest
summary: DualMiT-Net is a dual-branch network combining transformer and convolutional fusion for improved breast mass segmentation in mammographic images, addressing challenges like low contrast and irregular shapes.

title: Generation of Synthetic Fingerphotos with GANs
summary: This paper explores the generation of synthetic fingerphotos using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) to address data limitations and privacy concerns in contactless fingerprint biometric authentication.

title: MOSS-VL Technical Report
summary: This technical report introduces MOSS-VL, an open vision-language model family designed for real-time interaction, allowing it to perceive information while speaking.

title: MEDR: Query-Independent Frame Selection via Multi-Signal Event Modeling and Dynamic Rescoring
summary: MEDR introduces a method for query-independent frame selection using multi-signal event modeling and dynamic rescoring to efficiently process long videos for multimodal large language models.

title: Do Visual Grounding Decoders Need Feed-Forward Networks? A Controlled Study over Frozen Vision-Language Features
summary: This research investigates whether feed-forward networks are essential in visual grounding decoders by conducting a controlled study on their contribution to processing frozen vision-language features.

title: SA-GEM: Scale-Adaptive and Geospatial Evidence-Modulated Token Pruning for Efficient Remote Sensing Large Vision-Language Models
summary: SA-GEM introduces a scale-adaptive and geospatial evidence-modulated token pruning method to enhance the efficiency of Large Vision-Language Models for remote sensing applications.

title: Distribution-free false-alarm calibration and chance-corrected spatial evaluation for industrial anomaly detection
summary: This paper proposes a method for distribution-free false-alarm calibration and chance-corrected spatial evaluation, aiming to improve the assessment of industrial anomaly detection systems.

title: MODAL: Multi-Modal Object Re-ID via Model-Driven Sparse Decoupling and Text-Image Differential Filtering
summary: MODAL presents a method for multi-modal object re-identification using model-driven sparse decoupling and text-image differential filtering to improve cross-camera object retrieval.

title: ProjFormer: Point Cloud Completion via Geometric-Projective Transformer and Cross-Modal Semantic Constraints
summary: ProjFormer proposes a new method for point cloud completion, utilizing a geometric-projective transformer and cross-modal semantic constraints to address challenges of sparsity and ambiguity.

title: Fast Test-Time Refinement for Robust Learned Image Compression
summary: This paper introduces a fast test-time refinement method aimed at enhancing the robustness of learned image compression models against adversarial vulnerabilities.

title: Perspective-Invariant Attack with Enhanced Transferability of Adversarial Examples
summary: This research proposes a perspective-invariant attack method designed to create adversarial examples with enhanced transferability, posing security threats to black-box deep neural networks.

title: HOIMask: Towards Generative Masked Modeling for Human Object Interaction Generation
summary: HOIMask proposes a generative masked modeling approach for human-object interaction generation, aiming to overcome limitations of diffusion-based methods in producing high-quality interactions.

title: From "What-If" to "What-Is": Counterfactual Thinking-Inspired Semantic Alignment for Visual Brain Decoding
summary: This paper introduces a counterfactual thinking-inspired semantic alignment method to improve visual brain decoding, reconstructing perceived visual content from neural measurements like fMRI.

title: Beyond Natural-Image Foundation Models: Benchmarking Satellite Pretraining for Ophthalmic Image Analysis
summary: This research benchmarks the effectiveness of satellite pretraining for Vision Foundation Models, evaluating its applicability and performance in ophthalmic image analysis.

title: SpotlessGS: Relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting under Dynamic Illumination for Robotic Perception
summary: SpotlessGS introduces a relightable 3D Gaussian Splatting method designed to improve robotic perception in environments with dynamic and uneven illumination.

title: MISTac: A Vision-Based Tactile Sensor for Minimally Invasive Surgery
summary: MISTac is a new high-resolution, vision-based tactile sensor developed to provide essential tactile feedback for surgeons during minimally invasive and robot-assisted surgical procedures.

title: Imagining Recovery: Inference-Time Counterfactual Realignment for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This research introduces an inference-time counterfactual realignment method designed to improve the robustness and recovery of Vision-Language-Action models used in robotic manipulation when facing online disruptions.

title: Modeling and Control of an Eel-Inspired Soft Robot for Design Optimization
summary: This paper presents a simulation model for an eel-inspired soft robot, focusing on its anguilliform locomotion and aiming to aid in the design optimization of such robots.

title: From Continuous Design to Delay-Aware Discrete Synthesis: Guaranteed High-Bandwidth Joint Control for PMSM Drives
summary: This paper proposes a new method for high-bandwidth joint control in PMSM drives, crucial for modern robotic joints, addressing challenges like communication and computation delays.

title: SkillComposer: Learning Reusable Skills for Natural-Language Robot Programming
summary: This research introduces SkillComposer, a system enabling natural-language programming of robots by allowing large language models to learn and reuse skills for complex, multi-step tasks.

title: Evidence of Absence: Cross-Modal Abductive Risk Perception to Sustain World Models When Vision Fails
summary: This paper addresses how AI systems can maintain a structured world-state and perceive risks even when primary visual perception is degraded or occluded, using cross-modal information.

title: GaussMemory: Task-Driven 3D Gaussian Scene Memory for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
summary: GaussMemory is introduced as a task-driven 3D Gaussian scene memory system designed to provide persistent spatial memory for long-horizon robotic manipulation tasks, improving upon passive recording methods.

title: HP2-SLAM: Adaptive Hybrid ICP for Robust and Efficient LiDAR SLAM
summary: This paper presents HP2-SLAM, an adaptive hybrid ICP method for robust and efficient LiDAR simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM), which is critical for autonomous navigation.

title: NPU Offloading of a Frozen Visual Encoder for Robot Policy Training
summary: This research proposes NPU offloading of frozen visual encoders to reduce training costs for robot policies by optimizing the forward pass computation during training.

title: ForceU-VLA: A Force-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Ultrasound Scanning
summary: ForceU-VLA is a new force-aware vision-language-action model designed for embodied ultrasound scanning, integrating multiple modalities to automate and standardize the examination process.

title: PACE: Phase-Progress-Aware Credit for Long-Horizon Embodied Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces PACE, a phase-progress-aware credit assignment method for post-training vision-language-action (VLA) models, improving learning for long-horizon embodied manipulation tasks.

title: Max-Q Selective Imitation for Human-in-the-Loop Online Robot Learning
summary: This research presents Max-Q Selective Imitation, a new training method for human-in-the-loop online robot learning that enables real robots to quickly absorb human interventions and improve efficiently.

title: StructRL: Structured Action-Space Exploration for Flow-Based VLAs
summary: StructRL is proposed as a method for structured action-space exploration in online reinforcement learning for flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models, used in continuous robotic manipulation.

title: LAPF: LLM-Agent-Based Path Finder Using the UAVScenes Dataset
summary: This paper introduces LAPF, an LLM-agent-based pathfinder using the UAVScenes Dataset for uncrewed aerial vehicles to achieve intelligent adaptive decision-making for autonomous navigation in complex environments.

title: Remember Smarter: Visual History Compressor and Hyperbolic Experience Space for Robotic Memory
summary: Remember Smarter (RS) is introduced as a plug-and-play module that provides compact and reusable robotic memory through a visual history compressor and a hyperbolic experience space.

title: PhaseLoRA: Control-Regime-Conditioned Low-Rank Adaptation for Continuous-Action Vision-Language-Action Policies
summary: PhaseLoRA is a new parameter-efficient fine-tuning method for Vision-Language-Action policies, adapting them to continuous-action manipulation tasks by considering the phase-dependent nature of control rollouts.

title: MM-BEV: Enhancing Timeliness by Computing Where and When it Matters
summary: MM-BEV aims to enhance the timeliness of multimodal bird's-eye-view perception, a crucial component for real-time deployment in autonomous systems, by optimizing computational efficiency.

title: Accelerating Mixed Discrete-Continuous Motion Planning via Neural Graphs of Convex Sets
summary: This paper proposes accelerating mixed discrete-continuous motion planning through Neural Graphs of Convex Sets, offering a solution for complex problems like collision-free navigation and contact-rich manipulation.

title: GUIDER: Evaluating Goal-Free Human Intent Inference for Teleoperated Manipulation on Real-Robot Data
summary: This paper evaluates GUIDER, a goal-free probabilistic framework for human intent inference during teleoperated manipulation, tested on real-robot data from a robotic arm.

title: Detachable Wire Drive : Reconfigurable Robot Architecture with Shared Actuators
summary: This research presents a detachable wire drive, a reconfigurable robot architecture with shared actuators, aiming to reduce system weight, volume, and cost for diverse robotic tasks.

title: Vision-Based Tactile Intelligence for Robotics: Sensing, Learning, and Embodied Manipulation
summary: This paper explores vision-based tactile intelligence for robotics, focusing on sensing, learning, and embodied manipulation to improve robots' ability to handle contact-rich tasks.

title: Temporal Logic Guided Universal Task Representations for Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research investigates Temporal Logic Guided Universal Task Representations for Reinforcement Learning, aiming to improve the generalization capabilities of task-guided agents across diverse scenarios.

title: Degenerate in Whose Frame? An Equivariance Condition for Degeneracy Detection in LiDAR Registration
summary: This paper addresses degeneracy detection in LiDAR registration by analyzing an equivariance condition under body-frame changes, a technical challenge for robust LiDAR performance in autonomous systems.

title: MistyPilot: Enabling Social-Robot Control through Multi-Agent LLM Skill Orchestration
summary: This paper proposes MistyPilot, a multi-agent LLM skill orchestration framework to enable social-robot control through natural language instructions, by composing APIs into reactive physical and stateful social behaviors.

title: Not All History Helps: Velocity-Aware Selective Memory for Long-Horizon End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: This research introduces a velocity-aware selective memory mechanism for long-horizon end-to-end autonomous driving, aiming to improve planning reliability by selectively using historical planning information.

title: Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Efficient VLA Inference via Speculative Inference and Verification
summary: This paper proposes an algorithm-architecture co-design approach for efficient Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model inference in embodied AI, utilizing speculative inference and a dedicated accelerator to address high computational costs and enable real-time deployment.

title: Robo-Dopamine 2.0: History-Conditioned and OOD-Aware Process Reward Modeling for Robotic Manipulation
summary: This research introduces Robo-Dopamine 2.0, a history-conditioned and out-of-distribution aware process reward modeling technique to refine Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies for robust robotic manipulation through reinforcement learning.

title: GAINS: Leveraging Inconsistent Human Intervention Signals in Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper presents GAINS, a method for leveraging inconsistent human intervention signals in reinforcement learning to correct and improve robot manipulation policies for real-world deployment.

title: Making two action heads agree: coordination mechanisms and a runtime collapse certificate for flow-matching policies
summary: This research explores coordination mechanisms and a runtime collapse certificate for dual-representation flow-matching policies in robotic control, aiming to resolve inconsistencies between independently sampled action branches on multimodal tasks.

title: Tac4Loco: Learning Spatiotemporal Plantar Pressure Representations for Humanoid Locomotion
summary: This paper introduces Tac4Loco, a method for learning spatiotemporal plantar pressure representations to enable humanoid robots to achieve robust locomotion and adapt to uneven terrains and uncertain foot-ground interactions.

title: Reliable Piezoresistive Strain Sensing Through Physical Limits and Uncertainty Monitoring
summary: This research investigates methods for achieving reliable piezoresistive strain sensing, addressing the nonlinearity and hysteresis of soft sensors for wearable and soft robotic applications through physical limits and uncertainty monitoring.

title: ViTaR: Visuo-Tactile Residual Adaptation for Foundation VLA Manipulation
summary: This paper presents ViTaR, a visuo-tactile residual adaptation method to enhance Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robust contact-rich manipulation in real-world robotic deployments.

title: Scaling Manual-Grounded Appliance Manipulation with Data Synthesis and Unified Planning
summary: This research proposes MAGE, a scalable data synthesis and unified planning approach to enable long-horizon manual-grounded appliance manipulation by robots, addressing the lack of diverse, task-oriented datasets.

title: GigaBrain-0.7: Scaling Embodied Foundation Models to Emergent Capabilities with a Three-System Architecture
summary: This paper introduces GigaBrain-0.7, a three-system architectural design for scaling embodied foundation models (VLA models) to achieve emergent capabilities in generalist embodied agents.

title: Grouping Auction-Consensus Algorithm for Decentralized Task Allocation in Multi-Robot Systems
summary: This research proposes a Grouping Auction-Consensus Algorithm for decentralized task allocation in multi-robot systems, aiming to improve upon existing methods like the Consensus-Based Bundle Algorithm for scalable and resilient autonomous operations.

title: Tactile Sim2Real without Tactile Simulation via Bottlenecked Latent Reconstruction
summary: This paper introduces a Sim2Real method for tactile robot sensors that bypasses explicit tactile simulation, using bottlenecked latent reconstruction to enable more efficient transfer to physical robots.

title: Pre-training Visual Dexterity in Simulation
summary: This research investigates large-scale pre-training of visual dexterity in simulation to improve data efficiency for fine-tuning robot policies, particularly for dexterous, multi-fingered hands.

title: RAPAC-DP: Response-Aligned Pending-Action Compensation for Diffusion Policies under Delayed Execution
summary: This paper proposes RAPAC-DP, a response-aligned pending-action compensation framework designed to improve the control performance of diffusion policies under delayed execution, especially for cloud-side inference in robotics.

title: Revisiting Open-Loop Execution in Robotics: Toward Reactive, Higher-Performing Policies
summary: This research re-examines open-loop execution in robotics, proposing methods to improve reactivity and performance of imitation learning policies for robotic manipulation by addressing limitations of long open-loop prefixes.

title: Tabletop Pen Manipulation With a Vision-Guided 4-DoF Arm
summary: This paper demonstrates tabletop pen manipulation using a vision-guided four-degree-of-freedom (DoF) robotic arm, showcasing its capability for tasks typically requiring more complex systems.

title: Learning Varying Physical Therapist-Patient Interactions for Robot-mediated Upper Limb Task-Specific Training
summary: This research explores learning varying physical therapist-patient interactions to optimize robot-mediated upper limb Task-Specific Training, aiming to increase therapy dosage for motor function recovery.

title: Benchmarking Identity-Sensitive LLM Outputs for Surveillance and Security Robots
summary: This paper focuses on benchmarking identity-sensitive outputs from large language models when used to generate design specifications and interaction policies for surveillance and security robots.

title: ScenarioCharacterization: A Modular Toolkit for Characterizing Safety across Trajectory Datasets
summary: This paper introduces ScenarioCharacterization, a modular open-source toolkit for automated and dataset-agnostic profiling of driving scenarios to characterize safety across trajectory datasets for autonomous vehicles.

title: US-VLA: An Ultrasound Vision-Language-Action Model for Embodied Abdomina
summary: A new "Ultrasound Vision-Language-Action Model" (US-VLA) is developed to assist ultrasound scanning by providing real-time guidance and reducing operator dependence.

title: Unified Condition-Action Modeling for Accurate One-Step Action Generation
summary: A new "Unified Condition-Action Modeling" approach is proposed for accurate and efficient one-step action generation in robot manipulation, focusing on jointly evolving conditions.

title: SparkVLA: Stop-Aware Hierarchical VLA with Adaptive Action Chunking for Long-Horizon Manipulation
summary: "SparkVLA" is introduced as a stop-aware hierarchical Vision-Language-Action (VLA) system with adaptive action chunking for long-horizon manipulation tasks.

title: RoboStriker: Latent-Space Strategic Games for Autonomous Humanoid Boxing
summary: "RoboStriker" is presented as a system using latent-space strategic games and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning to enable autonomous humanoid robots to engage in boxing.

title: Deep Probabilistic Indoor Gas Source Localization via Physical Dependency-Guided Sequential Inference
summary: A deep probabilistic method is proposed for indoor gas source localization (GSL) using physical dependency-guided sequential inference to improve safety in complex environments.
