summary: This study proposes SAGE-XGBoost, a machine learning framework utilizing Spatially Augmented Graph Embeddings, for natural hazards susceptibility mapping under data scarcity. It aims to improve the generalizability of predictions despite limited labeled data.

title: A Locally Tokenized Generative Model for Robust Time-Series Watermarking
summary: This paper proposes a locally tokenized generative model for robust time-series watermarking, addressing reliability failures under post-editing attacks. It aims to improve provenance for generative models by overcoming issues with existing detectors that rely on globally coupled re-encoding.

title: RecPFN: Prior-Fitted Networks for In-Context-Based Recommendations
summary: This paper introduces RecPFN (Prior-Fitted Network), a novel architecture that applies in-context learning to sequential recommendation systems. RecPFN is pretrained on synthetic clickstream environments to enable efficient Bayesian-style inference from limited support data.

title: Truncate Bad, Upweight Good: BoN-Style Distillation via Rank-Based Classification
summary: This research introduces BoN-Style Distillation, a method using rank-based classification to improve the quality of AI model generations by distilling inference-time selection into a single policy.

title: Credit Without Ground Truth: Auditing Step-Level Credit Assignment in LLM Agents Against Executed Replay
summary: This paper audits step-level credit assignment signals used in LLM agents against executed replays in a tool environment, finding current methods do not reliably identify causally important steps.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Using Flow Matching on Tabular Data
summary: This study proposes an unsupervised anomaly detection method for tabular data using flow matching, addressing challenges like training-set contamination in financial logs.

title: MileGPO: Milestone Inference with Local Evidence for Graph-Based Policy Optimization of Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: This paper presents MileGPO, a method for graph-based policy optimization that uses milestone inference with local evidence to address credit assignment challenges in long-horizon LLM agents.

title: Answer-Level Trust Selection for Physical Vision-Language Reasoning
summary: This research investigates answer-level trust selection for physical reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs), aiming to assess the reliability of individual predictions beyond overall model performance.

title: FAR-DPO: Feasibility-Aware and Robust Direct Preference Optimization for Cyclic Peptide Design
summary: This paper introduces FAR-DPO, a feasibility-aware and robust Direct Preference Optimization method for designing cyclic peptides, a challenging area in generative models for drug discovery.

title: Adaptive Probabilistic Shielding by Learning MDPs for Safe Reinforcement Learning
summary: This work proposes an adaptive probabilistic shielding technique for safe reinforcement learning, where an observer learns MDPs to constrain a learning agent's actions.

title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
summary: This study reveals that language models can inadvertently leak sensitive user context, such as calendars and credentials, through hidden correlations in their benign outputs.

title: Online Test-Time Adaptation for Generalizable Dynamic Graph Anomaly Detection
summary: This research focuses on online test-time adaptation for generalizable dynamic graph anomaly detection, aiming to improve performance in unseen target domains.

title: Reliable Neural Collapse Approximation for Open-World Test-Time Adaptation
summary: This paper introduces a new method for reliable neural collapse approximation to improve Test-Time Adaptation in open-world scenarios with label distribution shifts.

title: PETA:Parameter-Efficient Test-Time Adaptation for Virtual Screening
summary: This paper presents PETA, a parameter-efficient Test-Time Adaptation method applied to virtual screening in drug discovery, leveraging DrugCLIP for improved ranking of ligands.

title: Multi-Source Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Graph Learning
summary: This work explores Multi-Source Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Graph Learning for network topology inference, addressing challenges in fusing heterogeneous source-domain data.

title: G-MARK: Grounded Multi-Agent Reasoning for Cooperative Driving via Knowledge Graphs
summary: This research introduces G-MARK, a method for grounded multi-agent reasoning using knowledge graphs to enhance cooperative driving in autonomous systems under partial observability.

title: Green BOA: Determining the environmental break-even point for ML-based data compression
summary: This summary details research determining the environmental break-even point for ML-based data compression, assessing the sustainability impact of such algorithms.

title: Scale-Aware Pretraining of Time Series Foundation Models via Multi-Patch Token Alignment and Hybrid Masking
summary: This paper proposes a scale-aware pretraining method for time series foundation models, using multi-patch token alignment and hybrid masking to handle varying sampling frequencies across datasets.

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS for Zero-Shot Probabilistic Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
summary: This study provides a systematic evaluation of TabPFN-TS for zero-shot probabilistic heat load forecasting in district heating networks, assessing its performance for efficient operational scheduling.

title: CLaST: Context-aware Contrastive VAE for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces CLaST, a context-aware contrastive VAE, designed as a deep generative model for robust probabilistic time series forecasting in various domains.

title: An Inclusive and Lightweight Approach to Federated Continual Learning for Cultural Heritage
summary: This work proposes an inclusive and lightweight approach to federated continual learning for cultural heritage, enabling large-scale retrieval and analysis of distributed, evolving collections.

title: End-to-end Early Classification of Time Series in Non-Stationary Environments
summary: This research addresses end-to-end early classification of time series in non-stationary environments, focusing on making accurate and timely decisions in evolving online settings.

title: DecoVAE: a Lightweight Interpretable Trend-Seasonal VAE Framework for Efficient Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces DecoVAE, a lightweight and interpretable VAE framework that decomposes time series into trend and seasonal components for efficient probabilistic forecasting.

title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts
summary: This paper proposes a compute-efficient hyperparameter transfer method for optimizing learning rates in large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, addressing the computational challenges of scaling these models.

title: SAE-Xplainers: Rule-Based Feature Interpretation for Extreme Earth Events
summary: This research introduces "SAE-Xplainers," a rule-based feature interpretation method to improve the interpretability of deep learning models used for predicting extreme Earth events, which is crucial for operational adoption.

title: A Standardized Framework for Machine Learning in Power System Protection
summary: This paper proposes a standardized framework for evaluating machine learning models used in power system protection, addressing the variability in evaluation settings that currently undermines the meaning of reported performance scores.

title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models
summary: This theoretical paper focuses on the exact algebraic computation of learning coefficients for two-dimensional singular models, which helps address the limitations of classical information criteria like BIC in deep learning contexts.

title: Decoding silent reading from non-invasive EEG
summary: This research investigates the non-invasive decoding of silent reading from EEG signals, addressing the fundamental data challenges associated with collecting brain activity data corresponding to spontaneous inner monologue.

title: A Virtual Member of a Community of Practice for the Society of Petroleum Engineers: From Prototype to Deployment
summary: This paper details the development and deployment of "ATHENA," a virtual assistant designed to facilitate knowledge capture, retrieval, and dissemination for members of the Society of Petroleum Engineers in the Oil and Gas sector.

title: Transformer Models for Text Summarization: A Comparative Study of BART, BERT, and RoBERTa
summary: This research presents a comparative study of transformer models, specifically BART, BERT, and RoBERTa, for automatic text summarization, evaluating their effectiveness in condensing documents while preserving key information.

title: Automatic bioinformatic software named entity recognition from literature
summary: This research focuses on developing an automatic named entity recognition (NER) system to systematically identify and extract mentions of bioinformatics software and databases from scientific literature, addressing the current challenges in cataloging these resources.

title: Asymmetric Attention Heads: Structured Head-Wise Context Allocation for Transformer Attention
summary: This paper proposes a new method called "Asymmetric Attention Heads" for transformer attention, which enables structured, head-wise context allocation to improve how different attention heads process varying contextual information.

title: Hallucination as a Feature, not a Defect: Evaluating a multi-agent architecture to transform speculative language-model outputs into testable scientific hypotheses
summary: This research evaluates a multi-agent architecture designed to transform speculative language model "hallucinations" into testable scientific hypotheses, exploring how to leverage combinatorial creativity rather than solely suppressing it for factual retrieval.

title: Compliance, Capability, and Conflict: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs under System Messages
summary: This paper addresses the lack of evaluation for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) adherence to system messages by proposing a new benchmarking approach to assess their compliance and capabilities in multimodal contexts.

title: When Irrelevant Text Matters: Affine Margin Shifts in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper investigates the impact of task-irrelevant auxiliary textual context on Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) during visually grounded tasks, exploring how such context influences model behavior through "affine margin shifts."

title: Represented but Ignored: A Causal Account of Prosodic Underuse in Audio-Language Models
summary: This research provides a causal analysis of "prosodic underuse" in audio-language models, explaining why these models often fail to fully leverage the linguistic and emotional information conveyed by speech prosody.

title: NepOOC-M: Bilingual Nepali-English Benchmark and Comparative Analysis of Multimodal Architectures for OOC Detection
summary: This paper introduces NepOOC-M, a new bilingual Nepali-English benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal architectures for detecting out-of-context misinformation, where authentic images are paired with misleading captions.

title: Time-Series Retrieval for Grounding Multimodal Language Models in Remaining Useful Life
summary: This research explores the use of time-series retrieval methods to ground Multimodal Language Models (MLLMs) for domain-specific maintenance and prognostics tasks, particularly focusing on predicting remaining useful life (RUL).

title: Can Conversational AI loosen Us-Versus-Them Boundaries? The Effects of Common, Dual, and Separate Identity Framings on Pro-Immigrant Intergroup Helping
summary: This preregistered experiment investigates whether conversational AI can reduce intergroup tensions and promote pro-immigrant helping behavior by studying the effects of common, dual, and separate identity framings on majority-group members.

title: A Speech Corpus for Mizo Automatic Speech Recognition: Whisper and SraVaani 1.0 Fine-Tuning with Morphology-Aware Evaluation
summary: This study reports on the development of an Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) system for Mizo, a low-resource language, through the creation of a dedicated speech corpus and fine-tuning of Whisper and SraVaani 1.0 multilingual models.

title: Linguistic Holonomy and Statistical Watermarks: Inner Geometry of Meaning-Preserving Transformations
summary: This paper explores the theoretical properties of statistical watermarks for language models, focusing on how meaning-preserving transformations can erode them by altering text form while maintaining content.

title: Are LLMs becoming similarly creative? Evidence from three years of models
summary: This research investigates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) are becoming similarly creative over time by examining their performance on open-ended tasks, where creativity, originality, and diversity are crucial, contrasting with tasks with verifiable answers.

title: Hear2Act: Benchmarking When Prosody Should Change What an Assistant Does
summary: This paper introduces a new benchmarking approach to evaluate how AI assistants should interpret and respond to prosodic cues in task-oriented dialogue, considering perception, response appropriateness, and task outcomes.

title: Automated Summarization of Financial News Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation: An Early Empirical Study (Fall 2023)
summary: This empirical study explores the use of Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for automated summarization of financial news to aid stock market analysts and investors.

title: When Machines Speak: A Unified Generative Framework for Integrating Machine-Native Symbols into Pretrained Large Language Models
summary: This research proposes a unified generative framework for integrating machine-native symbols into pretrained Large Language Models, enabling them to process structured information beyond natural language tokens.

title: Generating Diverse Personas for User Simulators to Test Interview Dialogue Systems
summary: This paper introduces a method for generating diverse user personas for simulators to efficiently test interview dialogue systems, reducing the labor and cost associated with human-based evaluation.

title: Reliable Financial Named Entity Recognition under Domain Shift
summary: This study investigates reliable financial Named Entity Recognition under domain shift, focusing on confidence estimation methods to ensure safe automation when AI systems encounter varying input distributions.

title: Remember, Verify, or Ask? Cross-Family Evaluation of Memory Commitment in LLM Agents
summary: This research evaluates memory commitment in LLM agents, exploring how interaction-derived information should be handled – whether persisted, used contextually, re-verified, or clarified with the user, to avoid distorting future behavior.

title: Forking Fast: Efficiently Estimating Uncertainty Dynamics in Text Generation
summary: This paper presents a method for efficiently estimating uncertainty dynamics in LLM text generation by analyzing the distribution of reasoning chains using resampling-based analyses.

title: Mitigating Identity Essentialism in LLM Agents with Longitudinal Life Trajectories
summary: This research proposes using longitudinal life trajectories to mitigate identity essentialism in LLM agents, enhancing their ability to capture human-like diversity in social simulations.

title: ReCache: Efficient KV Cache Reuse and Compression for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces ReCache, a framework designed for efficient key-value (KV) cache reuse and compression in tool-augmented LLM agents, optimizing the handling of recurring tool and skill schemas.

title: The Asymmetric Harms of LLM Compression
summary: This work systematically evaluates the asymmetric harms of Large Language Model (LLM) compression, revealing behavioral shifts often masked by standard aggregate metrics like perplexity and accuracy.

title: Projector Is All You Train
summary: This research investigates whether fine-tuning the language model backbone of a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) is necessary when adapting it to new modalities, suggesting that focusing on the projector might suffice.

title: One Success Isn't Reliability: Thinkingbox, a Sandbox and Benchmark for Agents in Stateful Business Workflows
summary: This paper introduces Thinkingbox, a sandbox and benchmark designed to evaluate the reliability and performance of AI agents in complex stateful business workflows beyond simple task completion.

title: PersonalBench: Measuring the Authorship Gap in LLM Personalization
summary: This paper introduces PersonalBench, a new benchmark designed to measure the authorship gap in LLM personalization by evaluating how closely a model's output matches a target author's writing style.

title: FlashPrefill V2: Block-Sparse Prefill Attention for Long-Context LLM Serving
summary: This paper introduces FlashPrefill V2, a block-sparse prefill attention mechanism designed to optimize long-context serving for Large Language Models by mitigating the quadratic complexity bottleneck during the prefilling phase.

title: SWE-bench Science: Can Coding Agents Resolve Engineering Tasks in Science?
summary: This research introduces SWE-bench Science, an evaluation framework designed to assess the capability of coding agents in resolving engineering tasks specifically within scientific contexts.

title: LoRA-GA$^2$: Low Rank Adaptation with Multi-step Gradient Adaptive Alignment
summary: This paper introduces LoRA-GA$^2$, an enhanced Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning method that utilizes multi-step gradient adaptive alignment to further reduce the performance gap between LoRA and full fine-tuning for large models.

title: Stopping and Routing LLM Judge Panels
summary: This research focuses on optimizing LLM evaluation pipelines by developing strategies for stopping and routing LLM judge panels, determining which judges to use for specific examples and tasks.

title: A knowledge-guided agentic framework for mitigating patient-context ambiguity in health queries
summary: This paper introduces a knowledge-guided agentic framework designed to mitigate patient-context ambiguity in health queries, enabling healthcare chatbots to provide more appropriate responses to underspecified patient requests.

title: Interrupting the Loop: Periodic Subject Changes Raise Judged Surprise and Connection in Base Language Models
summary: This research explores how periodic subject changes influence novelty, surprise, and connection in base language models by analyzing a cognitively inspired generation loop.

title: Learning how to Forget: Fine-tuning for Long-Context Sparse Attention
summary: This paper introduces a new fine-tuning method for transformer language models that enables long-context sparse attention, optimizing key-value (KV) cache selection and compression for more efficient inference.

title: Dynamic Gated Cross-Modal Fusion with Sarcastic-aware Contrastive Regularization for Multimodal Sarcasm Detection
summary: This research proposes a dynamic gated cross-modal fusion method with sarcastic-aware contrastive regularization to improve multimodal sarcasm detection, addressing challenges with instance-dependent inconsistencies. The method aims to better identify ironic intent from multimodal content.

title: Natural Language Code Retrieval for 1C:Enterprise: An Open Benchmark and Efficient Bi-Encoder
summary: This paper introduces an open benchmark and an efficient bi-encoder for natural language code retrieval within the 1C:Enterprise ecosystem, which previously lacked open datasets and specialized models. It aims to address the challenges of Russian syntax and domain-specific terminology in this task.

title: Robust Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis via Iterative Proxy Correction
summary: This research proposes an iterative proxy correction method for robust incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis, aiming to mitigate the issues caused by missing or corrupted multimodal inputs. The approach addresses the weakening of cross-modal complementarity and misleading information in such scenarios.

title: HealMed: Multilingual Evaluation of Large Language Models in Medicine
summary: HealMed is presented as an expert-reviewed benchmark for the multilingual evaluation of large language models in medicine, featuring 1,000 examples across nine languages and three task formats. It was developed over two years to assess LLM performance in a medical context.

title: Auditing Cross-Lingual Fairness in Language Model Watermarking
summary: This research audits cross-lingual fairness in language model watermarking, highlighting how current evaluation methods, primarily focused on English text, fail to adequately assess performance in multilingual deployments. It discusses the impact of evaluation-design choices on determining conclusive results for such schemes.

title: SABET-QA: Temporal Knowledge Graph Question Answering
summary: SABET-QA is introduced as a framework for Question Answering over Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKGQA) that iteratively refines reasoning states across multiple hops. It aims to address the limitations of existing embedding-based methods that struggle with multi-step queries.

title: OenoBench: A Wine-Domain Benchmark for Knowledge-Grounded Evaluation of Large Language Models
summary: OenoBench is introduced as a wine-domain knowledge benchmark of 3,266 multiple-choice questions across six pillars and four difficulty tiers for evaluating Large Language Models. The corpus is built from 38,104 atomic, source-anchored facts.

title: When Text and Numbers Disagree: Evidence Arbitration in Large Language Models
summary: This research investigates how Large Language Models arbitrate between conflicting evidence from textual summaries, numerical observations, and external tool outputs when making decisions. A controlled synthesis setup is introduced to study this evidence arbitration process.

title: FormalTCS: Benchmarking End-to-End Frontier Formal Theoretical Computer Science Research of Large Language Models
summary: FormalTCS is presented as an expert-validated benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models on frontier, end-to-end Theoretical Computer Science research, addressing the gap between existing benchmarks and realistic research settings. It aims to assess LLMs' potential in automated TCS research.

title: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection
summary: Task-CoEvolve proposes a novel approach for efficient Large Language Model (LLM) agent harness optimization through adaptive validation task selection. This method iteratively rewrites harness code based on validation performance to achieve substantial performance gains.

title: Inject, Align, Recover: Staged Post-Training for Retrieval-Free Document Knowledge Internalization
summary: This research introduces "Inject, Align, Recover," a staged post-training method for retrieval-free document knowledge internalization in Large Language Models. It aims to convert a fixed corpus into usable parametric knowledge, allowing LLMs to answer questions about it without explicit retrieval at inference time.

title: G-CARL: Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning for Patient-Oriented Medical Report Interpretation
summary: G-CARL proposes a Grounded Checklist-Aligned Reward Learning approach for patient-oriented medical report interpretation, addressing the need for both evidence-grounded medical factuality and context-dependent patient communication. It aims to improve personalized interpretation of medical reports.

title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
summary: ConceptGuard introduces a benchmark for evaluating context-sensitive unlearning in Large Language Models, which assesses their ability to selectively remove harmful or sensitive knowledge. It addresses limitations of existing methods that rely on disjoint forget and retain sets.

title: HARP: Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking with Preference-Adaptive Fusion for Query-Based CVE Prioritization
summary: HARP proposes a Hierarchical Adaptive Ranking with Preference-Adaptive Fusion method for query-based CVE prioritization, addressing the challenge that vulnerability prioritization is inherently preference-dependent. It aims to provide flexible ranking unlike existing fixed-criterion methods.

title: Measuring What a Specification Determines: A Formal Semantic-Block Model and an Execution-Judged Benchmark
summary: This work introduces a formal semantic-block model for specifications and an execution-judged benchmark to evaluate specification quality independently of model capability. It represents a specification as a structure of semantic blocks, dependency relations, and rules.

title: Does Listening Matter? Backchanneling and Nodding in AI Clone
summary: This research investigates whether integrating multimodal listening behaviors, such as verbal backchannels and head nodding, can enhance the presence and authenticity of AI clones. It explores how these behaviors, typically absent, could improve human-like interaction.

title: PEA-DPO: Perception-Enhanced Alignment Direct Preference Optimization for MLLMs Alignment
summary: PEA-DPO introduces a Perception-Enhanced Alignment Direct Preference Optimization method for aligning Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with human preferences. It aims to address a key limitation in multimodal preference optimization identified through representational analysis.

title: StreamSoccer: Event-Driven Memory for Streaming Soccer Commentary
summary: StreamSoccer proposes an event-driven memory system for streaming soccer commentary, designed to causally update its state as video arrives and organize growing history into semantic units. It allows for recalling information under bounded computation and memory constraints.

title: TempJail: Temporal Jailbreak Attack against Large Vision-Language Models via Subtitle Scheduling
summary: TempJail introduces a novel temporal jailbreak attack against Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) that leverages subtitle scheduling. This research explores video-based jailbreaks, a relatively unexplored area compared to text and image-based attacks.

title: Clustering and Token Denoising for Faster and More Robust VLMs
summary: This research proposes clustering and token denoising techniques to make Visual-Language Models (VLMs) faster and more robust, particularly addressing the computational burden of processing visual tokens. The goal is to facilitate edge deployment of models like LLaVA.

title: SceneGTMM: A Conformal Mapping-based Scene-Aware Transferable GNN-Transformer Dual-Graph Interaction Framework for Map Matching
summary: This paper introduces SceneGTMM, a GNN-Transformer framework for map matching that addresses challenges in noise robustness, cross-regional transfer, and interpretability using a conformal mapping-based approach.

title: Does Marginal Coverage Guarantee Class-Conditional Safety for Zero-Shot VLMs Under Shift?
summary: This research audits whether marginal coverage guarantees class-conditional safety for zero-shot Vision-Language Models (VLMs) under deployment shift, evaluating techniques like split-conformal prediction for models like CLIP.

title: CAViAR: A Causal Video Dataset for Fine-Grained Accident Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios
summary: This paper introduces CAViAR, a new causal video dataset designed to facilitate fine-grained accident reasoning in real-world scenarios, aiming to improve autonomous driving systems' ability to interpret traffic accidents.

title: Beyond Recognition: Compact Multi-Domain Arabic Manuscript HTR with Candidate-Selection Analysis and Evidence-Preserving Review
summary: This research presents Phoenix, a compact multi-domain system for historical Arabic manuscript transcription that goes beyond simple recognition to preserve uncertain readings and distinguish visual evidence from linguistic plausibility.

title: HiRA-CAM: Preserving Fine-Grained Spatial Relevance in Gradient-Based Visual Explanations
summary: This paper introduces HiRA-CAM, a method designed to improve the interpretability of deep learning models, specifically convolutional neural networks, by preserving fine-grained spatial relevance in gradient-based visual explanations.

title: VideoRun2D Demo: Markerless Body Tracking for Biomechanical Analysis of Running
summary: This demo showcases VideoRun2D, a markerless body tracking system for biomechanical analysis of running, utilizing advancements in deep learning for human pose estimation with applications in sports analysis.

title: A Plug-in Interpretation of Conditioning in Score-Based Diffusion Models
summary: This research proposes a novel plug-in conditioning mechanism for score-based diffusion models, using multi-speed joint diffusion to enforce conditioning at inference time via a correction term.

title: CVSD-Reg: Cross-Modal Visual Semantic Prior Distillation for Robust LiDAR Registration
summary: This paper proposes CVSD-Reg, a new method for robust global LiDAR registration that uses cross-modal visual semantic prior distillation to overcome the sensitivity of existing learning-based methods to variations in point cloud characteristics.

title: Where Grounding Accuracy Lives on the IoU Curve: Label-Free Inference-Time Boundary Refinement
summary: This research investigates label-free inference-time boundary refinement for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), exploring how a frozen model can use its own predictions to improve the precision of bounding boxes without needing target annotations.

title: Stream4D: 4D-Consistency for Streaming Autoregressive Diffusion Video Models
summary: This paper introduces Stream4D, a method to improve 4D-consistency in streaming autoregressive diffusion video models, addressing issues like geometric drift and unnatural motion in long-horizon video generation.

title: Block3D: Efficient Text-to-3D Generation via Block-Wise Diffusion
summary: This paper introduces Block3D, a method for efficient text-to-3D generation that uses block-wise diffusion to achieve high geometric fidelity at a lower inference cost.

title: VGI-BENCH: Probing Visual Intelligence in Video Generation Models
summary: This paper introduces VGI-BENCH, a new benchmark designed to reliably evaluate the visual intelligence and zero-shot visual reasoning capabilities of video generation models.

title: TextRefine: Improving Textual Fidelity, Spatial Placement, and Glyph Rendering for Text Editing in Product Posters
summary: This paper proposes TextRefine, a method aimed at improving text editing in product posters by enhancing textual fidelity, spatial placement, and glyph rendering, addressing limitations of general-purpose image editing models.

title: When Guidance Goes Off-Scale: Recalibrating Diffusion Transformers under Analog Compute-in-Memory Nonidealities
summary: This research investigates recalibrating Diffusion Transformers to function effectively with analog compute-in-memory (CIM), aiming to reduce memory traffic and energy costs by addressing non-idealities inherent in CIM hardware.

title: PL-NBA: A Possession-level Universal Basketball Video Dataset Supporting Multiple Visual Understanding Tasks
summary: This paper introduces PL-NBA, a new possession-level universal basketball video dataset designed to support multiple visual understanding tasks and address limitations of existing datasets in preserving temporal continuity of game events.

title: MUST-PET: MUltimodal Self-supervised learning across Tracers for whole-body PET/CT-based lesion segmentation
summary: This research introduces MUST-PET, a multimodal self-supervised learning method across tracers for whole-body PET/CT-based lesion segmentation, addressing generalization limitations due to scarce annotations in cancer applications.

title: Scaffolding Minds: Optimizing Latent Visual Target Representations for Multimodal Reasoning
summary: This research proposes a two-stage training paradigm for optimizing latent visual target representations to enhance multimodal reasoning, involving encoding helper images into latent tokens and refining them with reward feedback.

title: RIPE++: Reinforced Keypoint Learning from Positive Pairs Only
summary: This paper introduces RIPE++, a method for reinforced keypoint learning that utilizes only positive pairs, addressing challenges in sparse keypoint extraction and matching for geometric computer vision tasks.

title: Robust Cross-Modal Foundation Model Perception for Underwater Robots under Degraded Visual Conditions
summary: This research explores robust cross-modal foundation model perception for underwater robots, aiming to improve their ability to operate in degraded visual conditions by integrating information from various sensors like sonar.

title: Scale-Separated Conditioning for Style-Encoder-Free Diffusion Stylization
summary: This paper proposes Scale-Separated Conditioning, a method for style-encoder-free diffusion stylization that aims to separate target geometry from transferable appearance in reference-based stylization.

title: Learning to Beat: Phenotype-Guided Latent Flow with Regional Motion Priors for Biventricular Motion Synthesis
summary: Focuses on synthesizing full-cycle 3D+t biventricular motion from end-diastolic anatomy using a phenotype-guided latent flow for cardiac function analysis.

title: Question-Guided Evidence Acquisition for Multimodal Visual Question Answering
summary: Develops a question-guided evidence acquisition method to improve multimodal LLMs' reliability in reading documents for Visual Question Answering.

title: Gallileo-4D: Frozen Backbone Ensemble for Dynamic 4D Reconstruction
summary: Describes an entry to the PhysAI Dynamic 4D Reconstruction Challenge, which placed third on the leaderboard using a frozen backbone ensemble.

title: Towards Clinically Faithful Medical Image Captioning via Enhanced Vision-Language Alignment
summary: Explores enhanced vision-language alignment for medical image captioning to achieve clinically faithful descriptions and improve diagnostic workflows.

title: A 360-Degree Vision Dataset for Learning Yaw Control on GPS-Denied Micro-UAVs in Disaster-Response-Relevant Environments
summary: Presents a data-driven approach using 360-degree vision for learning yaw control on micro-drones in GPS-denied indoor disaster-response environments.

title: DIFFCZSL: Compositional Zero-Shot Learning Regularized by Diffusion Representations
summary: Introduces DIFFCZSL, a method for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning that uses diffusion representations to regularize the recognition of unseen attribute-object compositions.

title: Unified and Efficient Point-Line Local Features
summary: Proposes a unified and efficient method for point-line local features to improve multi-view computer vision pipelines for matching and pose estimation.

title: AvatarDynamizer: From Static to Dynamic Human Avatars via Generative Dynamic Textures
summary: Presents AvatarDynamizer, a method that generates dynamic human avatars from static inputs using generative dynamic textures to achieve perceptual realism.

title: Flow Matching Meets 3D Curvilinear Structure Segmentation in Medical Imaging
summary: Applies flow matching techniques for 3D curvilinear structure segmentation in medical imaging, addressing challenges like complex topology and weak contrast.

title: Open-Vocabulary 3D Object Detection with Co-Distillation Discovery and Dual Guidance Robust Training
summary: Proposes a new method for open-vocabulary 3D object detection using co-distillation discovery and dual guidance robust training to detect unseen objects in 3D scenes.

title: From Street View Imagery to Street Quality Indicators: Vision Language Inference for the Suburban 15-minute City
summary: Applies vision-language inference to Street View imagery to derive street quality indicators for urban planning, particularly for the 15-minute city concept.

title: V-REX: Efficient Specialist VLM Training for Veterinary X-Rays
summary: Introduces V-REX, an efficient specialist Vision-Language Model training approach for veterinary X-Rays, challenging assumptions about fine-tuning large foundation models.

title: HandMvNet: Real-Time 3D Hand Pose Estimation Using Multi-View Cross-Attention Fusion
summary: Presents HandMvNet, a real-time method for 3D hand pose and shape estimation from multi-view camera images using cross-attention fusion.

title: BeyondMasks: Evaluating Causal and Physical Consistency in Video Object Removal
summary: Proposes new evaluation protocols for video object removal, focusing on causal and physical consistency beyond traditional masked region fidelity in generative video models.

title: ArmorOCR: Grounded Adversarial Visual Perception via Observation-Transferred Self-Distillation
summary: Introduces ArmorOCR, a method using observation-transferred self-distillation to enhance large multimodal models' robustness against adversarial visual text for OCR.

title: ID-VTG: Image-Disambiguated Video Temporal Grounding
summary: Presents ID-VTG, a method for Image-Disambiguated Video Temporal Grounding that addresses challenges in distinguishing visually similar events with natural language queries.

title: Feature Evolution and Migration during Vision Transformer Training
summary: Investigates feature evolution and migration in Vision Transformers during training by visualizing changes across network depth and training time.

title: DPC-Net: Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration
summary: Introduces DPC-Net, a Dual-Prior Collaborative Network for All-in-One Image Restoration designed to handle diverse image degradations within a unified model.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Workflow Analysis in Colorectal Surgery: A Multicentric, Cross-Procedural Development and Generalization Study
summary: Develops and validates an AI-powered tool for workflow analysis in minimally invasive colorectal surgeries using video-based assessment to improve outcomes.

title: G3Ego: Gaze-Guided Graphs for Egocentric Action Understanding
summary: Proposes G3Ego, a graph-based framework using gaze-guided graphs for egocentric action understanding, focusing on hand-object interactions in first-person videos.

title: RoMAN-Flow: Taming Autoregressive Normalizing Flows for Offline Reinforcement Learning in Robotic Manipulation
summary: This paper introduces RoMAN-Flow, a method using autoregressive normalizing flows for offline reinforcement learning to improve robot policies in robotic manipulation tasks.

title: Unwarping the Lens: A Physics-Grounded Approach to Video Glasses Removal

title: Prompt-Conditioned Channel Attention for Hierarchical Feature Modulation toward Anatomy-Agnostic Segmentation
summary: This paper proposes a prompt-conditioned channel attention method for hierarchical feature modulation, aiming to improve anatomically plausible segmentation despite low contrast and ambiguous boundaries.

title: Ultra-High-Definition Restoration Transformers with Correlation Matching Transformation
summary: This work introduces UHDformer++, a general Transformer-based framework designed for Ultra-High-Definition (UHD) image restoration tasks, operating across high and low-resolution learning spaces.

title: APPROVE: Visual End-User-in-the-Loop Robot Programming with LLMs

title: The Missing Touch: Spatially Distributed Tactile Feedback Brings Teleoperation Closer to Human Dexterity
summary: This research explores how spatially distributed tactile feedback can improve robotic teleoperation, bringing it closer to human dexterity for controlling remote robots.

title: Learning the Right Abstraction: Neural Reduced Dynamics for Complex Robot Control
summary: This work advocates for using neural reduced dynamics in less accurate but faster simulations to facilitate large-scale reinforcement learning for complex robot control in embodied AI.

title: SCAPE: Scenario-Conditioned Simulation-Augmented Policy Evaluation
summary: SCAPE is presented as a method for scenario-conditioned simulation-augmented policy evaluation, aiming to reliably assess robot-learning policies by bridging the sim-to-real gap.

title: Hybrid Feedback Sampling for Sample-Efficient Model Predictive Control
summary: This paper proposes Hybrid Feedback Sampling to improve the sample efficiency of Model Predictive Control (MPC) for real-world robotic systems, particularly for high-dimensional and unstable dynamics.

title: When Automata Meet Streams: Temporal Logic Compilation for Stream-Based Robotics Task and Motion Planning
summary: This research introduces Temporal Logic Compilation for Stream-Based Robotics Task and Motion Planning, integrating symbolic planning with continuous parameters for executing long-horizon robot tasks.

title: Fine-Tuning VLAs with Self-Demonstrated Generative Control for Multi-Task Manipulation
summary: This study addresses fine-tuning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for multi-task robot manipulation, mitigating performance drops caused by hardware mismatches through self-demonstrated generative control.

title: LF-GICP: Parameter-Free Degeneracy-Aware LiDAR Odometry via a Voxel-Normal Localizability Field

title: Multimodal Trajectory Planning for Surface Vehicles using Turning Circle-based Control Barrier Functions
summary: This paper presents a guide path-free multimodal trajectory planning framework for autonomous surface vehicles operating in dynamic environments, integrating Model Predictive Control with control barrier functions.

title: OrthoSkillVLA: Continual Skill Learning via Gradient-Informed Skill Subspace Adaptation
summary: OrthoSkillVLA enables continual skill learning for robot learning using Vision-Language-Action models, adapting skill subspaces to prevent catastrophic forgetting when learning diverse tasks.

title: The Verification Gap in Networked Physical AI: A Post-Semantic Communication Framework

title: World-Model-Grounded LLM Planning for AUV and ASV Navigation Near Offshore Wind Farms
