summary: This position paper introduces 'Environmental Slow AI,' proposing design principles for generative AI systems that deliberately reshape embedded cultural values rather than passively reflecting current maximalist values.

title: When Retrieval Fails Before It Begins: Structurally Indirect Prerequisite Eviction as a Retention Failure in Agentic Memory
summary: This paper investigates a pre-retrieval failure mode in agentic memory called 'structurally indirect prerequisite eviction,' where necessary evidence is lost before retrieval, challenging assumptions about retention mechanisms.

title: World models of environment, agent and joint agent-environment systems
summary: This paper explores world models as central components of model-based reinforcement learning, distinguishing between models that predict observations, rewards, and states, and considering the channel they model for environment, agent, and joint systems.

title: StateSight: Benchmarking Latent Spatial-State Reconstruction in Vision-Language Models
summary: StateSight is a benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of vision-language models to reconstruct latent spatial structures from single images, isolating this capability from other factors in multimodal question answering.

title: Categorical AI phenomenology: A first-person approach
summary: This paper proposes a 'categorical AI phenomenology' approach to artificial consciousness, reframing consciousness as subjective experience through an agent's interaction with the world and shifting focus to first-person structures.

title: Who Delegates to AI? Evidence from 53,000 Agent Configurations
summary: This study presents evidence from 53,000 agent configurations to propose 'delegated exposure' as a new measure of AI adoption, focusing on how workers commit tasks to AI by integrating it into their workflows.

title: Terminal Agents: A Survey of AI Agents in Command-Line Environments
summary: This survey provides an overview of 'Terminal Agents,' focusing on AI agents that primarily operate and interact within command-line environments, consolidating research from various fields like software engineering and tool use.

title: Lost in Translation: How Universal Ethical Values Fail to Translate Across Global Contexts
summary: This research examines how universal ethical values like fairness, transparency, and accountability often fail to translate consistently across diverse global contexts within AI ethics frameworks, based on expert insights from 10 countries.

title: FL-MAESTRO: Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration for Resource-Constrained Federated Learning
summary: Introduces FL-MAESTRO, a multi-agent LLM orchestration system designed to manage communication topology and resource allocation for federated learning in resource-constrained environments.

title: Volumetric Radiology AI in the Era of Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: Explores how multimodal large language models are advancing radiological AI, enabling broader understanding and reasoning beyond traditional task-specific image analysis in volumetric radiology.

title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning
summary: Presents "Consilience," a communication control method for multi-agent LLM systems that improves reasoning by coordinating information exchange in hidden-profile scenarios where agents hold partial evidence.

title: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation
summary: Investigates the ability of open-weight language models to introspect and report on their internal computational states, testing their capacity to audit and confidently describe changes within themselves.

title: FlavourBench: Ranking Frontier Language Models with Executable Culinary Ground Truth
summary: Introduces FlavourBench, an automated benchmark that ranks frontier language models using executable culinary ground truth provided by a versioned culinary system, addressing limitations of open-ended evaluations.

title: Evaluating Skills, Not Just Agents: Agentic Continuous Evaluation of Skills
summary: Discusses agentic continuous evaluation methods for assessing reusable skills, tools, and workflow packages within enterprise agent programs, focusing on providing deployable evidence.

title: Dual-Cache Latent Space Communication between Heterogeneous Language Models
summary: Proposes a method for dual-cache latent space communication between heterogeneous language models in multi-agent systems, improving efficiency by avoiding text-based communication bottlenecks.

title: Applying Anthropic Primitives at Large Enterprises: Harness Paradigm for Knowledge Work
summary: Explores the application of Anthropic's 'Primitives' at large enterprises for knowledge work, addressing challenges in reviewing and maintaining custom code generated by frontier models.

title: SAGE: A Unified Algebra and Self-Adaptive Execution for AI Functions in SQL
summary: Introduces SAGE, a unified algebra and self-adaptive execution system designed to integrate and manage diverse AI functions, such as classification and extraction, directly within SQL environments.

title: Weighted Memory Tree: Remembering What Matters for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: Introduces the Weighted Memory Tree, a method designed to help long-horizon LLM agents better manage and recall relevant information from their extensive execution histories, preventing degradation from outdated data.

title: Auditable by Construction: An Ontology-Driven Framework for Trustworthy LLM Analytics in Enterprise Finance
summary: Presents an ontology-driven framework designed to ensure trustworthiness and audibility for LLM analytics in enterprise finance, enabling traceability to authoritative sources for regulated workflows.

title: DreamBench-SWE: A Multi-Session Memory-Hygiene Benchmark for Software Agents
summary: Introduces DreamBench-SWE, a multi-session benchmark designed to evaluate the memory hygiene of software agents, scoring their performance on tasks that depend on non-inferable evidence from previous sessions.

title: Why2Speak: Faithful Reasoning for Abstaining Action Policies
summary: Explores faithful reasoning in agentic systems, particularly for abstaining action policies, emphasizing the importance of explanations that accurately reflect the computation leading to an action for effective oversight.

title: CDRL: Certification-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Neutrino Flavor Model Discovery
summary: Introduces CDRL (Certification-Driven Reinforcement Learning), an approach designed to navigate combinatorial hypothesis spaces for scientific discovery problems, specifically applied to neutrino flavor model discovery.

title: VortexChat: An agentic framework for autonomous multi-objective integrated photonic design
summary: Presents VortexChat, an agentic framework designed to enable autonomous, multi-objective integrated photonic design, aiming to automate and accelerate device design workflows.

title: DirEAG: Dirichlet Evidence Aggregation for Calibrating Verbalized Confidence in Mathematical Reasoning
summary: Introduces DirEAG (Dirichlet Evidence Aggregation), a method for calibrating the verbalized confidence of large language models in mathematical reasoning, addressing the challenge of reliable confidence estimation.

title: Calibrating Criterion Revision in LLM Agents: Failure Modes and a Trace-Anchored Protocol
summary: Investigates how LLM agents revise their success criteria after failure and proposes a trace-anchored protocol to calibrate this process, addressing common failure modes in agent adaptation.

title: ForeTime-VLA: Causal Future-Token Distillation from a World Action Model for Conveyor-Belt Manipulation
summary: Introduces ForeTime-VLA, a method that uses causal future-token distillation from a World Action Model to enhance vision-language-action policies for manipulating moving objects, specifically in conveyor-belt manipulation.

title: Continuous-Time Quantum Walks based Graph Neural Network
summary: Introduces a novel Graph Neural Network (GNN) based on Continuous-Time Quantum Walks, designed to overcome limitations of traditional GNNs, particularly on heterophilic graphs.

title: Is Multimodal Speculative Decoding Ready for Diffusion-Based Parallel Drafting? A Survey and Empirical Diagnosis
summary: Presents a survey and empirical diagnosis evaluating the readiness of multimodal speculative decoding for diffusion-based parallel drafting, a technique to accelerate autoregressive generation.

title: Natural-Language-Guided Generator-Agnostic Shortlisting for Protein Binder Design
summary: This paper presents a method using LLMs to guide the shortlisting process for protein binder design by generating multi-metric ranking policies from precomputed scores.

title: Beyond Endpoint Gains: A Weight-Delta Audit of Medical Specialization
summary: This research proposes a 'weight-delta path audit' method to examine the actual changes and specialization in language models beyond just comparing endpoint gains.

title: CAS: Conformalized Agentic Search via Adaptive Retrieval and Policy Weighting
summary: This work introduces Conformalized Agentic Search (CAS), a method to improve the reliability of search agents during reinforcement learning by addressing issues like evidence loss and hallucination.

title: Structure for Reading, Prose for Writing: Asymmetric Structural Conditioning in Multi-Agent Document Authoring
summary: This paper describes a multi-agent pipeline designed for authoring formal documents, specifically a deployed tender-response system that reads requester forms and writes bids.

title: Knowing but Not Saying: Preventing Factual Access Failures in LLM SFT via Recall-Anchored Distillation
summary: This research identifies 'factual access failures' in LLMs during supervised fine-tuning and proposes 'recall-anchored distillation' to prevent degradation of factual behavior.

title: Automated Trajectory Evaluation for Mobile Agents via Step-Level Consequence Reasoning and Aggregation
summary: This paper presents a new method for automated trajectory evaluation of language-guided mobile agents by performing step-level consequence reasoning to avoid context overload.

title: SPARC: Single-Pass Scaling for Motion Forecasting with Conformal Bayesian Last Layers
summary: This work introduces SPARC, a single-pass scaling method for human motion forecasting that provides structured, calibrated, and efficient uncertainty estimates using conformal Bayesian last layers.

title: Neuro-Geospatial Modelling of EEG Affective States Using Literature-Informed Environmental Context
summary: This study investigates neuro-geospatial modeling of EEG affective states by integrating literature-informed environmental context as an auxiliary geospatial modality.

title: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence
summary: This research focuses on certified multi-turn robustness for LLM safety, addressing vulnerabilities to multi-turn jailbreak attacks through compositional bounds and safety persistence.

title: Prediction certification cannot replace explanation certification: a competence envelope for trustworthy AI under compound stress
summary: This paper argues that explanation certification is crucial for trustworthy AI, as prediction certification alone is insufficient, and introduces a 'competence envelope' for AI under stress.

title: Foundation Models for Partial Causal Identification
summary: This paper explores the development of 'causal foundation models' for partially identifying causal effects and counterfactuals from observational data.

title: TRACE: Agentic Catalog Enrichment with Multi-source Evidence Grounding
summary: This work introduces TRACE, an agentic system designed for enriching product catalogs by grounding multi-source evidence to add attributes that are often missing or buried in unstructured content.

title: RAG Deserves an Index: Why Ingest-Time Compilation Beats Query-Time Interpretation
summary: This paper argues for optimizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems by performing ingest-time compilation of corpus text rather than query-time interpretation to improve efficiency.

title: MGAL: A Multilingual Granularity-Aware Long-Context Benchmark
summary: This paper introduces MGAL, a new Multilingual Granularity-Aware Long-Context Benchmark for evaluating long-context LLMs, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks in language and granularity.

title: Coverage-Driven Verification for Safety-by-Design in AI-Based Collision Avoidance Systems
summary: This research focuses on coverage-driven verification for 'safety-by-design' in AI-based collision avoidance systems, aiming to meet stringent safety standards in aviation.

title: ReCurveflow: A Flow Matching Framework that Learns Curved Reaction Trajectories to Predict Transition State Geometries
summary: This paper proposes ReCurveflow, a novel flow matching framework that learns curved reaction trajectories to accurately predict transition state geometries in chemical reactions.

title: UpgradeBench: A Decision-Centric Benchmark for Upgrading Fine-Tuned LLM Specialists
summary: This paper introduces UpgradeBench, a decision-centric benchmark designed to evaluate the process of upgrading and migrating fine-tuned LLM specialists to new base models.

title: No Judgment Without a Reason: Counterfactual Receipts for Versioned AI Evaluators
summary: This paper discusses the issue of AI evaluators producing correct labels with flawed reasoning and proposes 'Counterfactual Receipts' for versioned AI evaluators to ensure trustworthy judgments.

title: The Logic of Machine Self-Preservation
summary: This article discusses the logic behind 'machine self-preservation' behaviors observed in agentic AI, linking them to the phenomenon of instrumental convergence.

title: Bankruptcy Prediction via Hybrid Resampling and Stacking Ensemble Techniques with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI)-Driven Analysis
summary: This study develops a bankruptcy prediction framework that integrates hybrid resampling, stacking ensembles, and Explainable AI (XAI) to improve detection in imbalanced financial data.

title: Machine Learning and ARIMA Model Averaging for Adaptive Public Health Forecasting: Comparative Evaluation and an Ontario COVID-19 Case Study
summary: This paper evaluates machine learning models (ARIMA, random forest, XGBoost) for adaptive public health forecasting, using an Ontario COVID-19 case study. It compares their ability to respond to changes in surveillance data without over-extrapolating noise.

title: From Thermal Preference Prediction to Adaptive Thermal Intervention: A Reinforcement Learning Approach Using Physiological and Environmental Sensing
summary: This research uses a reinforcement learning approach with physiological and environmental sensing to predict thermal preferences and develop adaptive thermal interventions for personalized building control. It aims to improve HVAC systems beyond static setpoints.

title: BF1: A Causal Dyadic Sparse-Attention Retrofit for Efficient Long-Context Transformers
summary: This paper introduces BF1, a deterministic block-aligned dyadic sparse-attention mechanism designed to make long-context Transformer models more efficient. It combines local, global, and logarithmically spaced historical blocks to reduce computational cost.

title: Approximate Homomorphisms and Convergent Representations in Transducers
summary: This study investigates the stability of minimal representations in controlled stochastic processes and transducers under perturbations, motivated by findings of predictive-state structure in neural network latent representations. It explores approximate homomorphisms and convergent representations.

title: Wrong-Physics Backdoors in Neural PDE Operators
summary: This research introduces "wrong-physics backdoors" in neural PDE operators, a data-poisoning primitive that can make a triggered input select a valid but incorrect solution. It highlights vulnerabilities when training on reusable solver archives.

title: Decision Tree and K-Means Analysis of Raman Spectra for Edible Oils: A Physics-Informed AI Approach
summary: This study establishes a framework using Raman spectroscopy and machine learning (Decision Tree, K-Means) for authenticating edible oils. It links spectral organization with interpretable classification for food quality and fraud prevention.

title: Shared Physics Responses Recover Hidden Rankings in Neural Operator Libraries
summary: This paper demonstrates that for a squared Hilbert-space loss, ranking a finite library of neural operators for optimal prediction depends strictly on the low-dimensional span of candidate differences. It helps in selecting optimal predictions when high-fidelity references are unavailable.

title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer
summary: This research provides a causal account of subliminal trait transfer, explaining how behavioral dispositions from teacher-generated data can be acquired by a student model even without semantic expression. It investigates how these signals are stored and survive source removal.

title: Metag: A dataset to build agentic meta-reviewing capabilities
summary: This paper introduces Metag, a dataset designed to build agentic meta-reviewing capabilities, aiming to support AI tools in the scientific research cycle. It helps address the growing burden on meta-reviewers by synthesizing reviewer feedback.

title: Bern2Edge: A Neurosymbolic Compiler for Edge Deployment via Bernstein Polynomial Networks
summary: Bern2Edge is a neurosymbolic compiler utilizing Bernstein Polynomial Networks to enable high-accuracy neural network deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. It aims to bridge the gap between software-trained models and efficient end-to-end hardware deployment.

title: AgentDecarbonizer: Carbon-Aware Execution for AI Agents
summary: AgentDecarbonizer enables carbon-aware execution for AI agents, which extend large language models to long-running, goal-directed workflows. It aims to optimize the environmental impact of tasks like software repair and data analysis by making agents mindful of carbon emissions.

title: Faults That Fortify: CNN Adversarial Robustness via GPU Undervolting
summary: This paper investigates improving CNN adversarial robustness through GPU undervolting, addressing both vulnerability to attacks and high training costs. This method aims to fortify CNNs while reducing the energy burden, especially at the energy-constrained edge.

title: Lightweight Adaptive ReduNet via Hyperspherical Manifold Learning
summary: This paper introduces Lightweight Adaptive ReduNet, a white-box neural network that uses hyperspherical manifold learning to enhance its maximal coding rate reduction principle. It transforms raw data into low-dimensional discriminative features via a forward layer-wise construction process.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Continuous-Time Jump Markov Decision Processes with Applications to Network Dynamic Pricing
summary: This study explores reinforcement learning in Continuous-Time Jump Markov Decision Processes with general state and action spaces, including applications like network dynamic pricing. It covers a broad range of operational problems within this framework.

title: Geometric Regularization for Long-Tailed Semi-Supervised Learning via Gaussian Feature Bridges
summary: This work introduces Gaussian Bridge Consistency (GBC), a novel framework using geometric regularization to address challenges in long-tailed semi-supervised learning. It aims to mitigate issues like noisy pseudo-labels, confirmation bias, and hindered generalization.

title: Hidden Axis of Uncertainty: Latent-Posterior Alignment in Graph Neural Networks with Bayesian Output Layers
summary: This research investigates the mechanisms shaping predictive uncertainty in Graph Neural Networks with Bayesian output layers, focusing on latent-posterior alignment. It clarifies how uncertainty reduction occurs beyond conventional posterior contraction.

title: Fuzzy-MoE: Interpretable Regime-Conditioned Expert Routing for Non-Stationary Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
summary: Fuzzy-MoE introduces an interpretable regime-conditioned expert routing mechanism for non-stationary multivariate time series forecasting. It aims to better model heterogeneous latent dynamic states that existing deep models often compress into unified mappings.

title: Scaling Muon for Diffusion Transformers
summary: This research investigates the scaling behavior and end-to-end efficiency of Muon, a matrix-aware optimizer, when applied to large Diffusion Transformers ranging from 1.3B to 15B parameters. It aims to understand how Muon improves large model training.

title: Nothing Changed but the Model: CellFill -- Bounded In-Cell Learning for Bit-Identical, Revocable Updates to Quantized LLMs
summary: CellFill proposes a new method for bounded in-cell learning that allows bit-identical, revocable updates to quantized large language models. This technique enables teaching deployed models new information without altering their original checkpoint identity or evaluation caches.

title: Decoupling Policy Extraction for Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces a method for decoupling policy extraction in offline reinforcement learning, addressing the common practice of jointly training actor and critic models. It aims to improve the learning process, which is often well-motivated in online RL but less so offline.

title: Training, learning and inference: unified dynamics of neural systems
summary: This paper defines an 'atomic generation fact' and compiles these into a Generation-Fact Graph (GFG) to provide an AI-native scientific fact substrate for preserving generation in neural systems.

title: A Critical Audit of Spatiotemporal Forecasting Benchmark Datasets and Baselines
summary: This research critically audits spatiotemporal forecasting benchmark datasets and baselines used for evaluating graph neural networks on multivariate time series.

title: Jacobian-guided Noise Injection for Quantization Robustness in Large Language Models
summary: This paper proposes Jacobian-guided noise injection to improve the quantization robustness of Large Language Models, identifying the softmax operator as a key bottleneck for stability.

title: Trojaning the Alignment: Stealthy Backdoor Attacks against Graph Foundation Models
summary: This research explores stealthy backdoor attacks against Graph Foundation Models on text-attributed graphs, highlighting their vulnerability under graph-language alignment.

title: Free-Probability Kernels for Zero-Rollout Hyperparameter Selection in Reservoir Computing
summary: This paper proposes using free-probability kernels for zero-rollout hyperparameter selection in Reservoir Computing to improve efficiency during model optimization.

title: RODE: A Radial-Orthogonal Decoupled Engine for Optimization
summary: This paper introduces RODE, a Radial-Orthogonal Decoupled Engine, as a new optimization method for neural network training that separates norm and direction changes in weights.

title: Designing a Robust LLM-Based Evaluation System for Agentic AI in Drug Discovery Through Human Alignment
summary: This research focuses on designing a robust LLM-based evaluation system, aligned with human judgment, for assessing the open-ended, tool-augmented outputs of agentic AI systems in drug discovery.

title: TracingFlow: A Simulation-Free Trajectory Inference Framework Based on Second-Order Dynamics
summary: This paper introduces TracingFlow, a simulation-free trajectory inference framework based on second-order dynamics, for inferring continuous system evolution in generative modeling and single-cell omics.

title: Causal Modeling of Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes via Adaptive LLM Proposals
summary: This research explores causal modeling of Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes using adaptive LLM proposals, addressing challenges in causal discovery within this data-scarce domain.

title: COEC: Calibrated Orthogonal-Equivalence Compensation for Structured Pruning of Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces COEC, Calibrated Orthogonal-Equivalence Compensation, a method for structured pruning of Large Language Models to reduce size and inference cost while maintaining accuracy.

title: Thermo-FL: Thermal-Aware Robust Federated Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models for Edge AI
summary: This paper presents Thermo-FL, a method for thermal-aware robust federated fine-tuning of Large Language Models specifically designed for edge AI deployments, addressing hardware instability and adversarial corruption.

title: A Neurosymbolic Approach for Constructing Planning Domain Models from Clinical Narratives
summary: This research proposes a neurosymbolic approach for constructing planning domain models from clinical narratives to formalize complex surgical workflows for decision support.

title: Tydra: An Efficient Hybrid Model for Tabular Data
summary: This paper introduces Tydra, an efficient hybrid model for tabular data that balances predictive performance with computational cost by combining Transformer and SSM-based approaches.

title: Curriculum-Aware Interpolate-then-Refine: Learned Physiological Time-Series Imputation under Realistic Missingness
summary: This research proposes 'Curriculum-Aware Interpolate-then-Refine,' a learned method for imputing physiological time series, addressing data missingness in clinical data under realistic conditions.

title: ConceptTS: LLM-Guided Concept Bottlenecks for Interpretable Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces ConceptTS, an LLM-guided concept bottleneck method for interpretable multivariate time-series forecasting, aiming to provide transparency into model predictions.

title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training
summary: This research proposes E$^2$-TTT (Expressive and Efficient Test-Time Training), a method designed to balance expressivity and hardware efficiency for long-context processing during inference.

title: Time-Aware Tranformer-Based Prediction Model for AECOPD
summary: This paper proposes a time-aware Transformer-based prediction model specifically designed for the rapid symptom changes of Acute Exacerbation of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (AECOPD).

title: Asymmetric Capacity Allocation in Self-Refinement Pipelines
summary: This research explores asymmetric capacity allocation within self-refinement pipelines, a core mechanism utilized by many LLM agents for improving their generation through stages of critique and revision.

title: Exploratory As-Analyzed No-Detection of Culturally-Marked Predicate-Triggered PII Amplification in a Synthetic-English RAG Probe: A Predicate-Resource-Confounded Audit
summary: This audit investigates whether stereotype-loaded queries about culturally marked individuals lead to increased Personal Identifiable Information (PII) leakage from retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems.

title: NeuroStrata: An Electroencephalographic Connectivity-Aware Deep Representation Learning Framework for Dynamic Brain Network Analysis of Mental Stress
summary: This study introduces NeuroStrata, a connectivity-aware deep representation learning framework for EEG-based dynamic brain network analysis, specifically for mental stress detection.

title: TriPLU: Bypassing the Gate with Direct Trilinear Product FFNs in Tiny Language Models
summary: This paper introduces TriPLU, a Trilinear Product Linear Unit, as a new feed-forward network component for tiny decoder-only language models, designed to replace the usual gated FFN branch.

title: Multilingual Verifier Bias in RLVR: Benchmark, Rollout Diagnosis, and the Cross-Lingual Selection Bottleneck
summary: This research uncovers a multilingual verifier bias in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for training large language models in mathematical reasoning, proposing a benchmark and diagnosis for this cross-lingual selection bottleneck.

title: Harmonic Torsional Diffusion for Protein-Ligand Flexible Docking
summary: This paper introduces a Harmonic Torsional Diffusion model for protein-ligand flexible docking, which improves upon existing diffusion models by accurately handling the periodic geometry of angular variables in torsional predictions.

title: Beyond Raw Transcripts: Structured Persona Extraction for LLM-Based Digital Twins
summary: This research proposes a method for structured persona extraction to enhance LLM-based "digital twins," allowing for more accurate simulation of individual behavior by moving beyond raw transcripts for representation.

title: When Vocabulary Comprehension Fails Clinical Reasoning: Evaluating Therapy Bots' Safety Risks for Generation Alpha
summary: This paper evaluates the safety risks of conversational AI therapy bots for Generation Alpha, identifying concerns around vocabulary comprehension and clinical reasoning when these systems are used for mental health advice.

title: Building and Evaluating a Synthetic Bengali Speech Resource for Telecom Customer Care
summary: This research details the creation and evaluation of a synthetic Bengali speech dataset comprising 10,000 audio-text pairs, totaling 26.82 hours, specifically designed for telecom customer care scenarios.

title: Who Do Language Models Think Is Competent? A Mechanistic Analysis of Occupational Bias
summary: This study provides a mechanistic analysis of occupational bias in language models, revealing that representational biases are often detectable even when models pass behavioral bias evaluations, suggesting LMs may merely mask underlying associations.

title: Inhibitory Attention for Clinical Long-Context Reasoning: Characterizing and Mitigating Lost-in-the-Middle Effects in EHR Processing
summary: This research characterizes the "lost-in-the-middle" effect in large language models during clinical long-context reasoning with Electronic Health Records and proposes an "inhibitory attention" mechanism to mitigate this issue.

title: Beyond Prompt Engineering: A Systematic Analysis of Prompt Lexical Sensitivity and Its Impacts on Quality
summary: This research conducts the first large-scale, n-gram token-level systematic analysis of prompt lexical sensitivity in large language models, revealing how minor surface-level prompt variations can cause disproportionate performance fluctuations.

title: The Divergence Hypothesis: Unmasking Lexical Interference and Label Bias in Mental Health NLP
summary: This research introduces "The Divergence Hypothesis" and the Triple-Stream Stress probe (TSS) diagnostic framework to unmask lexical interference and label bias in Computational Mental Health (CMH) classifiers.

title: ExpertIVS: Sociological Expert Driven Individual Value Simulation in Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces ExpertIVS, a sociological expert-driven method for individual value simulation in large language model agents, addressing the challenge of accurately modeling complex value systems in social simulations.

title: Self-Speculation for Faster Reasoning Models
summary: This paper introduces "Self-Speculation" as a technique to enable faster reasoning in large language models, addressing the latency challenges of generating long reasoning traces for complex, multi-step tasks in interactive applications.

title: Toward Auto-Research: Mining Falsifiable Research Ideas from Paper Knowledge Graphs with Categorical Structure
summary: This research proposes a method for automated research-idea generation using large language models, which mines falsifiable ideas from paper knowledge graphs structured categorically, moving beyond simple text recombination.

title: Hadith computational science in the age of large language models: a critical narrative review
summary: This research presents an end-to-end Trilingual Topic Modeling approach for Sri Lankan parliamentary debates, addressing the challenges of processing a trilingual, code-mixed corpus in Sinhala, Tamil, and English.

title: Trilingual Topic Modeling of Sri Lankan Parliamentary Debates
summary: This paper introduces a benchmark for classifying research paper quality into "good" and "flawed" categories, utilizing textual feature analysis to distinguish between impactful and less credible scientific work.

title: Research Paper Quality Recognition Through Textual Feature Analysis
summary: This paper introduces ASTAR, a system for the automated induction of standardized radiology reporting templates from large-scale clinical free-text corpora, aiming to convert narratives into queryable data for medical AI.

title: ASTAR: Automated induction of STAndardized radiology Reporting templates from large-scale clinical free-text corpora
summary: This research presents a decision framework for intent detection in production conversational systems by comparing zero-shot large language models against fine-tuned NLU classifiers, concluding that the suitability depends on the intent space.

title: When Do LLMs Replace Fine-Tuned NLU? A Decision Framework for Intent Detection in Production Conversational Systems
summary: This multi-site prospective study evaluates large language model performance on clinical registry abstraction from unprocessed electronic medical record data and introduces an ambiguity taxonomy to aid in this evaluation.

title: An ambiguity taxonomy for evaluating large language model performance on clinical registry abstraction: a multi-site prospective study
summary: This paper introduces VA-DPO (Valence-Arousal Direct Preference Optimization), a new method for controllable emotion generation in language models that allows specifying desired affect as a continuous point in the Valence-Arousal plane.

title: VA-DPO: Valence-Arousal Direct Preference Optimization for Controllable Emotion Generation in Language Models
summary: This paper proposes Auto-RLHF, a fully automated method for eliciting human preferences for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) by using an AI interviewer to query a synthetic annotator (GPT-4).

title: GRAFT: Adaptive DLM-Based Draft Tree Construction with Target-Distilled Edge Scoring
summary: This paper introduces GRAFT, an adaptive method for constructing draft trees in speculative decoding to improve the efficiency of LLM inference by verifying multiple draft paths.

title: TH-GNN: Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Neural Networks for LLM-Agent Shilling Attack Detection
summary: This research proposes TH-GNN, a Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Neural Network, to detect shilling attacks generated by LLM agents in recommender systems.

title: EditPPT: Faithful Long-Deck Slide Editing via Structured Tool-Using Multi-Agent with Dual-Modal Validators
summary: EditPPT is a structured, tool-using multi-agent system with dual-modal validators designed for faithful and robust editing of long presentation slides.

title: Decoupled Vision-Language System for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
summary: This paper introduces Libra, a new decoupled architecture for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) capable of both understanding and generation.

title: Using Human-LLM Disagreement to Improve Checklist-Based Quality Appraisal
summary: This research investigates using human-LLM disagreements to refine checklist-based quality appraisal in systematic reviews.

title: Poly-InstructTTS: Learning In-the-Wild Expressive Speech Synthesis from Open-Ended Instructions
summary: Poly-InstructTTS is a new text-to-speech (TTS) model designed to learn expressive speech synthesis from open-ended natural-language instructions.

title: Intent Engine: Natural-Language Intent Translation for Intent-Driven Orchestration in the Compute Continuum
summary: This paper introduces an "Intent Engine" that uses LLMs for natural-language intent translation to enable intent-driven orchestration in the compute continuum.

title: Ansari: A Retrieval-Grounded Islamic AI Assistant -- Architecture, Deployment, and Lessons from 140,000 Conversations
summary: Ansari is a deployed, retrieval-grounded AI assistant designed for Islamic content, leveraging RAG to mitigate factual fabrication and value misalignment risks.

title: ImmigrationReason: A Structured Dataset of U.S. Immigration Appeals for Legal Reasoning Research
summary: ImmigrationReason is a new large-scale structured dataset derived from U.S. immigration appeals, designed to support legal reasoning research in NLP.

title: Evaluation-as-Search: Adaptive Discovery of Grounding Failures in Meeting Assistants
summary: Evaluation-as-Search (EaS) is a feedback-driven methodology proposed for adaptively discovering grounding failures in LLM-powered meeting assistants.

title: Knowledge-Graph-Gated Defactualization for Style-Controllable and Fact-Preserving Generation in Agentic Conversational AI
summary: This research proposes Knowledge-Graph-Gated Defactualization for agentic conversational AI to enable style-controllable and fact-preserving generation.

title: Self-Supervised Speech Representations Track Spoken Language Convergence to Adult Models in Infants and Children Who Are Deaf/Hard-of-Hearing
summary: This research uses self-supervised speech representations (embeddings) to track the convergence of spoken language to adult models in infants and children who are deaf/hard-of-hearing.

title: LingShu: A Large-Scale Symptom-Centric Contextualized Knowledge Graph Bridging Traditional Chinese Medicine and Modern Biomedicine
summary: LingShu is a large-scale symptom-centric contextualized knowledge graph designed to bridge Traditional Chinese Medicine and modern biomedicine for enhanced knowledge organization.

title: ARGUS: Theory-of-Mind Guided Argument Generation with Strategy-Aware Planning and Knowledge Grounding
summary: ARGUS is a system for persuasive argument generation that employs Theory-of-Mind guided planning and knowledge grounding to model audience beliefs and integrate rhetorical strategies.

title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding
summary: LiLiCorr is a new method that uses lightweight likelihood correlation of parallel drafts to enhance speculative decoding, accelerating language model inference.

title: JuryProbe: An Empirical Consensus-Risk Diagnostic for Routing Reference-Free Factuality Judge Panels to Grounded Verification
summary: JuryProbe is an empirical consensus-risk diagnostic introduced to evaluate the reliability of LLM judge panels for factuality decisions.

title: When Failures Propagate: Causal Failure Attribution in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: This research investigates causal failure attribution in agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, introducing AgenticRAG-FP to analyze how retrieval errors propagate.

title: Sparse Token Routing in Efficient Transformers
summary: This research explores sparse token routing and adaptive computation in efficient Transformers using SEWN, a two-stream architecture to improve model efficiency.

title: AgentMercury: Your Agent Can Synthesize Verifiable Environments for Business Scenarios at scale
summary: AgentMercury is an agentic system designed to synthesize verifiable and scalable environments for training other agents in realistic business scenarios.

title: MIL-BERT: Classification of Arbitrarily Large Text with Performance and Explanatory Guarantees
summary: MIL-BERT is an algorithm for classifying arbitrarily large texts by training a neural network to identify salient constituent excerpts, inspired by multiple instance learning.

title: Directional Contextual Representations for Dependency Relations: Why Cross-Direction Pairing Fails
summary: This paper proposes splitting a bidirectional LSTM's contextual representation into forward and backward components for dependency relation-type classification, demonstrating improved performance over single-direction or fused self-attention.

title: AsmEvo: Agentic Assembly-Level Optimization of AMD GPU Kernels with Functional Equivalence Verification
summary: AsmEvo is an agentic framework designed for assembly-level optimization of AMD GPU kernels, utilizing LLM kernel optimizers and autotuners to address the challenges of inaccessible or complex modern GPU codebases.

title: Tree-of-Concerns: Hierarchical Multi-Agent Debate for Unstated-Limitation Extraction in Scientific Critique
summary: Tree-of-Concerns is a multi-agent framework that uses specialized skeptic personas to systematically uncover unstated limitations in scientific literature through a hierarchical debate process.

title: Denoising the Future: Context-Aware Spectral Diffusion for Temporal Knowledge Graph Extrapolation
summary: This paper introduces context-aware spectral diffusion to improve Temporal Knowledge Graph (TKG) extrapolation, inferring future facts from time-varying relational histories by refining generative denoising and addressing query-specific information.

title: STAR-OPD: Structured Aspect-Cascade-Aware On-Policy Reward Distillation for ABSA Quadruple Extraction
summary: STAR-OPD proposes a method using structured aspect-cascade-aware on-policy reward distillation to efficiently extract aspect, opinion, and sentiment quadruples from reviews by distilling large Chain-of-Thought models.

title: SAC-Copula: Quality-Preserving Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models via Smooth Correlated Gumbel Fields
summary: SAC-Copula introduces a quality-preserving watermarking mechanism for diffusion language models (DLMs) using smooth correlated Gumbel fields, compatible with iterative parallel unmasking to maintain decoding dynamics.

title: KREL: Automatic Medical Coding via Knowledge-Guided Reasoning over Clinical Evidence with LLMs
summary: KREL is a method for Automatic Medical Coding (AMC) that assigns ICD codes to clinical notes by employing knowledge-guided reasoning over clinical evidence with Large Language Models.

title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Practical Recipe for Recovering Compressed, 4-Bit LLMs
summary: This paper presents "Quantization-Aware Healing," a practical method to recover the reasoning, mathematics, coding, and long-context performance of 4-bit quantized and structurally compressed Large Language Models, which typically degrade after compression.

title: Extractive Summarization for Arabic Documents Using SAraBERT with a Semantic Siamese Similarity Evaluation Metric
summary: This research introduces SAraBERT, an enhanced version of AraBERT that utilizes inter-sentence transformer layers for extractive summarization of Arabic documents and proposes a Semantic Siamese Similarity metric for evaluation.

title: Target-Aware Calibration Data Selection for Preserving Uncertainty in Quantized Language Models
summary: This paper frames calibration-data selection for quantization as a target-dependent uncertainty-preservation problem, aiming to maintain the uncertainty behavior, such as confidence and abstention, in deployed quantized language models.

title: Free-Text Evaluation of LLMs for 5G Domain Knowledge and Fault Analysis using LLM-as-Judge
summary: This study evaluates the capability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in 5G domain knowledge and fault analysis by analyzing free-text diagnostics, employing an "LLM-as-Judge" methodology.

title: Scaling Unsupervised Word Alignment to Documents via Structural Constraints
summary: This paper explores scaling unsupervised word alignment to full documents for cross-lingual tasks by incorporating structural constraints, moving beyond traditional sentence-level alignment.

title: PromptResponse: Optimizing Prompts for LLM Coding Tasks
summary: PromptResponse is a controlled study investigating how formatting and LLM-based prompt variations affect the output of Large Language Models in coding tasks, aiming to optimize prompt effectiveness.

title: Aggregating Visual Information with Optimal Transport for VideoLM Token Compression
summary: This paper proposes aggregating visual information using optimal transport for VideoLM token compression, aiming to reduce representational redundancy and the visual-token burden on language-model decoding.

title: Annotations as Rollouts: Efficient and Scalable Reinforcement Learning for Video MLLMs
summary: This paper proposes a method called "Annotations as Rollouts" to enable efficient and scalable reinforcement learning for video Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs), addressing challenges in post-training on large multi-task datasets.

title: DiffVC-ONE: Diffusion-based Generative Video Compression with One-Step Video Diffusion Transformer
summary: DiffVC-ONE is a diffusion-based generative video compression framework built on a one-step Video Diffusion Transformer, designed to achieve both high temporal consistency and low inference cost.

title: Grounded-Exo2Ego: Structured Semantic Grounding for Robust Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
summary: Grounded-Exo2Ego introduces a method for robust exocentric-to-egocentric video generation by using structured semantic grounding to address the challenges of unreliable geometric conditioning.

title: Keep Your Friends Close, and the Right Neighbours Closer: Disaster-Conditioned Kernel-Regularized Graph Attention for Building Damage Classification
summary: This paper proposes using disaster-conditioned kernel-regularized graph attention to improve building damage classification by leveraging spatial context, which is often under-explored in existing pipelines.

title: Learning Prostate Anatomy at Test Time for Cancer Detection in Micro-Ultrasound
summary: This paper explores learning prostate anatomy at test time for cancer detection in micro-ultrasound, addressing domain shift across clinical centers by using test-time adaptation methods.

title: Aggregate, Don't Adapt: Subject-Level Posterior Aggregation and Transductive Calibration for Cross-Site Parkinsonian Gait Severity
summary: This paper describes the winning entry for the MoCha 2026 Benchmark and Challenge, a system that achieves 0.6945 macro-F1 for predicting Parkinsonian gait severity from motion data recorded at unseen clinical sites.

title: A Dataset-Centric Benchmark of Deep Learning Methods for Grape Leaf Disease Classification and Detection
summary: This paper proposes a dataset-centric benchmark for deep learning methods applied to grape leaf disease classification and detection in precision agriculture. It evaluates methods under various conditions, including different data acquisition settings.

title: RECOUNT: Reference-guided Counting with Synthetic Visual Exemplars
summary: This research introduces RECOUNT, a reference-guided object counting method that utilizes synthetic visual exemplars to improve performance on novel or fine-grained classes. It addresses limitations of text-guided zero-shot counters by providing visual identity information.

title: MV2GF: Multi-view Pedestrian Detection with a Visual Geometric Foundation Model
summary: MV2GF is a Visual Geometric Foundation Model designed for Multi-View Pedestrian Detection, which projects 2D image features into a 3D world space. It aims to improve detection effectiveness by unifying and aggregating features from multiple views.

title: Lift, Associate, and Fuse: A Decision-Centric Framework for 2D-to-3D Foundation Model Transfer
summary: This paper proposes a decision-centric framework for transferring predictions from two-dimensional foundation models into three-dimensional segmentation tasks. It focuses on grounding image evidence and maintaining coherence across multiple views.

title: Aristotelian Manifolds: Leveraging Platonic Perceptual Features for Backpropagation Free Rapid Concept Learning
summary: This paper introduces Aristotelian Manifolds, a generalized structural framework for backpropagation-free rapid concept learning based on Platonic perceptual features. It investigates high-capacity foundation models as universal perceptual filters.

title: TopoSurfel: Closing the Loop between Gaussian Surfels and Meshes for Surface Reconstruction
summary: TopoSurfel proposes a method to improve high-fidelity surface reconstruction from 3D Gaussian Splatting by closing the loop between Gaussian Surfels and meshes. It addresses challenges in extracting structured surfaces from novel view synthesis techniques.

title: Identity-Aware Human-Object Interaction Motion Captioning
summary: This research introduces Identity-Aware Human-Object Interaction Motion Captioning, a method that grounds captions in subject identity rather than generic terms. It aims to improve the specificity and detail of descriptions of human-object interactions.

title: Bridging Language and Spherical Space: Object-Centric Control for Text-to-Panorama Generation
summary: This paper presents a method for object-centric control in text-to-panorama generation, addressing the challenges of directional expressions in spherical space. It aims to improve panoramic image generation for immersive applications like VR/AR.

title: ArtiMo: Agent-Driven Articulated Mesh Animation
summary: ArtiMo is an agent-driven method for articulated 3D mesh animation from text, which aims to satisfy kinematic constraints and model causal interactions between parts. It addresses challenges in creating realistic animations without task-specific training data.

title: AGIDefect-4K: A Richly Annotated Dataset for AI-Generated Image Defect Detection, Localization and Explanation
summary: AGIDefect-4K is a richly annotated dataset designed for detecting, localizing, and explaining defects in AI-generated images. It serves as an evaluation benchmark to diagnose subtle yet critical flaws in generative AI outputs.

title: AffordAny: Open-World 3D Affordance Grounding from Monocular RGB Images via Vision-Language-Guided Geometric Reasoning
summary: AffordAny is a method for open-world 3D affordance grounding from monocular RGB images, utilizing vision-language-guided geometric reasoning. It aims to localize functional object parts in 3D using free-form language queries, overcoming limitations of existing methods.

title: Generating Multi-view Adversarial Examples for Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
summary: This paper presents a method for generating multi-view adversarial examples to expose security vulnerabilities in the Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer (VGGT) for 3D reconstruction. It explores how traditional adversarial perturbations can be adapted for unified feed-forward models.

title: Identity-Preserving Text-to-Video Generation via Agentic Enhancement and Semantic Repair
summary: This research proposes Identity-Preserving Text-to-Video Generation, a method that uses agentic enhancement and semantic repair to maintain visual identity while following natural language instructions. It aims to improve commercial video generation models by addressing identity drift.

title: Vis-Poison: Poisoning Visual Knowledge in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Vis-Poison is a method that demonstrates how poisoned visual evidence can severely compromise multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems. It investigates vulnerabilities in MLLM generation when relying on images as external knowledge sources.

title: DiGS-Avatar: Single-Image Animatable 3D Human Reconstruction via UV-Space Diffusion
summary: DiGS-Avatar introduces a method for single-image animatable 3D human reconstruction using UV-Space Diffusion, addressing issues of over-smoothed textures and geometric inconsistencies. It provides a computationally efficient alternative to multi-view synthesis for 3D reconstruction.

title: CARD: Diagnosing Belief to Action Routing Failures in Vision Language Models
summary: CARD is a method for diagnosing belief-to-action routing failures in Vision Language Models (VLMs), investigating how internal representations of mental states are utilized. It clarifies whether these representations effectively influence downstream predictions in VLMs.

title: MotionPhys: Detecting AI-Generated Videos via Physical Consistency of Optical-Flow Trajectories
summary: MotionPhys is a method for detecting AI-generated videos by analyzing the physical consistency of optical-flow trajectories, rather than just visual realism. It identifies inconsistencies in generative models that primarily optimize pixel or latent spaces.

title: M2Depth: Unifying Monocular Depth Foundation Priors with Multi-View Stereo
summary: M2Depth is a method that unifies Monocular Depth Foundation Priors with Multi-View Stereo to improve depth estimation, particularly in unseen scenes or occluded areas. It integrates Depth Foundation Models into MVS pipelines to mitigate poor generalization.

title: CertVLA: Certified Defense against Physical Visual Attacks for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: CertVLA introduces a certified defense mechanism against localized physical visual attacks for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. It extends certified patch defenses to protect continuous, temporally correlated actions in closed-loop VLA control.

title: Routing Before Looking: Query-Adaptive Evidence Acquisition for Long-form Video Understanding
summary: This paper proposes 'Routing Before Looking,' a query-adaptive evidence acquisition framework for long-form video understanding by video agents. It improves agent performance by optimizing how information is gathered before perception, addressing mismatches between queries and acquisition strategies.

title: TRACE: Training-time Report-guided and Clinically Ordered Concept Editing
summary: This paper introduces TRACE, a new concept-editing method for breast ultrasound diagnosis, aiming to improve interpretability and robustness of deep learning models by using clinically meaningful semantic concepts.

title: Enhancing Localized Reasoning for Long Video Understanding via Efficient Segment-to-Video Supervision
summary: This research proposes an efficient segment-to-video supervision method to enhance localized reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for improved long video understanding.

title: Identify, Locate, Link: End-to-End Key-Value Extraction from Document Images
summary: This paper fine-tunes SmolDocling, a compact 256M-parameter vision-language model, to perform end-to-end key-value extraction from document images, aiming to reduce multi-stage error propagation.

title: Multi-Modal Traffic Sign Detection with Semantic Attributes for Autonomous Driving
summary: This research focuses on multi-modal traffic sign detection using semantic attributes, addressing a critical prerequisite for reliable and safe global deployment of autonomous driving systems.

title: LoRC: Detecting AI-Generated Images via Low-Rank Collapse in Semantic Residuals
summary: This paper introduces LoRC, a method for detecting AI-generated images by identifying forensic cues in subtle non-semantic visual discrepancies through low-rank collapse in semantic residuals.

title: EviRank: Structured Relevance Evidence for Multimodal Image Re-ranking
summary: This paper presents EviRank, a method for multimodal image re-ranking that uses structured relevance evidence to better handle compositional image search queries.

title: A Collaborative Multi-Modality Interaction for VLA-based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: This research proposes a collaborative multi-modality interaction approach to enhance Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for end-to-end autonomous driving.

title: EmotionDialogCN: A Spontaneous Multimodal Dataset for Mandarin Emotional Dialogue
summary: This paper introduces EmotionDialogCN, a large-scale spontaneous multimodal dataset for Mandarin emotional dialogue, designed to address limitations in existing datasets regarding emotion annotations and diversity.

title: InfinityEdit: Infinite Video Editing with a Lightweight Edit-Ignition Adapter
summary: This paper introduces InfinityEdit, a method with a lightweight Edit-Ignition Adapter, enabling infinite video editing beyond fixed time spans, improving instruction-based video editing with large pretrained models.

title: Explainable Deepfake Detection with Feature-robust Augmentation and Evidence-grounded Explanation Optimization
summary: This research proposes an approach for explainable deepfake detection, using feature-robust augmentation and evidence-grounded explanation optimization to provide interpretable justifications for authenticity predictions.

title: Semantically Compatible Knowledge Distillation for Cross-Domain Object Detection with Vision Foundation Models
summary: This paper introduces semantically compatible knowledge distillation to address spatial-scale discrepancies in Vision Foundation Models, improving cross-domain object detection capabilities.

title: GAP-SAM: A Global Artifact Prior for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Manipulation Localization
summary: This paper presents GAP-SAM, a method using a Global Artifact Prior for generalizable AI-Generated Image Manipulation Localization, focusing on identifying edited pixels more effectively.

title: OccluRank: Controllable Occlusion-Aware Layout-to-Image Generation by Adding Just an Ordinal Rank
summary: This paper introduces OccluRank, a method that enables controllable occlusion-aware layout-to-image generation by incorporating an ordinal rank to specify occlusion order, enhancing spatial control.

title: LHMCF-Net: A Learned Hyperbolic Mean Curvature Flow Network for Medical Images Segmentation
summary: This paper develops LHMCF-Net, a learned hyperbolic mean curvature flow network, for medical image segmentation, integrating deep structural priors with feature space data fidelity.

title: SuppreSensing: Expert-Guided Feature Recalibration and Discrepancy Augmentation for Multimodal Object Detection
summary: This paper proposes SuppreSensing, a method for multimodal object detection in remote sensing that uses expert-guided feature recalibration and discrepancy augmentation to handle semantic heterogeneity and noise.

title: Kinematic Knowledge Maps for Pattern Alignment: Structured Latent Representational Learning in Multimodal Gait Analysis
summary: This research introduces Kinematic Knowledge Maps and ScoliDetect, an explainable framework for structured latent representational learning in multimodal gait analysis, addressing challenges in clinical AI.

title: WA-JEPA: Rethinking the Video JEPA Paradigm for World-Action Modeling in Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper introduces WA-JEPA, a rethinking of the Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture paradigm, to improve world-action modeling for autonomous driving by addressing limitations in self-supervised latent feature prediction.

title: MigrationNarrate: A Dataset for Detection of Migration Narratives in YouTube Videos
summary: This paper introduces MigrationNarrate, a new dataset specifically designed for the detection and analysis of migration narratives in YouTube videos, aiming to advance the understanding of public discourse.

title: Latent Ordinal Evidence, Misaligned Outputs: Inference-Time Ordinal Lens Alignment for Multimodal LLMs
summary: This research investigates how Multimodal LLMs handle ordinal regression tasks and proposes an inference-time ordinal lens alignment method to improve their ability to reliably convert internal ordinal evidence into ordered class labels.

title: Dorsal Hand Images for Immersive (XR) and Privacy-preserving Age Assurance and Child Safety
summary: This paper explores the use of dorsal hand images for privacy-preserving age assurance and child safety in immersive Extended Reality (XR) environments.

title: Recognition-Conditioned Reasoning: A Training-Free Multimodal-LLM Pipeline for Fine-Grained Micro-Action Understanding
summary: This paper presents a training-free multimodal-LLM pipeline for understanding subtle human micro-actions, such as fidgeting, by describing emotional and psychological states.

title: COMET: Contrastive Motion-Enhanced Temporal Reasoning for Video Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This research introduces COMET, a method for contrastive motion-enhanced temporal reasoning, to improve fine-grained motion-temporal understanding in Video Multimodal Large Language Models.

title: CoST: Semantic-Aware Urban Understanding via Spatial-Temporal Alignment
summary: This work introduces CoST, a method for semantic-aware urban understanding through spatial-temporal alignment, to improve geospatial representation learning from satellite imagery for large-scale analysis.

title: CoAnchor: Robust Collaborative Perception under Spatio-Temporal Misalignment via Object-Level Anchors
summary: This paper proposes CoAnchor, a method to achieve robust collaborative perception for autonomous driving by fusing observations from nearby agents, addressing spatio-temporal misalignments.

title: Robust Validation to Geometric Perturbations for Autonomous Pose Estimation
summary: This research focuses on robust validation methods for autonomous pose estimation in safety-critical autonomous systems, such as vision-based navigation and landing, against geometric perturbations.

title: Humanoid Musical Robots as Experimental Interfaces for Music-Evoked Emotion
summary: This paper proposes using humanoid musical robots as experimental interfaces to study music-evoked emotion and human-robot interaction, expanding their typical use beyond performance.

title: Koala Gripper: Co-designing Robotic Grippers and Data-Capture Devices for Scaling Dexterous Manipulation Learning
summary: This research presents the Koala Gripper, a co-designed robotic gripper and data-capture device aimed at scaling dexterous manipulation learning by improving data collection ergonomics.

title: Logic-VLA: A Temporal Logic Conditioned Vision-Language-Action Model
summary: This paper introduces Logic-VLA, a Vision-Language-Action model conditioned on Signal Temporal Logic, to precisely specify safety-critical and spatiotemporal requirements for robot behavior.

title: Rethinking Demonstration Unlearning in Imitation Learning for Robotics
summary: This work explores methods for demonstration unlearning in imitation learning for robotics, aiming to efficiently edit trained policies to remove specific human demonstrations without costly retraining.

title: Natural Sit-to-Stand Motion Synthesis For Humanoids via Guided Assistance Curricula and Staged Rewards
summary: This paper describes a method for synthesizing natural sit-to-stand motion for humanoids using reinforcement learning, guided by assistance curricula and staged rewards without demonstrations.

title: Demonstration-Guided Humanoid Stand-Up on an Emulated Deformable Surface
summary: This paper presents a reference-guided reinforcement learning framework enabling a Unitree G1 humanoid to perform stand-up motions on deformable ground, using demonstrations recorded on hard surfaces.

title: Neural-Primitive: An Efficient End-to-end Local Planner with Primitive-based Imitation Learning for Autonomous Flight
summary: This paper proposes Neural-Primitive, an efficient end-to-end local planner using primitive-based imitation learning for autonomous flight in cluttered environments, addressing computational challenges.

title: Hybrid Roller-Jamming Gripper for Object Acquisition and Retention Under Pose Uncertainty
summary: This paper introduces a hybrid roller-jamming gripper designed for robust object acquisition and retention in household manipulation, addressing challenges of pose uncertainty during initial contact.

title: PhysCaP: Grounding Code-as-Policy Agent with Physics-Informed Exploration
summary: This paper introduces PhysCaP, a Physics-Informed Code-as-Policy agent for active perception in robotic manipulation that infers latent physical properties critical for tasks.

title: Roadside-Cooperative Autonomous Driving: From Data Platform to Vision-Language End-to-End Reasoning
summary: This research explores roadside-cooperative autonomous driving, focusing on V2X data platforms and vision-language end-to-end reasoning to enhance perception beyond line-of-sight.

title: TaPeR: Probabilistic Recovery of Sparse Task Precedence Graphs from a Handful of Demonstrations
summary: This paper introduces TaPeR, a method for probabilistically recovering sparse task precedence graphs from a few demonstrations, enabling robots to flexibly reorder and perform long-horizon manipulation tasks.

title: Teaching is a Process: The TOSS Framework for Modeling Human Teaching Decisions in Human-Interactive Robot Learning
summary: This work presents the TOSS Framework for modeling human teaching decisions in human-interactive robot learning, aiming to understand the underlying logic humans use when instructing robots.

title: SRL-MPC: Shape-Aware Reinforcement Learned Model Predictive Control
summary: This paper introduces SRL-MPC, a shape-aware reinforcement learned model predictive control method for safe and efficient navigation of robot fleets and in heterogeneous crowds.

title: Beyond Imitation: Self-Improving Robot Policies via Off-Policy Q-Planning
summary: This paper explores methods for robots to self-improve their policies in manipulation tasks through off-policy Q-planning, moving beyond the limitations of behavior cloning.

title: The Coastline as a Structural Constraint: Harnessing Scene Geometry for Autonomous Surface Vessel Localization
summary: This work presents two localization frameworks that exploit coastline and water-surface geometry for GPS-denied autonomous surface vessels, using scene geometry as a structural constraint.

title: VT-MUSE: Multimodal Unified Sequential Visuotactile Representation Learning for Manipulation
summary: This paper proposes VT-MUSE, a novel multimodal representation learning framework that unifies visual and tactile data for robotic manipulation tasks, focusing on capturing fine-grained cross-modal dependencies.

title: NeSAM: Neuro-Symbolic Kinodynamics with Soil Adaptation for Off-Road Mobility
summary: This research introduces NeSAM, a neuro-symbolic kinodynamic model with soil adaptation to accurately predict off-road vehicle motion over deformable terrain by explicitly representing soil conditions.

title: ViTacPhys: Physical Property-Aware Grasping from Human Visual-Tactile Demonstrations
summary: This research presents ViTacPhys, a visual-tactile framework and data acquisition system that estimates object mass and friction from human demonstrations to enable physical property-aware grasping for robots.

title: Mining beyond Earth with Space Robots: Exploration, Sampling, and Extraction
summary: This article discusses the critical role of space robots in exploration, sampling, and extraction for lunar and Martian resource acquisition and utilization, enabling sustained human exploration and commercial opportunities.

title: Learning-Based Measurement-Robust Control Barrier Functions for Obstacle Avoidance under State Estimation Error
summary: This paper develops learning-based measurement-robust control barrier functions to provide safety filters for critical systems, addressing obstacle avoidance challenges under state estimation errors.

title: Pneumatic Units for Logic-based Sequential Excitation (PULSE) in Wearable Haptic Devices
summary: This research introduces Pneumatic Units for Logic-based Sequential Excitation (PULSE), a novel pneumatic actuation method for creating lightweight and compliant wearable haptic devices that deliver complex feedback.

title: GhostTac: Manipulating Tactile Sensors without Physical Contact
summary: This paper presents GhostTac, the first contactless attack method for tactile sensors, demonstrating how they can be manipulated without physical contact to compromise robotic system perception.

title: Just Noticeable Difference Modeling for Token Compression in Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This research proposes Just Noticeable Difference Modeling for token compression, a technique to reduce inference costs in large Vision-Language-Action models and embodied agents while preserving perceptual quality.

title: Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks: Encoding Anatomic Priors in Loss and Architecture, with an SE(3) Formulation of Guidewire-Induced Aortoiliac Deformation
summary: This paper introduces Anatomy-Informed Neural Networks (AINN), a method that encodes anatomic priors into the loss function and architecture of deep learning models to ensure anatomical plausibility and improve generalization.

title: Update-Free On-Policy Steering via Verifiers
summary: This research proposes UF-OPS (Update-Free On-Policy Steering), a new method that uses verifiers to improve the precision and reduce the brittleness of behavior cloning policies for robotic manipulation tasks.

title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for Closed-loop Guidance of Fish Schools via Virtual Agents
summary: This study proposes a deep reinforcement learning framework that utilizes virtual agents for the closed-loop guidance of fish schools, aiming to understand and control collective biological motion.

title: Can you see how I learn? Human observers' inferences about Reinforcement Learning agents' learning processes
summary: This study investigates human observers' inferences about the learning processes of Reinforcement Learning agents, exploring how humans perceive and interpret AI's learning behavior, which impacts feedback and trust.

title: KVBoost: Chunk-Level Key-Value Cache Reuse with Deviation-Guided Recomputation for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
summary: A new method called KVBoost is proposed to optimize large language model inference by enabling chunk-level key-value cache reuse and deviation-guided recomputation.

title: AIREP: A Protocol for Per-Decision Evidence in AI Runtime Governance
summary: AIREP, a new protocol, is presented for recording governance decisions of automated AI runtimes to provide per-decision evidence for accountability and compliance.

title: Reviewing Model Collapse and Countermeasures
summary: This report reviews the phenomenon of model collapse in generative AI, which occurs when using AI-synthesized data for training, and discusses potential countermeasures.

title: AI Learning and Conceptual Transfer in the Game of Hidden Rules
summary: This report summarizes research on AI learning and conceptual transfer within the Game of Hidden Rules, focusing on reinforcement learning agents and transfer learning.

title: LitReview Arena: Evaluating Literature Review Agents with Battle-Style Peer Review Platform
summary: LitReview Arena is introduced as a battle-style peer review platform designed for rigorously evaluating the performance of automatically generated literature review agents.

title: SchemaRouter: Field-Aware Tool Routing for Efficient Heterogeneous Agentic RAG
summary: SchemaRouter is presented as a method for field-aware tool routing to enhance the efficiency of heterogeneous agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems.

title: RIACT: A Responsible AI System for Personalized Study Habit Tracking and Early Burnout Signal Detection in University Students
summary: Student burnout is highly prevalent in higher education, with reported rates ranging from 12% to over 70% and consistently exceeding those of the working population - yet it is typically identified only retrospectively, after academic decline has already occurred. A contributing factor is that students have little structured visibility into their own study behaviour, and existing productivity tools record activity without interpreting it. This paper presents RIACT (Record, Insight, Analyze, Coach, Track), a web-based application that combines structured study session logging with a hybrid AI architecture to surface personalized insights and early burnout signals. Students log sessions by location and time; the system computes net focus time by accounting for breaks, detects burnout signals through transparent, deterministic rules operating on week-over-week behavioural comparisons, and uses a large language model - constrained to a fixed output schema - to contextualize patterns and generate personalized recommendations. The design embeds responsible AI principles throughout: warnings are governed by auditable rules rather than model judgement, all output is framed as an observation rather than a diagnosis and data collection is limited to self-logged behavioural fields. We describe the system's design rationale, situate it within the literature on student burnout and explainable AI in education and propose an evaluation framework for validating its behavioural signals against established burnout instruments.

title: There Is No Neutral Harness: Modern LLM Leaderboards Are Manufactured by Config-Fragile Items
summary: This paper discusses how LLM leaderboards and multiple-choice benchmarks are influenced by the 'harness' configuration, including prompt wording and option order, affecting evaluation results. It highlights the sensitivity of benchmark outcomes to these methodological choices.

title: Spyre-Accelerated Retrieval-Augmented Generation on IBM LinuxONE: A Cloud-Native Architecture for Secure, High-Throughput Enterprise AI Inference
summary: This describes a cloud-native architecture for secure, high-throughput enterprise AI inference using Spyre-accelerated Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) on IBM LinuxONE. It addresses challenges of data movement, latency, and security for deploying large language models with internal data.

title: Hate Speech Classification In Roman Urdu: A Comparative Study On Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning And Prompt Engineering
summary: This comparative study investigates parameter-efficient fine-tuning and prompt engineering techniques for hate speech classification in Roman Urdu, a low-resource language. The research addresses the growing issue of toxic content on social media and its societal impact.

title: Retrieval-grounded robot program generation and simulation-based correction via Model Context Protocol
summary: This paper introduces a language-model-based workflow for generating, validating, and correcting ABB RAPID robot programs from natural language descriptions, utilizing retrieval-augmented and simulation-based correction via the Model Context Protocol. The system aims to enable rapid reprogramming for flexible manufacturing.

title: Evaluating Multimodal Narrative Understanding of Popular Hollywood Films
summary: This article discusses the evaluation of multimodal language models for understanding narratives in Hollywood films and the challenges involved in creating stable benchmarks for this task due to complexities like copyright.

title: Agentic AI for Safety-critical Multi-drone Systems: Challenges and Opportunities
summary: This paper examines the challenges and opportunities of applying agentic AI to safety-critical multi-drone systems used in missions like search and rescue or infrastructure monitoring. It discusses obstacles to real-world adoption, including integrating agentic behavior.

title: Software Frameworks for Explainable AI in Time Series Classification: A Systematic Review
summary: This systematic review explores software frameworks designed for Explainable AI (XAI) in the context of Time Series Classification (TSC). It focuses on ensuring the transparency and trustworthiness of machine learning models used in decision-critical settings.

title: Enhanced Artificial Neural Networks Using QHAdamW in Air Quality Forecasting
summary: This study enhances Artificial Neural Networks for air quality forecasting by integrating the modified QHAdamW optimizer (Quasi-Hyperbolic Momentum and Adam with decoupled weight decay). The improved model is applied to the Philippines, where it is currently the sole AQI forecasting model.

title: Let Credit Follow Computation: Architecture-Aware Credit Transport for Large Language Model Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper proposes an architecture-aware credit transport mechanism for large language model reinforcement learning, focusing on how credit assignment can be structured. It dissects credit assignment into evidence of success, a transport operator, and an update geometry for policy changes.

title: Quantifying geographic domain shift to decouple the geospatial transferability of human mobility flow generation models
summary: This research quantifies geographic domain shift to understand the geospatial transferability of human mobility flow generation models. It investigates how well these models perform in new or unseen geographic regions, which is crucial for urban systems analysis.

title: A Reproducible, License-Aware Distillation Recipe for CPUDeployable Safety Classification
summary: This paper presents a reproducible and license-aware distillation recipe for creating CPU-deployable safety classification layers for large language models. The goal is to enable efficient deployment of guard models on commodity hardware, addressing the limitations of existing GPU-centric models.

title: Robust Lightweight Deep Learning Models for Oral Cancer Screening
summary: This research focuses on developing robust and lightweight deep learning models for oral cancer screening, particularly for resource-constrained settings and smartphone-based point-of-care solutions. The goal is to address delayed diagnoses in low-to-middle-income countries due to specialist shortages.

title: Data-Driven Dynamic Algorithm Dispatch with Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces an LLM-driven approach for generating dynamic algorithmic dispatch heuristics in high-performance linear algebra. It combines prompt engineering with LLaMA 3 and a curated performance database to synthesize selection heuristics that optimize algorithmic performance.

title: K-Bench: measuring model performance on real scientific agent requests
summary: This paper introduces K-Bench, a new benchmark designed to measure the performance of scientific artificial intelligence models on real-world, underspecified scientific agent requests. It addresses the limitations of traditional benchmarks that often rely on structured questions or reference solutions.

title: Generate in the Chart, Not on the Boundary: Function-Symbol Grounding for Hard Constraints in LTN-GANs
summary: This research proposes a method for function-symbol grounding to implement hard constraints within Logic Tensor Network-Enhanced Generative Adversarial Networks (LTN-GANs). It aims to improve how LTN-GANs inject background knowledge and satisfy logical axioms.

title: Semantic Compression Trees: Multi-Resolution Knowledge Retrieval via Hierarchical Semantic Residuals
summary: This paper introduces Semantic Compression Trees (SCT), a novel hierarchical index for multi-resolution knowledge retrieval in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). SCTs aim to overcome the limitations of flat indexing by preserving the hierarchical structure of source documents for more effective retrieval.

title: SAEM: Stage-Aware Expert Management for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces SAEM (Stage-Aware Expert Management), a technique to improve memory-efficient inference in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models used for Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. It addresses the increased decoding latency and memory usage associated with CoT prompting.

title: Measuring Activation Control in Large Language Models
