summary: This research explores measuring activation control in large language models as a component of safe deployment, especially concerning potential model deception or scheming. It investigates how models might control their own activations, which could complicate latent-space monitoring.

title: From Mastery Profile to Simulated Response: Stochastic Student Knowledge Graphs (SSKG) for Faithful LLM Student Simulation
summary: This paper introduces Stochastic Student Knowledge Graphs (SSKG) to achieve faithful large language model (LLM) student simulation. The method aims to generate more realistic simulated responses based on mastery profiles for synthetic data generation and tutoring system stress-testing.

title: Context as an Environment: Programmatic Context Management for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: This research proposes 'Context as an Environment' for programmatic context management in long-horizon LLM agents. It addresses the challenge of agents performing long-running tasks that exceed typical context windows by introducing dynamic memory representations.

title: From Association to Causation: Improving Retrieval Precision of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Causal Relations and an Attention Mechanism
summary: This paper proposes a method to improve the precision of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by incorporating causal relations and an attention mechanism to address issues with standard dense-vector similarity retrieval.

title: ATHENA: Knowledge-guided agentic neural architecture search for AutoFormer-based electronic health record modeling
summary: ATHENA introduces a knowledge-guided agentic neural architecture search method to automate the design of AutoFormer-based transformer models for clinical prediction using electronic health records.

title: ECHO: A Cognitively Inspired, Auditable Memory Plane for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: ECHO is an auditable memory architecture and service prototype inspired by cognitive processes, designed to provide long-horizon AI agents with memory that can identify relevant experiences and track provenance.

title: What Does CLIP Learn for Regional Geolocalization? Probing Visual Cues and Scene Configuration After Adaptation
summary: This research probes how the CLIP model learns visual cues and scene configurations after adaptation for fine-grained regional geolocalization from street-view imagery.

title: Physics-Knowledge-Guided Hybrid Neural Learning for Arctic Sea Ice Concentration Evolution and Short-Range Prediction
summary: This paper presents a physics-knowledge-guided hybrid neural learning approach for modeling and short-range prediction of Arctic sea ice concentration evolution, essential for polar climate assessment.

title: HIRA: A Human-in-the-Loop Retrieval-Augmented Cascade for Document Classification in Regulated Industries
summary: HIRA is a training-free, on-premises retrieval-augmented cascade system with human-in-the-loop capabilities designed for document classification in regulated industries with strict data and governance constraints.

title: Hints, Critics, and Teachers: Prior Injection for Sparse-Reward RL in Vision-Language Math Reasoning
summary: This research investigates prior injection methods for sparse-reward reinforcement learning to improve vision-language math reasoning, addressing the challenge of limited correct rollouts.

title: VisAdj: Learning Adjacency Matrices from Node-Link Images
summary: VisAdj proposes a new method for learning adjacency matrices from node-link images, aiming to overcome limitations of existing KNN-based heuristics in capturing edge dependencies for graph information recovery.

title: Beyond Success and Failure: Length-Aware Contrastive Learning for GUI Agents
summary: This research explores length-aware contrastive learning to improve the training of Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents powered by Multimodal Large Language Models for automating digital tasks.

title: GameXpert-Bench: How Far Are Coding Agents from Expert Game Development?
summary: GameXpert-Bench evaluates the capabilities of coding agents powered by large language models in building complete games from natural language requests, assessing their current proficiency compared to expert game development.

title: LLM4LLM: Bridging Kernel Benchmarks and Real Deployment via Closed-Loop Agentic Optimization
summary: LLM4LLM introduces a closed-loop agentic optimization framework that uses large language models to bridge the gap between kernel benchmarks and real-world deployment behavior for low-level code optimization.

title: AI Watchdog: Agent Interfaces for Detecting and Defending Against Manipulative Dark Patterns in AI Conversations
summary: AI Watchdog is a browser-based agent interface designed to monitor live AI conversations and detect manipulative dark patterns, providing users with support to recognize and resist such tactics.

title: MemGuard: Persisting Verifier Signals for LLM-Agent Memory Governance
summary: MemGuard proposes a method for persisting verifier signals to improve the governance and reliability of reusable memory for LLM agents engaged in long task streams across various applications.

title: HiMA-MDD: A Hierarchical Multi-Agent Harness for Interpretable Multimodal Depression Detection in Clinical Interviews
summary: HiMA-MDD is a hierarchical multi-agent system designed for interpretable multimodal depression detection from clinical interviews by integrating dispersed evidence from various symptoms.

title: From Solver Feedback to Faithful Plans: Multi-Role Reinforcement Learning for Symbolic Planning
summary: This research explores multi-role reinforcement learning to enable faithful conversion of natural-language instructions into executable symbolic plans, addressing the brittleness of large language models in this domain.

title: Training Needs Trustworthy Worlds: Verified Synthetic Web Environments for Agent Learning
summary: This paper addresses the need for trustworthy and verified synthetic web environments to effectively train web agents, aiming to overcome limitations of current plausible but unreliable environments.

title: ESCRAG-R1: Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Emotional Support Conversation
summary: ESCRAG-R1 introduces a retrieval-augmented reinforcement learning approach for emotional support conversation systems, aiming to balance therapeutic competence with empathy by improving reasoning and expertise alignment.

title: GuardianBench: A Same-Scene Instruction-Contrastive Benchmark for Latent Contextual Risk in Embodied AI
summary: GuardianBench is a new same-scene, instruction-contrastive benchmark designed to evaluate latent contextual safety risks in embodied AI by varying instructions while keeping the visual scene fixed.

title: Multimodal Prompt Learning with Irregular EHRs for Robust Monitoring of Critical Care Patients
summary: This research investigates multimodal prompt learning with irregular electronic health records to enable robust monitoring and accurate assessment of critical care patients in intensive care units.

title: TessIndex: Capability Verified Identity System for the Agent Economy
summary: Introduces TessIndex, an identity system for the 'agent economy' where AI agents autonomously translate goals into tasks and orchestrate tools and services.

title: SSDi8: Accurate and Efficient 8-bit Quantization for State Space Duality
summary: Presents SSDi8, an 8-bit quantization method for Mamba-2's Structured State Space Duality architecture, aiming for accurate and efficient sequence modeling.

title: Repo2Skill-Evo: Repository Skills Go Stale in Silence
summary: Discusses Repo2Skill-Evo, focusing on how LLM agents operate over evolving software repositories by externalizing repository-specific procedural knowledge into reusable agent skills.

title: Closed-loop AI achieves certifiable engineering design
summary: Demonstrates how closed-loop agentic AI can automate and achieve certifiable designs for complex physical engineering, including satisfying simultaneous constraints.

title: Beyond Similarity: Heterogeneous Graph Learning for Multi-Objective Food Substitution in Charitable Food Agencies
summary: Explores heterogeneous graph learning for multi-objective food substitution in charitable food agencies, aiming to match household preferences, nutritional needs, and supply.

title: Redteaming Leading Arabic LLMs with ASAS
summary: Introduces the Arabic Safety Index (ASAS) for redteaming and adversarially evaluating leading Arabic Large Language Models to ensure their safety and cultural alignment.

title: DynaContext: Self-Improving Dynamic Contextualization of Optimized Prompts for Heterogeneous Parameter Extraction
summary: Proposes DynaContext, a self-improving method for dynamic contextualization of optimized prompts, allowing AI systems to adapt to varying contexts for heterogeneous parameter extraction.

title: SPAR-Hate: An Auditor-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Bilingual Hate Speech Parsing
summary: Presenta SPAR-Hate, un marco multi-agente guiado por auditores diseñado para el análisis estructurado y la detección de discurso de odio bilingüe.

title: One-Step Evolution for Long-Time Extrapolation: An Error-Bound-Informed and Prior-Guided Neural Residual Framework for Autonomous PDEs
summary: Proposes a neural residual framework for accurate long-time extrapolation in systems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs), integrating error bounds and prior guidance.

title: More Accurate or More Efficient? Evaluating Locally Deployed Compact Open-Weight Language Models for Mathematical Reasoning
summary: Evaluates the accuracy, efficiency, runtime, and energy consumption of compact open-weight language models deployed locally for mathematical reasoning tasks.

title: Distinguishing Revision and Delayed Elaboration in Incremental Narrative Interpretation
summary: Investigates how AI systems process narrative content incrementally, distinguishing between revision and delayed elaboration mechanisms. The research focuses on how internal representations are updated as input is received over time.

title: KSE-Web: An Analysis of Hybrid Retrieval and LLM-Assisted Query Expansion for Low-Resource Khmer Semantic Search
summary: Presents KSE-Web, an analysis of hybrid retrieval and LLM-assisted query expansion for low-resource Khmer semantic search. The study aims to address retrieval challenges in Khmer, including limited data and weak multilingual embedding support.

title: Wazobia Eval: A Benchmark for Nigerian Pidgin Emotion Understanding, Sarcasm Detection, and Cultural Reasoning
summary: Introduces Wazobia Eval, a new benchmark for evaluating language models on Nigerian Pidgin. It focuses on critical aspects like emotion understanding, sarcasm detection, and cultural reasoning, which are underrepresented in existing evaluations.

title: On the Role of Citations in Preference Data
summary: Examines the role of citations in NLP outputs and preference data, focusing on how humans and large language models evaluate them. The study highlights the importance of attribution for combating hallucination and verifying output credibility.

title: Agentic Scaffolding Amplifies Sycophantic Behavior in Large Language Models
summary: Investigates how agentic scaffolding amplifies sycophantic behavior in large language models, where models prioritize user agreement over truthful responses. The study examines this tendency beyond single-turn settings.

title: Beyond Two Bytes per Letter: Tokenization Overhead in Cyrillic AI Systems
summary: This research quantifies the tokenization overhead in modern multilingual AI systems for Cyrillic-script languages compared to English, highlighting disparities in cost and context capacity.

title: Mitigating Bias in Large Vision-Language Models via Counterfactual Ensemble Decoding
summary: This research proposes a counterfactual ensemble decoding method to mitigate social biases inherited from training data in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) when processing portraits.

title: Agentic Security: A Systematization of Tools, Failure Modes, and Design Laws for LLM-Driven Penetration Testing
summary: This paper systematizes the tools, failure modes, and design laws for LLM-driven penetration testing in "agentic security," evaluating operational failures encountered in deployed systems.

title: CyrillicQA: The Influence of Phonetically Encoded Secret Language on LLM Performance
summary: This research, using CyrillicQA, investigates the influence of phonetically encoded secret language on Large Language Model (LLM) performance, highlighting disparities due to training data selection.

title: Forgotten in Weights, Recovered by Tools: Agentic Tool Unlearning for LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces "agentic tool unlearning" for LLM agents, addressing the challenge of removing tool-related information from tool-augmented agents, an issue not covered by traditional unlearning methods.

title: Automating Multi-Hop RAG Evaluation via TRIAD: From Context Extraction to Validated Dataset Generation
summary: This research introduces TRIAD for automating multi-hop RAG evaluation by generating validated, domain-specific question-answer datasets to assess Retrieval-Augmented Generation system performance.

title: Evidence-State Reliability Under Controlled Degradation: Parser-Validity Divergence in a Multi-Stage LLM Pipeline
summary: This paper introduces and operationalizes Evidence-State Reliability (ESR), an evaluation layer for multi-stage LLM pipelines, to assess the reliability of intermediate evidence under degradation.

title: Can LLMs Truly Forget? Revealing Unlearning Gaps Through Adversarial Evaluation
summary: This research investigates whether LLMs truly forget by revealing unlearning gaps through adversarial evaluation, addressing the challenge of assessing the inaccessibility of removed training data.

title: Mitigating Database Leakage in RAG Systems with Keyword-Grounded Fact Substitution
summary: This paper proposes keyword-grounded fact substitution to mitigate database leakage in RAG systems, addressing their vulnerability to prompt injection attacks that expose sensitive external knowledge.

title: L\"etzCross: A Cross-Lingual Page-Level Benchmark for Multimodal Retrieval over Luxembourgish Documents
summary: This paper introduces L"etzCross, a new cross-lingual page-level benchmark for evaluating multimodal retrieval systems' performance on Luxembourgish PDF documents.

title: FCPRAG: Fusion-Controller Parametric Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Stable Multi-Passage LoRA Injection
summary: This paper introduces FCPRAG, a Fusion-Controller Parametric Retrieval-Augmented Generation method for stable multi-passage LoRA injection, addressing evidence-level fusion challenges in RAG systems.

title: Evaluation Awareness in Language Models: Representation, Verbalization, and Control
summary: This paper explores "evaluation awareness" in language models, questioning the reliability of capability and safety benchmarks if models alter their behavior when they infer they are being tested.

title: No One Model Catches Every Harm: Benchmarking Content Moderation Across Safety Scenarios
summary: This paper benchmarks content moderation across various safety scenarios for Large Language Models (LLMs), highlighting that no single model effectively catches every type of harmful content.

title: Lexical Coupling in GUI Element Grounding: Sentence Embeddings Track Labels across Mobile and Web
summary: This research shows that high instruction-element embedding similarity in GUI grounding evaluations is often confounded by lexical coupling from visible labels, questioning its interpretation as semantic grounding.

title: MCite-RL: Towards Reliable Multimodal RAG via Citation-enhanced Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces MCite-RL, a method for reliable Multimodal RAG using citation-enhanced agentic reinforcement learning to improve traceability and verifiability in MLLMs.

title: Do Large Language Models Perform Well on Comprehending Poetic Logic in Modern Chinese Poetry?
summary: This research investigates the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in comprehending poetic logic within modern Chinese poetry, an area largely unexplored despite their NLP advancements.

title: Training a Knowledge Base: Supervised Structure Learning for Agent-Curated Document Stores
summary: This paper proposes supervised structure learning for "agent-curated document stores," where a training agent actively curates and learns to manage a knowledge base for retrieval-augmented generation.

title: GUI-Primitives: Diagnosing Spatial Reasoning Failures in Vision-Language GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces GUI-Primitives, a 994-item benchmark designed to diagnose spatial reasoning failures in vision-language GUI grounding for computer-use agents. It aims to isolate how models bind relational language to correct interface elements.

title: PUMA: A Polish Benchmark for Culturally Grounded Multimodal Understanding
summary: Introduces PUMA, a Polish benchmark for evaluating large language models' culturally grounded multimodal understanding capabilities. It focuses on assessing multimodal data processing in the context of specific cultures and languages.

title: HiDiffTIR: Hierarchical Difficulty-Aware Policy Optimization for Multi-Turn Tool-Integrated Reasoning
summary: Presents HiDiffTIR, a hierarchical difficulty-aware policy optimization method for improving multi-turn tool-integrated reasoning in LLM agents. This approach enhances agents' ability to solve complex tasks by interacting with external tools iteratively.

title: The Chase Is the Curriculum, the Capture Anchors the Credit: Pursuit-Evasion Self-Play for Zero-Data LLM Reasoning
summary: Proposes Pursuit-Evasion Self-Play, a zero-data method for improving large language model reasoning by leveraging reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. This approach aims to reduce dependency on large human-curated task collections.

title: BanglaVeilGuard: Cross-Script Safety Benchmarking and Lightweight Guardrails for Bangla Large Language Models
summary: Introduces BanglaVeilGuard, a compact Bangla-first safety benchmark for cross-script safety evaluation of Bangla large language models. It addresses challenges in assessing LLM safety due to varied language use by Bangla speakers.

title: Modeling Claim Dependency Structure for Patent Litigation Prediction with Graph Attention Networks
summary: Presents a method for modeling claim dependency structure using Graph Attention Networks to improve patent litigation prediction. This research applies AI techniques to address the practical task of early risk identification in legal contexts.

title: EDGE: Experience-Distillation for Guided Exploration in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Proposes EDGE, an experience-distillation method for guided exploration in agentic reinforcement learning, to help LLM-based agents solve complex, long-horizon tasks. This approach aims to reuse exploration patterns embedded in interaction trajectories.

title: Bulbul: A Dataset for Dialectal Arabic Speech Recognition
summary: Introduces Bulbul, a new dataset specifically designed for dialectal Arabic speech recognition. This dataset aims to address challenges posed by diglossia and extensive regional dialect variation in Arabic ASR.

title: ToSCA: Leveraging Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning on Temporal and Strategic Abstractions of Conversational Agents
summary: Proposes ToSCA, a two-level hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for conversational agents, inspired by human temporal and strategic abstractions. This framework aims to improve the capabilities of conversational agents.

title: Machine learning and digital pragmatics: Which word category influences emoji use most?
summary: This study uses the MARBERT model to examine which word categories most influence emoji use in Colloquial Arabic posts on X, within a digital pragmatics approach. It analyzes a corpus of 15,856 posts containing emojis.

title: Align, Unify, Suppress, Route: A Coherentist View of Transformer Computation
summary: Introduces Coherentist Probabilistic Compositionalism (CPC), an interpretive framework for understanding transformer computation. This framework aims to provide a shared vocabulary for mechanistic interpretability of transformer circuits.

title: Real-TurnTurk: A Multimodal Turkish Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction
summary: Introduces Real-TurnTurk, a multimodal Turkish corpus designed for turn-taking prediction in natural, synchronous dialog systems. This dataset aims to address the lack of naturalistic conversational data for this research area.

title: Semantic Reasoning Denoising: Correcting Language Model Reasoning with Semantic Operators
summary: Presents a method called Semantic Reasoning Denoising, which uses semantic operators to correct reasoning errors in large language models. This approach aims to prevent the propagation of local semantic errors to incorrect conclusions.

title: RAG Collapse: LLM Responses Collapse When Retrieved Documents Are Self-Authored
summary: This research identifies "RAG Collapse," a phenomenon where large language model (LLM) responses degrade when retrieved documents are self-authored by AI. It highlights a potential self-reinforcing feedback loop affecting RAG systems.

title: LLM assisted writing deserves empirical evaluation
summary: This paper argues for empirical evaluation of LLM-assisted writing, presenting an analysis of health informatics papers that links it to focused presentation, broader citation practices, and globally distributed authorship. It discusses questions of clarity, integrity, and equity.

title: SSE-Bio: A Structured Self-Evolving Agent with Agentic Retrieval Policy for Multi-Hop Biomedical Reasoning
summary: Presents SSE-Bio, a structured self-evolving agent with an agentic retrieval policy designed for multi-hop biomedical reasoning. This agent aims to improve evidence connection across intermediate entities in biomedical question answering.

title: Lexical Perturbations Disrupt LLM Reasoning: An Empirical Study of Attention Diversion
summary: An empirical study investigating how lexical perturbations disrupt large language model (LLM) reasoning and their robustness to realistic lexical corruption. It evaluates several LLMs across reasoning benchmarks under various types of lexical noise.

title: The Collaboration Tax: How Much LLM Multi-Agent Systems Pay to Coordinate
summary: This research investigates the "collaboration tax" in LLM multi-agent systems, quantifying the performance loss incurred when two LLMs must coordinate. It forms this as the team-decentralization loss in a cooperative game.

title: How Agents Represent Humans: Human-Directed Stereotypes in an Open Agent Social Network
summary: This study examines human-directed stereotypes formed by LLM-based agents in persistent social environments like Moltbook. It investigates how agents construct humans as a social category within these platforms.

title: Dual-Layer Agentic Memory with Fast Write Routing and Slow Consolidation
summary: Proposes a dual-layer agentic memory system with fast write routing and slow consolidation for large language model agents. This new approach aims to address retrieval degradation and increasing computational costs in dynamic environments.

title: Grounded Normative Rule Generation with Structured Search
summary: This paper presents a method for generating grounded normative rules that are both human-readable and operationally verifiable, focusing on structured output and evaluation beyond surface fluency.

title: Whitewashing Hate, Smearing Harmless Content: Annotator-Style Rebuttal Attacks on LLM-Based Moderation
summary: This research investigates vulnerabilities in LLM-based hate speech moderation, demonstrating how human feedback can be manipulated to either whitewash hateful content or falsely flag harmless content.

title: Improving Few-Step Language Flows with Untied Self-Conditioning
summary: This paper proposes a method called 'Untied Self-Conditioning' to improve the generation quality of flow-matching language models, particularly when generating with few sampling steps.

title: N\"urnberg NLP @ GermEval Shared Task 2026: Harmful Content Detection in German Social Media through Error-Independent LLM Voters
summary: This article describes a participation in the GermEval 2026 shared task, which evaluates methods for detecting harmful content in German social media, focusing on challenges like class imbalance.

title: Length-Adaptive Decoding for Masked Diffusion Machine Translation
summary: This research introduces 'Length-Adaptive Decoding' to improve masked diffusion language models for machine translation by accurately determining target length before denoising.

title: LLM Evaluation on Unseen Questions: Contextual Multidimensional IRT Model
summary: This paper presents a Contextual Multidimensional IRT Model for evaluating large language models, aiming to predict their performance on unseen questions and tasks.

title: Text-Anchored Semantic Perturbations for Transferable Jailbreak Attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This research explores text-anchored semantic perturbations to create transferable jailbreak attacks on Multimodal Large Language Models, exposing vulnerabilities in their safety alignment.

title: Semantics or Structure? Auditing Text Sensitivity in Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting
summary: This paper audits the sensitivity of text in Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting, investigating how natural language context contributes to predictive performance in various models.

title: Noise Floor Audit for Agent Benchmarks
summary: This audit examines the measurement variability for agent benchmarks, specifically focusing on native tool-calling endpoints across different providers and grading methodologies.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via Sequential Activation Patching
summary: This work investigates the mechanistic interpretability of Chain-of-Thought reasoning in Large Language Models using sequential activation patching to understand the causal effects of CoT.

title: Register Shifts Break LLM Safety: A Bengali Benchmark with Culturally Grounded Harms
summary: This paper introduces BanglaSafe, a benchmark for evaluating LLM safety in Bengali, featuring culturally grounded harm categories to address safety beyond English-centric evaluations.

title: When Not to Imitate: Boundary-Aware Skill Memory for Reliable Tool-Use LLM Agents
summary: This research proposes 'Boundary-Aware Skill Memory' for LLM agents to improve reliable tool-use by guiding when to generalize and when to avoid imitating past successes.

title: Context-Aware Cluster Decoding: Semantic Anchor-Driven Coherence in dMLLMs
summary: This paper introduces 'Context-Aware Cluster Decoding' to enhance coherence in diffusion multimodal large language models, addressing semantic drift and repetition in long-form outputs.

title: Can Large Language Models "Hyper-Thread"?
summary: This research investigates whether Large Language Models can execute multiple tasks concurrently during token generation, exploring the mechanism of broader attention allocation.

title: EditStream: A Unified Autoregressive Framework for Interactive Video Generation and Editing
summary: This report introduces 'EditStream', a unified autoregressive framework for interactive video generation and editing, built upon a DiT-based model architecture.

title: Aligning Human Sense: Calibrated Distributional Reward Learning for Video Generation
summary: This paper addresses challenges in video generation by proposing 'Calibrated Distributional Reward Learning' to better align generated videos with human preferences through improved reward signals.

title: AI Visual Inspection for Garment Production
summary: This paper explores the application of AI visual inspection for quality control in the garment manufacturing industry, aiming to detect defects like broken stitches and skipped stitches.

title: Few-Shot Cross-Dataset Adaptation for Tuberculosis Detection Using DenseNet
summary: This research investigates Few-Shot Cross-Dataset Adaptation using DenseNet for tuberculosis detection from chest X-rays, addressing challenges posed by severe domain shifts between datasets.

title: Boosting Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering with Structured Context Reasoning
summary: This research proposes boosting Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering by integrating external knowledge and using Structured Context Reasoning with Large Language Models.

title: DesignAgent3D: Interactive 3D Scene Editing via Designer-like Multimodal Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces DesignAgent3D, an interactive system for 3D scene editing that utilizes designer-like multimodal reasoning to interpret and ground natural language requests in complex 3D environments.

title: WorldMind: Decoupled Game World Model for State-Aware NPC Behavior
summary: This item introduces WorldMind, a game world model designed to generate visually coherent gameplay videos and state-aware non-player character (NPC) behavior.

title: Text-Guided Visual Dependency Graph Learning with Cross-Modal Attention Priors
summary: This item proposes CM-GLasso (Cross-Modal Graphical Lasso), a framework that integrates vision-language representation learning with sparse Gaussian Graphical Models for text-guided visual dependency graph learning.

title: ViTexSZ: Heterogeneous Vision-Text Knowledge Distillation for EEG Seizure Detection
summary: This item proposes ViTexSZ, a method using heterogeneous vision-text knowledge distillation for automated electroencephalography (EEG) seizure detection, improving neurological monitoring.

title: BIMScript: Material-Aware Structured Scene Programs for BIM Ingestion
summary: This item investigates structured-language models like SceneScript for their application in reconstructing scenes as parametric commands for automated Building Information Modeling (BIM) ingestion.

title: Beyond Visual Similarity: Entity-Aligned Retrieval for Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
summary: This item describes a method for entity-aligned retrieval, focusing on enhancing Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering (KB-VQA) by prioritizing entity-level semantic similarity over surface-level visual similarity in external information retrieval.

title: Multi-Scale Fruit Capsules: Dilated Convolutions and Dynamic Routing for In-the-Wild Explainable Fruit Recognition
summary: This item introduces Multi-Scale Fruit Capsules, a method using dilated convolutions and dynamic routing for explainable and accurate automated fruit recognition in diverse real-world conditions.

title: CLSC DETR: Reliable Candidate Ranking via Cross Layer Geometric Support for UAV Small Object Detection
summary: This item proposes CLSC DETR, a method enhancing UAV small object detection through reliable candidate ranking via cross-layer geometric support in complex aerial scenes.

title: FigmaTrace: Capturing Creative Nuances in Human Figma Design Workflows
summary: This item introduces FigmaTrace, a method for capturing the creative nuances of human Figma design workflows to improve the performance of Vision Language Models on subjective design tasks.

title: Complexity Induction: Compositional Generalization via Structured Label Distortion
summary: This item demonstrates 'complexity induction,' a method of structured distortion of training data, to achieve compositional generalization in standard CNN classifiers without architectural changes.

title: EXPL-FR: Explaining Face Recognition Models via Vision-Language Alignment
summary: This item introduces EXPL-FR, a method to explain deep face recognition models by aligning a vision-language model's image embeddings to reveal semantic attributes relied upon for similarity scores.

title: TASSO: TAsk-Specific Subspace Optimization for Continual Learning of Vision-Language Models
summary: This item proposes TASSO (TAsk-Specific Subspace Optimization), a method designed to address catastrophic forgetting and zero-shot degradation in Vision-Language Models during continual learning.

title: DamageScope: Vision-Language Retrieval at Scale for Disaster Damage Assessment from Satellite Imagery
summary: This item describes DamageScope, a system that utilizes vision-language retrieval at scale for timely and accurate disaster damage assessment from satellite imagery.

title: presto: Efficient, Training-free, and Open-world Object Placement via Imaginary Search
summary: This item proposes 'presto,' an efficient, training-free, and open-world method for object placement in image composition, achieved via imaginary search.

title: Extending the Horizon of Early Diagnosis: Lung Cancer Prediction with Vision Transformers
summary: This item presents a study evaluating Vision Transformers (ViTs) for the early prediction of lung cancer from chest X-rays, aiming to improve diagnostic accuracy.

title: Perturb the Thought, Not the Pixels: Latent-Space Rollout Diversification for Reinforcement Learning of Vision-Language Models
summary: This item explores Latent-Space Rollout Diversification, a new method for reinforcement learning of Vision-Language Models, aimed at improving reasoning ability by perturbing thought processes rather than pixels.

title: Semantic Slots for Video Object-Centric Learning
summary: This item investigates Semantic Slots for Video Object-Centric Learning, arguing that traditional decoders are a primary bottleneck by forcing slots to be spatially anchored.

title: SketchFlow: Zero-Shot Vector Sketch Generation via GMM Prior Flow in CLIP Latent Space
summary: This item proposes SketchFlow, a method for zero-shot vector sketch generation that utilizes GMM Prior Flow within the CLIP latent space to produce human-like drawing styles.

title: Emotion Intensity Matters: Generating Realistic Expressions in Virtual Humans with CVAEs
summary: This item presents a novel approach using Conditional Variational Autoencoders (CVAEs) to generate realistic and controllable expressive facial behaviors in virtual humans.

title: StereoDiffuer: Diffusion-based Progressive Geometry Modeling with Saliency Attention Perception for Stereo Matching
summary: This item proposes StereoDiffuer, a diffusion-based model for progressive geometry modeling with saliency attention perception, designed to improve fine-grained detail preservation in stereo matching.

title: The Plan, Not the Decoder: Diagnosing and Repairing Compositional Failure in Reasoning-Augmented Text-to-Image Generation
summary: This paper diagnoses compositional failures in reasoning-augmented text-to-image models like GoT-R1 by determining if the issue lies in the generated textual plan or the image decoder's ability to execute it.

title: Calibrate What You SHIP: Post-Selection Risk Control for Verifier-Guided Text-to-Image Generation
summary: This research addresses the calibration mismatch in verifier-guided text-to-image systems that use test-time search by proposing a method for post-selection risk control.

title: Fidelity-Diversity-Consistency (FDC): Data Pruning for Remote Sensing Change Detection
summary: This study explores data pruning for remote sensing change detection, benchmarking six methods and proposing Fidelity-Diversity-Consistency (FDC) to improve model performance.

title: Learning to Look Again: Loss-Gap Supervision for Free-form Crop Routing in Vision-Language Models
summary: This research introduces Loss-Gap Supervision for free-form crop routing in Vision-Language Models to improve their ability to answer detail-centric questions by preventing loss of visual information.

title: LiteEvent-AE: Lightweight Autoencoder for Event-Based Vision on Low-Latency Energy-Constrained Edge Devices
summary: This paper introduces LiteEvent-AE, a lightweight autoencoder designed for event-based vision, enabling energy-efficient and low-latency AI processing on constrained edge devices.

title: DefaultShift: Auditing Semantic Default Shift in Accelerated Text-to-Image Models
summary: This research introduces DefaultShift to audit and characterize how accelerated text-to-image models can silently alter semantic distributions over unspecified attributes.

title: HP-UniIF: Hierarchical Prompt Learning for Unified Image Fusion
summary: This paper proposes HP-UniIF, a hierarchical prompt learning approach for unified image fusion, aiming to support diverse tasks like heterogeneous fusion and degradation restoration within a single system.

title: SAFE-G: Structure-aware Faithful Evidence-guided Generation for Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces SAFE-G, a structure-aware, faithful evidence-guided generation method to improve Knowledge-based Visual Question Answering by effectively retrieving and leveraging external knowledge.

title: Through the Schr\"odinger Bridge: Benchmarking Antemortem Image Restoration from Postmortem Autolysis to Enhance Forensic Diagnostics
summary: This research benchmarks image restoration techniques to enhance forensic diagnostics by reversing the effects of postmortem autolysis on tissue morphology.

title: PatchGate: Narrowing the Verbalization Gap with Intrinsic Object Inventories in Frozen Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces PatchGate, a method to improve image captioning in frozen Vision-Language Models by using intrinsic object inventories to generate precise and complete descriptions.

title: Towards Alias-Free 4D Gaussian Representations with Motion-Aware Filtering
summary: This research proposes motion-aware filtering to create alias-free 4D Gaussian representations, improving novel-view synthesis of dynamic scenes for AR/VR applications.

title: Towards Bitstream-corrupted Harsh Visual Understanding: Through Bitstream Language Modeling as Robust Semantic Priors
summary: This paper addresses Bitstream-corrupted Harsh Visual Understanding by proposing bitstream language modeling as robust semantic priors to interpret harshly degraded videos.

title: FIRM-Video: Check Before You Score for Reliable Text-to-Video Reward Modeling
summary: This research introduces FIRM-Video to enhance the reliability of reward models for text-to-video evaluation and alignment by addressing challenges in training supervision quality.

title: BC-IHV: Conditioning the Color Space for Stable Rectified-Flow Low-Light Enhancement
summary: This paper introduces BC-IHV, a method for conditioning the color space for stable rectified-flow low-light image enhancement, aiming to correct exposure without altering image geometry or chromatic content.

title: GaussVid: Sparse-View Gaussian Splatting with 3D-Aware Video Diffusion Priors
summary: This research introduces GaussVid, which combines sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting with 3D-aware video diffusion priors to improve novel view synthesis from limited input.

title: GuardPaint:SpeculativeSafetyDecodingforText-to-ImageGeneration
summary: This paper introduces GuardPaint, a speculative safety decoding method for text-to-image diffusion models to prevent the generation of policy-violating content from adversarial prompts.

title: ViSMoE: Visual-Aware Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Embodied Referring Expression Grounding
summary: This paper proposes ViSMoE, a Visual-Aware Sparse Mixture-of-Experts model, to improve Embodied Referring Expression Grounding, enabling an agent to navigate environments and localize objects based on natural language.

title: VIG: Visual Information Gain as a Reward Signal for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
summary: This research introduces Visual Information Gain (VIG) as a reward signal to compress Chain-of-Thought traces in multimodal large reasoning models, aiming to reduce inference cost.

title: Pixel-Space Diffusion via Observation Operators
summary: This paper explores optimizing pixel-space diffusion models by introducing observation operators to address challenges in their optimization, particularly regarding target reparameterization and denoising.

title: A Scalable Vector Graphics Latent Space
summary: This paper proposes a continuous, dense, and invertible latent space for Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG), providing a fundamental building block for deep learning models to generate and manipulate vector representations.

title: Entity-Constrained CBCT Retrieval for Low-Resource Dental Record Completion
summary: This research explores using entity-constrained retrieval for completing dental records from limited cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) data. It addresses the challenge of scarce annotation and varied evidence types for individual clinical fields.

title: AirAlign: Geometry-Aware Relative Pose Alignment for UAV Last-Meter Navigation
summary: This paper presents AirAlign, a geometry-aware approach for precise relative pose alignment in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) navigation during the critical 'last-meter' approach stage. It aims to improve target acquisition and manipulation despite viewpoint and appearance variations.

title: Sparse Multi-Stage Expert-Agent Routing for Complex Clinical Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes a sparse multi-stage expert-agent routing system for complex clinical reasoning. The system allows models to dynamically update diagnostic hypotheses and coordinate medical specialities as new evidence emerges, contrasting with single-pass or fixed multi-agent systems.

title: Trustworthy Visual Quality Inspection under Data Scarcity in Manufacturing
summary: This research focuses on developing trustworthy visual quality inspection systems for manufacturing under conditions of data scarcity. The goal is to automate routine inspections while ensuring reliability and reserving human expertise for ambiguous cases.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Visual Prompting: Guiding Foundation Models in Two-Photon Imaging
summary: This work introduces Retrieval-Augmented Visual Prompting to guide foundation models in challenging two-photon calcium imaging settings. It leverages retrieval to adapt models to varied image appearances and scarce annotations without fine-tuning weights.

title: Improved denoising diffusion probabilistic models with efficient non-diagonal covariance modeling
summary: This paper describes an improvement to denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) through efficient non-diagonal covariance modeling. The enhancement accelerates the sampling process, allowing for acceptable quality samples in fewer steps.

title: RoboShape: Information-Theoretic Point Cloud Representations for Privacy-Aware Robot Perception
summary: RoboShape investigates information-theoretic point cloud representations for privacy-aware robot perception in human environments. It addresses how 3D representations collected by robotic agents can reveal sensitive spatial context beyond just objects.

title: Multimodal-Language-Model-Driven Interaction and Companionship for Service Robots in Elderly-Care Facilities
summary: This paper explores multimodal-language-model-driven interaction and companionship for service robots in elderly-care facilities. The aim is to integrate capabilities for continuous companionship, natural interaction, and safety to support daily care.

title: On the Optimized Use of Non-Orthonormality Constraints for the Quasi-Static INS Alignment of Autonomous Underwater and Surface Vehicles
summary: This research optimizes the use of non-orthonormality constraints for the quasi-static initial alignment of inertial navigation systems (INS) in autonomous underwater and surface vehicles. Precise initial attitude determination is crucial for these systems.

title: ODG-NoMaD: Overhead-Camera Direction-Guided NoMaD
summary: ODG-NoMaD describes an overhead-camera direction-guided extension to the NoMaD learned vision-navigation policy. It enhances navigation and exploration for autonomous agents in unseen environments where traditional goal information is unavailable.

title: Mamba-based Selective State Space Modeling Improves the Accuracy-Complexity Tradeoff of SmolVLA Vision-Language-Action Experts
summary: This paper introduces Mamba-based Selective State Space Modeling to improve the accuracy-complexity tradeoff of SmolVLA Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. The technique aims to enable efficient robot control by reducing computational overheads associated with policy calls.

title: Position: Robot Privacy as Embodied Boundary Work. Connecting Capabilities, Contexts, and Design Responses in Everyday Robotics
summary: This position paper examines robot privacy as embodied boundary work, connecting capabilities, contexts, and design responses for everyday robotics. It discusses how robots' physical presence can reshape spatial, social, and relational boundaries, challenging traditional privacy frameworks.

title: RiskWorld: Object-Centric Latent World Modeling for Autonomous Driving Risk Identification
summary: RiskWorld introduces object-centric latent world modeling for identifying risks in autonomous driving scenarios. The approach focuses on predicting which observed objects are likely to become safety-critical to the ego vehicle.

title: Operational digital twin clinics enable task-based evaluation of embodied AI
summary: This work demonstrates how operational digital twin clinics can enable task-based evaluation of embodied AI. It shows that routine clinic images can be transformed into realistic, scalable environments for testing embodied AI systems.

title: Evaluating Human and LLM-Generated Thematic Analysis in HRI for Vulnerable Populations: A Comparative and Ethical Analysis
summary: This analysis evaluates human- and LLM-generated thematic analysis in Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) research, particularly for vulnerable populations. It raises critical ethical questions regarding the appropriateness of LLM-based interpretation in such sensitive contexts.

title: Geo-VLA: Geometry-Aware Vision-Language-Action Planning via Internalization of Map Semantics
summary: Geo-VLA presents Geometry-Aware Vision-Language-Action Planning via internalization of map semantics for autonomous driving. It aims to improve planning performance in complex environments by addressing the limitations of image-only representations.

title: Constructing Predictive Surgical Path for AI-based Capsulorhexis Skill Transfer
summary: This research focuses on constructing predictive surgical paths for AI-based capsulorhexis skill transfer to automate surgeon training. The goal is to leverage AI and surgical data to minimize training risks and expenses.

title: Model-Free Adaptive Parameter Tuning for Efficient Multi-Robot Warehouse Operations
summary: This paper proposes model-free adaptive parameter tuning for efficient multi-robot warehouse operations. The method addresses challenges in robotic fulfillment centers, particularly in optimizing 'digout' behavior for retrieving inventory from dense blocks.

title: GOLEM: Modular Humanoid Autonomy Towards Electric Vehicle Battery Disassembly
summary: GOLEM introduces a modular humanoid autonomy system for the disassembly of electric vehicle battery packs, using the Unitree H1-2 humanoid robot. This open-source architecture aims to automate dull and dangerous tasks currently performed by humans.

title: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Task Assignment Under Distribution Shifts
summary: This work explores model-based reinforcement learning for heterogeneous multi-robot task assignment under distribution shifts. It addresses how to efficiently assign tasks and construct schedules for diverse robot systems while adapting to changing demands.

title: Force/Torque-Based Kinematic Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation Tasks
summary: Contact-rich robotic manipulation requires an accurate model of the kinematic relationship between a robot's joints and the task features it senses. This relationship is rarely known exactly: it changes with each tool the robot picks up and shifts, sometimes almost instantaneously, as contact modes change --- especially for multi-fingered hands that make and break contact at points that are not exactly prescribed, as in full-hand grasping. This paper develops an adaptive scheme that estimates that relationship online, using only joint-angle sensing and a wrist-mounted force/torque sensor, with no exteroceptive measurement of the tool tip. We derive a provably stable kinematic update law that identifies the kinematics of an unknown tool from force/torque feedback alone, and prove stability of both the rigid case and the case with a compliance controller as an inner loop. We show that identification is confined to the directions the motion excites --- so that, for example, a tool's length is unobservable under a rigid insertion push, while a compliant loop's passive yielding partially excites it; and that with a second-order admittance the compliant certificate holds unconditionally in continuous time. We also pose the combined control and estimation problem as a Quadratic Program (QP): the formulation yields the prediction term of the update law exactly but, instructively, cannot reproduce the tracking adaptation term. We validate the scheme in simulation on a peg-in-hole insertion. This work is the first step in a research program aimed at factoring manipulation learning into a task policy which can be learned in isolation of the robot, for instance by reinforcement learning, and an adaptive kinematic component that adapts online to the particular robot, hand, or tool in use.

title: Why Personalization Matters: Cross-Subject Challenges in EMG-IMU-based HRI Activity Recognition
summary: This paper investigates wearable-based recognition of human activities and gestures to support Human-Robot Interaction (HRI) in object-handover and assembly-like scenarios. Electromyography (EMG) and Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) signals were collected using a Myo armband, culminating in a novel dataset introduced as MAGIC-HRI (Multimodal Activity, Gesture and Intention Collection) with a large taxonomy of 53 movement classes, including Brazilian Sign Language (LIBRAS) numbers (0-9), hand gestures, object/tool handover actions (pick up/give/hold), tool-manipulation tasks, and generic assembly/idle motions, collected from 11 participants with 10 samples per class (530 samples per participant). Signals are segmented by detecting muscle activation via an EMG energy envelope, then processed using sliding windows; time- and frequency-domain features are extracted. Multiple classical classifiers are tuned via cross-validated grid search, with Random Forest as the strongest baseline. A Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) protocol reveals a large generalization gap, indicating substantial subject dependence. A personalized adaptation experiment suggests that injecting a small number of samples from a new user can markedly improve recognition. Overall, the study contributes a broad, HRI-driven multimodal dataset, a rigorous evaluation emphasizing generalization, and practical evidence that personalization is likely required for robust deployment in practical HRI.

title: Lifelong Robot Recomposition via Persistent Categorical Modeling for Unified Task-Driven Co-Design, Verification, and Planning
summary: Robotic systems are traditionally designed and deployed in static configurations, with assumptions made at design-time becoming immutable constraints during runtime. This design-then-deploy paradigm produces performant systems under narrow operating conditions, but renders robots brittle when qualities of themselves, their tasks, or their environments unexpectedly change. We address this challenge with a compositional framework that formalizes robotic systems as abstract circuits within a strict symmetric monoidal category, in which design and runtime composition of hardware, software, and behavior are synthesized simultaneously via an SMT-based solver, with monoidal functors projecting the system into lifecycle-specific views and free symbolic variables simultaneously solving for parameters and entire component specifications within larger compositions. This persistent model also supports queries a long-lived system needs beyond plan existence across its entire lifecycle, including mapping Pareto fronts over candidate compositions, diagnosing why a composition has become infeasible, finding its minimal restoration, and reconfiguring with limited change to the deployed system. We evaluate against official implementations of optimal numeric, stream-based, and SMT-based planners all measured onboard a deployed robot and demonstrate the approach end-to-end in a search-and-rescue scenario in which the robot recognizes when it has become unfit and synthesizes and assumes new holistic configurations to restore operation. We release our solver and supporting software open-source.

title: CounterAlign: Counterfactual Supervision for Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are typically trained with behavior cloning (BC) on expert demonstrations. However, BC provides only positive supervision for expert actions, without explicit negative supervision indicating which actions are instruction-inconsistent or otherwise inappropriate. Reinforcement learning (RL) can provide such corrective signals, but often relies on externally specified rewards or curated non-expert data, both of which are costly to obtain in robotics. We show that offline RL for VLA models need not rely on curated non-expert trajectories: successful expert demonstrations alone can be transformed into dense corrective supervision through instruction relabeling. Specifically, by pairing expert actions with mismatched alternative instructions, we synthesize counterfactual instruction-observation-action tuples from the dataset and combine them with adversarial discriminator training to learn an instruction-grounded reward model for offline RL, without collecting additional rollouts or annotations. On the robustness-focused LIBERO-PRO benchmark, our method improves robustness to object position and task perturbations over a strong state-of-the-art baseline. It also outperforms competitive baselines in real-robot experiments on the TX-G2 (compatible with AGIBot G2). More broadly, our results suggest that, for data-constrained VLA learning, extracting denser supervision from each demonstration can complement collecting additional data.

title: Vision Guided Target Conditioned Control for Autonomous Excavation
summary: Autonomous excavation requires an intelligent control system that can convert spatial work intent into coordinated bucket motion under contact-rich soil interaction. This paper presents a target-conditioned intelligent control framework for autonomous excavation in a physics-based deformable-soil simulation workflow. An image-aligned target mask serves as a visual spatial command for the desired digging region, while a mask-conditioned Action Chunking Transformer maps multi-view RGB observations, proprioception, and the target mask to temporally extended joystick commands. To reduce target-ignoring behavior, demonstrations are organized with paired-condition supervision, where the same or closely matched scene is demonstrated with different target masks and corresponding action chunks. The framework is evaluated through both a diagnostic manipulation task and an excavation simulation benchmark with single-scoop and sequential pile-clearing protocols. In manipulation, target success is 4\% for no-condition ACT, 63\% for non-paired mask-conditioned ACT, and 96\% for paired-condition mask-conditioned ACT. In sequential pile clearing, paired-condition mask-conditioned ACT removes 76.8\% of the pile versus 27.4\% and 15.7\% for the two baselines, with 91.0\% human-normalized efficiency. The results show that visual target conditioning, paired demonstration structure, and action-chunk control form a practical cyber-physical simulation pipeline for excavator automation.

title: An Interpretable Deep Learning Framework for Material Perception and Classification from Multisensory Tactile Data
summary: Human tactile perception relies on complex multisensory cues. Yet the relationship between tactile signals and perceptual representations remains poorly understood, limiting the integration of touch in digital environments and human-like robotic perception. To address this gap, we developed a computational framework comprising three interconnected deep learning models that map multisensory touch data to material perception, without relying on hand-crafted features. The models represent progressively different routes from tactile signals to material class: from low-level interaction signals to perceptual attribute distributions (Model 1), from predicted attribute distributions to material classification (Model 2), and directly from tactile signals to material categories, bypassing intermediate representations (Model 3). By combining deep learning with Integrated Gradients, the framework achieved high accuracy while offering interpretability, revealing which sensory modalities most strongly drive its decisions. Our results show that deep learning can approach near-perfect material classification when unconstrained by intermediate perceptual stages, but matching human-like performance is harder once those stages are modeled explicitly. Notably, thermal cues emerged as particularly informative across all models, providing robust signals for material differentiation. The results offer a computational account of how tactile signals lead to material perception and show how interpretable deep learning can both approach human-level performance and reveal cues that robotic and haptic systems need to incorporate.

title: CIDER: Continual Interactive Distillation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning
summary: Human-in-the-loop real-world reinforcement learning enables rapid acquisition of effective robotic manipulation policies for individual tasks, often within tens of minutes. Yet it remains unclear how to extend this paradigm to continual learning, where a single policy must acquire new skills without losing previously learned behaviors. Existing real-world continual learning methods do not explicitly constrain prior behaviors, leading to severe catastrophic forgetting. We introduce Continual Interactive Distillation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning (CIDER), a continual reinforcement learning framework that freezes the accumulated historical policy as a teacher before learning each new task and interleaves task learning with distillation-based retention. We further introduce gradient routing to separate the gradients used for acquiring new tasks from those used for preserving prior behaviors. We evaluate our method with a single shared actor on six real-world household and industrial manipulation tasks. Interactive Distillation maintains high measured success on previously learned tasks across our six-task real-robot sequence while acquiring each new task in 10 to 20 minutes, whereas every baseline forgets at least one previous task. Additional ablations reveal the key design choices that govern the tradeoff between stability and plasticity in real-world continual reinforcement learning.

title: Stakeholder Insights for Designing In-Home Social Robots for Dementia Disorientation Detection and Caregiver-Aware Intervention
summary: Disorientation is a common and distressing experience for people living with dementia. It often manifests as confusion about time, place, or personal context. These episodes can increase anxiety, agitation, and safety risks, especially for persons with dementia (PwDs) who live independently at home. While assistive technologies have explored reminders, monitoring, and activity support, little research has explored how socially assistive robots can support the detection and management of disorientation in everyday living contexts. Hence, disorientation detection and intervention remain under-examined as socio-technical challenges. We conducted 14 semi-structured interviews with dementia caregivers and practitioners, including family and professional caregivers, occupational therapists, mental health practitioners, dementia nurse practitioners, and well-being and technology leads. The findings reveal that recurrent and fluctuating. It often emerges through behavioural cues such as repeated questioning, inappropriate activity timing and disrupted daily routines. Caregivers described orientation as emotionally charged, and direct correction may increase distress. The participants were generally receptive to robotic assistance when framed as supportive rather than corrective. Based on the insights, we identify essential design implications for socially assistive robots that provide context-aware orientation support, integrate into daily routines and support caregivers through timely escalation.

title: DELTA: Deformable Elevation-Based Local Terrain Attention Encoder for Sparse-Terrain Quadrupedal Locomotion
summary: Stable quadrupedal locomotion on sparse terrain requires selecting state-relevant terrain evidence for precise foot placement. Model-based foothold planners provide precise foothold selection but rely heavily on explicit model assumptions. Recent attention-based map encoding (AME) studies show that end-to-end reinforcement learning (RL) can learn implicit foothold guidance. However, the computational cost of dense AME encoding grows with map resolution, limiting its scalability to fine-grained sparse terrain. We propose DELTA, a Deformable Elevation-Based Local Terrain Attention encoder. DELTA predicts state-conditioned sampling locations, forms terrain evidence tokens from adaptive local elevation patches, and attends only to a fixed-size token set. With fixed sampling and patch settings, DELTA's encoder cost is independent of map resolution. Experiments show that DELTA achieves final traversal performance comparable to AME at the standard resolution while improving learning efficiency. This fixed encoder cost enables the use of higher-resolution terrain maps, improving traversal on fine-grained sparse terrain. DELTA also demonstrates strong generalization to unseen mixed evaluation courses composed of continuous and discrete terrain elements. Beyond simulation, DELTA demonstrates successful sim-to-real transfer on RAIBO2. Analysis of the learned sampling offsets and attention weights shows that DELTA samples steppable regions and attends to terrain evidence relevant to future touchdowns without foothold labels or attention supervision.

title: Ludi${}_{\scriptscriptstyle 0.1}$: An Agentic System for Socially Intelligent Robots
summary: Robot foundation models have substantially advanced perception and control, but natural human-robot collaboration requires more than executing isolated commands. A robot must recognize ambiguity, maintain context across turns, communicate its intentions, and revise ongoing behavior as the user's intent changes. We present $\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ludi}_{\scriptscriptstyle 0.1}$, an agentic system for socially intelligent robots that integrates interactive speech, multimodal reasoning, memory, navigation, and learned manipulation. Its decision-making core is a fine-tuned vision-language model trained on multi-turn interaction traces spanning ambiguous requests, clarifications, corrections, interruptions, mixed social and task dialogue, and multi-step tasks. A purpose-built harness manages the model-tool interaction loop, while specialized navigation and manipulation policies execute physical skills. Ludi${}_{\scriptscriptstyle 0.1}$ demonstrates a practical path toward fluid human-robot collaboration today while producing the multimodal interaction traces needed to develop a more deeply integrated foundation model for robots and people.

title: Inferring Action from Future Latent State for Robotic Manipulation
summary: World-Action Models (WAMs) build robot control on video-generation backbones, which jointly predict dense future visual trajectories and robot actions. We argue that video generation is an unnecessary intermediate objective for world-action modeling. For robotic manipulation, the goal of a world model is not to reproduce how the world looks at every intermediate moment, but to predict the state that the world will reach after an action is executed. The intermediate frames only describe the visual transition between physical states, which consumes substantial model capacity and computation, but do not directly specify the physical outcome that the robot action is intended to produce. In this paper, we propose DELE-w0.5, which infers robot actions from predicted future states without relying on video generation. Concretely, DELE-w0.5 infers the action sequence from its corresponding compact future latent state. The future latent state captures the action-relevant physical outcome of robot interaction and serves as an explicit bridge between world modeling and action generation. The core design principle of DELE-w0.5 is to model how the physical world changes under robot actions, rather than how its visual appearance evolves frame by frame. This formulation removes the high-dimensional visual redundancy introduced by dense video representations, and it therefore enables cheaper training and low-latency inference. Across 480 real-robot trials on four long-horizon manipulation tasks, our DELE-w0.5 achieves the best performance among all compared policies, attaining 62.5 overall full-task success and 81.3 macro ordered-stage progress, outperforming the strongest baseline by 47.5 and 30.7 percentage points, respectively.

title: EndoNav: Semantic-to-Geometric Grounding for Language-Guided Robotic Endoscopic Examination
summary: Minimally invasive procedures performed within confined anatomical spaces depend on continuous endoscopic visualization. Current robotic endoscope systems can stabilize or reposition an endoscope, but they do not possess relevant context to provide effective visualization assistance. We present EndoNav, an anatomy-grounded natural-language framework that translates high-level surgeon commands into autonomous endoscopic visualization behaviors within patient-specific sinonasal anatomy. Spoken surgeon commands are transcribed and interpreted by an endoscopic viewpoint agent conditioned on a patient-specific anatomical scene representation. Rather than generating robot motion directly, the viewpoint agent generates structured visualization objectives that are converted into target viewpoints and inspection trajectories, which are then executed through geometry-constrained endoscope motion planning and joint-space control. We evaluate EndoNav using a structured three-pass sinus examination across three CT-derived anatomical models. For one cadaveric specimen, autonomous visualization is compared with sinus examinations performed by two resident surgeons. EndoNav achieved mean visualization IoUs of 87.04% and 84.37% relative to the two surgeon examinations, compared with an inter-surgeon IoU of 87.44%, while recovering 92.91% and 93.20% of surgeon-observed anatomical surfaces, respectively. These results demonstrate the feasibility of grounding high-level anatomical commands into patient-specific geometric objectives and translating them into anatomically constrained robotic visualization behaviors.

title: Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation in Construction via Zero-Shot Learning: A Diffusion Policy-Guided Adaptive Control
summary: Construction robotics and automation offer promising means of improving productivity, alleviating workforce shortages, and reducing workers' exposure to physically demanding tasks. However, reliable contact-rich robotic assembly remains challenging under tight tolerances, fabrication inaccuracies, and uncertain contact dynamics. To address this challenge, we present a framework coupling diffusion policies trained on simulation-generated pose and force/torque data with an L1-inspired adaptive controller that corrects policy-predicted actions online to compensate for unmodeled contact dynamics. We benchmark the framework against baselines in timber joinery, pipe fitting, and sequential full-scale truss assembly. It achieves 100% success on single-task assemblies and 90-100% success across sequential truss assembly subtasks, with lower, more stable contact forces than the baselines. By enabling zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for force-aware contact-rich assembly, the framework reduces costly, labor-intensive real-world data collection for policy training and advances scalable, robust automation of multistage assembly, motivating extension to broader contact-rich manipulation tasks in construction.

title: Meta-Ctrl: Guaranteed Plan Generation by Decoupling Syntactic and Semantic Constraints
summary: LLMs generate fluent plans for robots but routinely violate the syntactic and se8mantic constraints they must satisfy to execute, and existing remedies trade formal guarantees against plan quality: soft methods (affordance scoring, grounded decoding) give no guarantee, while symbolic planners (LLM+P) discard the LM's commonsense. We propose \textbf{Meta-Ctrl}, a constrained-decoding framework that guarantees the encoded constraints while preserving the base LM's plan quality. Meta-Ctrl introduces \emph{meta-tokens}---a compact vocabulary of grounded actions---enforcing syntax at the token level and semantics (preconditions, goals, ordering) at the action level, an exact factorization that cuts the memory of constrained decoding from over 107TB to under 2GB. With it, a small open-weight LM becomes competitive where it otherwise sits at the bottom of the leaderboard: on WAH-NL under the LoTa-Bench protocol it reaches the highest reported subgoal success rate, exceeding GPT-4's, with consistent gains across the Embodied Agent Interface. We further demonstrate it on a real tabletop robot, where every generated plan satisfies its preconditions and goals by construction. Project website: https://meta-ctrlg.github.io/.

title: DreamMimic: Learning Visuomotor Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation via World Model
summary: Vision-based whole-body loco-manipulation on humanoid robots is challenging due to partial observability, contact-rich dynamics, and the difficulty of learning long-horizon behaviors from high-dimensional visual inputs. We present \href{https://github.com/DreamMimic/DreamMimic}{DreamMimic}, a framework that distills privileged teacher policies into vision-based humanoid controllers via world-model-assisted distillation. Instead of using a Dreamer-style RSSM for planning, we repurpose it to learn predictive latent dynamics that serve as both a representation space and an action-conditioned multi-step supervision signal, while exposing compact predictive features to the student policy to reduce long-term drift. Beyond standard reconstruction objectives for proprioceptive and visual observations, we add auxiliary prediction heads for privileged state, contact, object state, and reward estimation. These heads provide additional supervision related to agent--object interaction and task progress, encouraging the latent representation to retain signals that are useful for contact-rich loco-manipulation. We further introduce Performance-Conditioned Guidance (PCG), a reward-driven adaptive distillation schedule that computes performance scores for both teacher and student to dynamically balance guidance and exploration. PCG prevents both premature teacher annealing and excessive teacher interference in challenging visual settings. Experiments on OMOMO and BEHAVE show improved tracking-based loco-manipulation performance over strong vision-based baselines, without exposing online privileged interaction states to the student at deployment. Qualitative simulations further examine morphology and simulator changes. These results suggest that world models can provide a useful mechanism for stabilizing visual policy distillation in contact-rich humanoid behaviors.

title: Beyond Instance Slots: Semantically Rich World Models for Physical Interaction Planning
summary: World models for physical interaction are typically trained to predict future observations or latent features; however, a planning-oriented model must answer a fundamentally different question: whether a candidate action produces a task-consistent future while preserving essential relations.Monolithic state representations obscure the underlying entities, while standard instance-level object slots merely identify \emph{what} is present without specifying \emph{what role} each entity plays in the task context. To bridge this gap, we present the Semantically Rich World Model (SR-WM), a task-conditioned world model structured around five functional roles: gripper, target, goal, relation, and phase.Within SR-WM, a visual entity encoder extracts soft entity hypotheses from pretrained patch features, allowing segmentation masks to serve as optional proposal priors without mandating them as required state representations or inference inputs.A role binder subsequently maps these hypotheses to task-specific roles, while an action-conditioned dynamics model predicts role transitions alongside fine-grained semantics, including grasp/contact, predicate establishment, relation preservation, fixture state, and phase change.Crucially, this unified role state grounds downstream multi-candidate action generation, stage-aware reranking, and violation-aware suffix resampling.Our comprehensive evaluation protocol spans all four LIBERO simulation suites, cross-suite transfer, perception diagnostics, and action-sensitivity analysis.Ultimately, this formulation transforms object-centric prediction into a semantic interface linking visual dynamics with planning-oriented decision making.

title: The Imitator Game: Benchmarking Robot Imitative Ability Beyond Action Prediction
summary: Humans imitate at the level of intent: given a demonstration, we infer its goal and carry it out with whatever tools, objects, and layouts are at hand. Current robot policies instead learn observation-to-action mappings from visual inputs and language instructions, without explicitly inferring the demonstrated task. Learning from human video thus remains largely trajectory-level: models can replay motions in near-identical scenes, but still struggle to imitate what the demonstrator intends rather than merely what they do. We introduce The Imitator Game, a four-level benchmark (L0-L3) that progressively widens the gap between the human demonstration and the robot's own scene, isolating where trajectory replay ceases to suffice and task understanding becomes necessary. We pair it with IG-10K, the largest environment-aligned paired human-robot dataset to date and the only one instantiated across all four levels in both real and simulated settings (20,000+ paired episodes, 50+ tasks, 6 domains), and Imitator Arena, an open platform for blind A/B human evaluation. Across nine state-of-the-art models, performance is stable from L0 to L2 but collapses at L3, identifying functional substitution - achieving the same intent through a different object affordance - as the decisive barrier to intent-level imitation. Human-video-conditioned models outperform caption-conditioned ones, yet every model falls below 13% zero-shot success on unseen tasks; fine-tuning IG-10K-pretrained models with only $10$ paired human-robot demonstrations yields large gains that grow with pretraining scale. The project website and access to Imitator Arena are available at https://imitator-game.github.io.

title: MotionDLO: Hybrid Event- and Frame-Based Tracking of Deformable Linear Objects
summary: Reliably tracking moving deformable linear objects (DLOs) while simultaneously ensuring robustness, accuracy, and temporally consistent state estimation remains a fundamental challenge in robot perception. We introduce MotionDLO, a real-time tracking framework specifically designed to overcome these limitations in temporal continuity and latency. The method exploits the high temporal resolution and sparsity of event-based cameras and combines segmentation with the Coherent Point Drift (CPD) algorithm under the principles of Motion Coherence Theory. This integration enables temporally consistent shape estimation while maintaining a low computational overhead. Existing event-based tracking methods are typically computationally efficient but exhibit reduced accuracy compared to frame-based approaches, or alternatively compromise event sparsity to achieve competitive performance. To resolve this trade-off, we propose a hybrid event- and frame-based tracking architecture that preserves the complementary strengths of both sensing modalities. The event stream ensures high-frequency motion updates, while frame-based information stabilizes spatial accuracy and object identity. We demonstrate that the proposed framework reliably associates DLO instances across video sequences, enabling robust perception for robotic manipulation tasks. Experimental results validate real-time performance at 12 ms update rates and accurate shape tracking with an point-to-curve error as measurement of accuracy of up to 0.43 mm, supporting dynamic path adaptation during manipulation. The source code and demonstration datasets are publicly available.

title: LD4WAM: Learning Latent Dynamics from Human Videos for World Action Models
summary: Human video is playing an increasingly central role in training World Action Models (WAMs), owing to its diversity and low collection cost relative to teleoperated robot data. However, most WAMs learn from such video only by predicting pixel-level future frames, giving dynamics that are not directly actionable, whereas motion retargeting recovers directly actionable actions but leaves a large visual gap across embodiments. We therefore propose motion-aligned latent dynamics as an embodiment-agnostic representation to bridge video priors and low-level actions. We further present LD4WAM, which pairs a Latent Dynamics Model trained with semantic reconstruction and real motion alignment with a World Dynamics Action Model built as a mixture-of-transformers (MoT), which preserves full future-video generation and uses learnable queries to distill these latent dynamics from generated futures for action conditioning. Pretrained on our curated unified dataset of over 5{,}000 hours of human and robot data, LD4WAM performs strongly in RoboTwin simulation and on real robots equipped with both grippers and dexterous hands, while generalizing well to unseen objects and backgrounds.

title: Robust Bimanual Vision-Language-Action Models via Embarrassingly Simple Modality Masking
summary: Query-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer low-latency inference that is attractive for bimanual robotic manipulation, but we observe that they can still exhibit discontinuous actions and execution failures in complex dual-arm tasks. We hypothesize that unstable multi-view and language fusion is one contributing factor in these failures, often coinciding with attention spreading to distracting regions. To improve robustness, we introduce the Modality Masking Mechanism (M3), an embarrassingly simple, training-only strategy that requires no architectural changes or large-scale robot pretraining. M3 stochastically masks subsets of modality channels during training, exposing the policy to controlled partial observations and encouraging it to rely less on distracting cues and more on evidence that remains reliable.
