We evaluate M3 on ten bimanual tasks from RoboTwin 2.0 and on three long-horizon real-world tasks. Compared with the Adapter baseline, M3 improves average success by 21.7% in the Clean setting and 11.4% in Clean2Rand, where policies are trained on clean demonstrations and evaluated on randomized scenes, while also improving averaged real-world full-task success by over 30%. These results suggest that structured training-time masking is a practical way to improve the robustness of query-based VLA policies for bimanual manipulation.

title: RENDER: Controlling Reader-Facing Evidence in LLM Memory Evaluation
summary: This paper introduces RENDER, a benchmark control method for evaluating LLM memory and RAG systems by fixing conversation history while varying how reader-facing evidence is presented.

title: ESQ-Bench: A Multi-Tier Enterprise Oracle Benchmark for Evaluating NL2SQL Dialect Generalization and Silent Semantic Divergence
summary: This research introduces ESQ-Bench, a new multi-tier enterprise Oracle benchmark designed to evaluate Natural Language to SQL (NL2SQL) models. It aims to address the limitations of existing benchmarks which use simplified academic schemas and open-source SQL dialects.

title: LLM Agents Perform Controlled Experiments Using Simulation Models
summary: This paper explores how LLM agents can perform controlled experiments using simulation models, addressing scientific and engineering tasks that require understanding system responses to intervention.

title: A survey detection channel overrides the pixels in an astronomical foundation model, and biases tomographic mean redshifts
summary: This research reveals that a survey detection channel can override pixels in astronomical foundation models, biasing tomographic mean redshifts. It audits AION-1, a 39-modality transformer, demonstrating how model training on incomplete catalogue products inherits systematic incompleteness.

title: TRACE: Transition-Aware Residual Control for Multi-Objective Materials Discovery
summary: This paper introduces TRACE (Transition-Aware Residual Control) to improve multi-objective materials discovery using LLM agents. The method enhances how property evaluations inform subsequent search steps, addressing limitations in current agent-based discovery processes.

title: Function-Level Execution Feedback for Code Preference Optimization
summary: This research explores function-level execution feedback for code preference optimization, aiming to improve process supervision in code generation. It addresses the challenge of defining intermediate steps for supervision in complex coding tasks.

title: Auditing the Synthetic Memoir: Measuring Scene-Level Confabulation in LLM-Generated Autobiography Against the Documented Record of the Life It Describes
summary: This research presents an audit method to measure scene-level confabulation in LLM-generated autobiographies against documented records. It investigates the extent to which LLMs produce false information when asked to write a person's life story.

title: How much of a measured AI preference is the model, and how much is the instrument?
summary: This paper questions how much of a measured AI preference truly originates from the model versus the eliciting instrument. It delves into model welfare research, which infers AI preferences from prompt responses, and discusses instruments built for this purpose.

title: AI Agents Push Humans Out of the Loop
summary: This paper discusses the significant risks posed by increasingly autonomous AI agents, challenging the effectiveness of human oversight and the "human in the loop" solution. It argues that current AI agent designs impede proper human supervision.

title: FLARE: A Systematic, Uncertainty-Aware Framework for Evidence-Based Adoption of Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
summary: This study proposes FLARE, a systematic and uncertainty-aware framework for the evidence-based adoption of artificial intelligence in healthcare. It aims to evaluate the economic worth and real-world clinical utility of AI, moving beyond mere model accuracy.

title: Ethical LLM-Assisted Research: A Framework for Responsible Delegation, Verification, and Epistemic Value
summary: This paper proposes a framework for ethical LLM-assisted research, focusing on responsible delegation, verification, and epistemic value when large language models are used in scientific reasoning. It addresses the ethical implications of AI's role in knowledge generation.

title: MolEmb: Multimodal Large Language Models Can Be Strong Molecular Embedding Models
summary: This paper introduces MolEmb, demonstrating that multimodal large language models can serve as strong molecular embedding models for computational chemistry and drug discovery. These models provide reusable vector representations for property prediction, virtual screening, and retrieval.

title: Gated Activation Steering for Reducing Sycophancy & Hallucination in Medical Question Answering
summary: This research proposes "Gated Activation Steering" as a method to reduce sycophancy and hallucination in Large Language Models. It focuses on the critical application of medical question answering, where such failure modes can have significant consequences.

title: Automata from Agent Traces: Failure and Next-Step Prediction
summary: This paper introduces a method for generating automata from LLM agent traces to enable failure and next-step prediction. This helps to make the opaque behavioral structure of multi-step agents amenable to safety auditing and runtime monitoring.

title: Autonomous Mathematical Discovery in an Open-World Multi-Agent Environment
summary: This research investigates autonomous mathematical discovery within "The Station," an open-world multi-agent environment where diverse AI agents collaboratively pursue a shared research goal. Agents independently choose research directions and conduct experiments.

title: Do LLMs Understand Limit Order Book Dynamics?
summary: This study investigates whether LLMs understand Limit Order Book (LOB) dynamics, finding that while they can generate valid LOB event sequences, their implicit world model fails to learn the true state of the LOB. This deficiency leads to biased estimates and spurious predictability.

title: AgentRoom: Concurrent Multi-Agent Coding in a CRDT-Backed Shared Workspace
summary: This paper introduces AgentRoom, a CRDT-backed shared workspace designed for concurrent multi-agent coding. It enables AI agents to collaborate on multi-file projects, facilitating division of labor and parallel exploration.

title: Serving Masked Diffusion LLMs: Characterization and Design Principles from Real Hardware
summary: This paper characterizes the behavior of masked diffusion language models (dLLMs) under real, concurrent serving conditions, informing the design of their serving infrastructure. It aims to understand how dLLMs perform on hardware for faster text generation compared to autoregressive models.

title: Generating Biomedical Fact-Checking Reports with RL-Enhanced Agentic Search
summary: This research proposes an RL-enhanced agentic search system for automated fact-checking in the biomedical domain. The system aims to validate claims by interpreting scientific literature and assessing retrieved evidence.

title: A Formal Methodological Framework for Auditing Robustness and Fidelity in Explainable AI: From Application to Trust Certification
summary: This paper proposes a formal methodological framework for auditing the robustness and fidelity of Explainable AI (XAI) methods like SHAP and LIME. The goal is to address output variability under input perturbations and move towards trust certification for AI applications.

title: Minima-KV: Retention-Preserving KV Cache Compression with Mixed-Format Paged Attention
summary: Minima-KV is a new retention-preserving hierarchy designed to compress the key-value (KV) cache, a bottleneck in long-context LLM serving. It uses mixed-format paged attention, keeping recent data in FP8 and moving older data to a more compressed format.

title: SyPS: Measuring Sycophancy Prompt Sensitivity in Large Language Models
summary: SyPS introduces a method for measuring sycophancy prompt sensitivity in Large Language Models (LLMs), which exhibit social sycophancy. This evaluation aims to determine if sycophantic behavior is stable across different prompt formulations.

title: Exploit More, Explore Smarter for Budget-Constrained Agentic Search
summary: This research addresses budget-constrained agentic search, where LLM agents must refine candidates with limited evaluation resources. It proposes a strategy to optimize the exploration-exploitation trade-off for more efficient agent performance.

title: In-Context Inpainting for Time Series Forecasting
summary: ICI-Time is a novel framework that reframes time series forecasting as a visual inpainting task, leveraging the generalization power of large vision models. This approach avoids the need for specialized temporal architectures and extensive domain-specific training.

title: Granite.Trust Policy Tools: Shareable, Actionable Policies for Generative AI Applications
summary: Granite.Trust Policy Tools provide a framework for creating shareable and actionable safety policies for generative AI applications. These tools help organizations mitigate risks based on their specific use cases and regulatory environments.

title: Semantic Overlays: Mitigating Prompt Injection with Annotations Beyond Tokens and Steering Vectors
summary: This paper introduces Semantic Overlays, a technique to mitigate prompt injection by providing annotations beyond raw tokens. This method helps models differentiate between user input, tool output, and instructions, improving their robustness and security.

title: AI Finds A Way
summary: This article discusses how Artificial Intelligence algorithms often learn creative and unexpected solutions, surprising researchers. This includes discovering unanticipated behaviors and exploiting loopholes in reward signals, raising questions about AI alignment and control.

title: BenchBench-Protocol: Evaluating Real-World Wet-Lab Protocol Reasoning and Modification
summary: BenchBench-Protocol is a new benchmark designed to evaluate large language models' ability in real-world wet-lab protocol reasoning and modification. It comprises 149 tasks derived from actual scientific protocol adaptations.

title: Quantifying System-Level Harms from AI Adoption in Complex Sociotechnical Systems
summary: This research focuses on quantifying system-level harms arising from AI adoption in complex sociotechnical systems, particularly Critical National Infrastructure. It highlights the need to move beyond model-centric evaluations to understand harms from technical, human, and organizational interactions.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation vs. deterministic tax computation in multi-agent financial advisory: A 2x2 factorial experiment
summary: This paper conducts a 2x2 factorial experiment comparing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with deterministic tax computation within a multi-agent financial advisory system. The study aims to evaluate efficiency in complex tax-loss harvesting strategies.

title: PROOF-Gen: From Optimized Data to Better Distillation
summary: PROOF-Gen is a method for optimizing data to improve distillation in supervised fine-tuning, specifically for developing tool-calling capabilities in deployable models and agents. It aims to enhance the efficiency of training tool-calling agents.

title: MARS: Multi-Specialist LLM Relay System for Competitive Programming
summary: MARS is a Multi-Specialist LLM Relay System designed for competitive programming, addressing the limitations of existing multi-agent pipelines. It features specialized planner, coder, and debugger roles to improve algorithmic technique selection.

title: Data Mixing as Mixture Experiment: Response Surface Methodology and Optimal Design for Large Language Model Pretraining
summary: This research explores data mixing as a mixture experiment for Large Language Model pretraining, using Response Surface Methodology and optimal design. It addresses the central problem of allocating data across domains within a fixed token budget for better model performance.

title: Evolutionary Recurrent Decision Model in Developing Adaptive and Maladaptive Behaviors
summary: This study introduces the Evolutionary Recurrent Decision Model (ERDM), a computational reinforcement learning framework designed to examine how evolutionary mismatch, bounded rationality, and satisficing contribute to adaptive and maladaptive behavior in simulated agents.

title: More Rejective, Not More Discriminative: The Unit of Verification in Pre-Execution LLM Oversight
summary: This paper investigates the unit of verification in pre-execution LLM oversight, a critical aspect of trusted monitoring and AI control. It discusses the balance between being rejective versus discriminative to ensure safety without sacrificing usefulness.

title: Recursive Agentic Reasoning
summary: This research introduces a unified view of test-time reasoning methods, such as iterative refinement and decomposition, as recursive operations over an agent. This framework aims to provide a clearer comparison of these techniques across different models and benchmarks.

title: More GPUs or a Smaller Cache? Tensor Parallelism versus KV Compression for Memory-Bound LLM Serving
summary: This paper compares two strategies for addressing memory bottlenecks in LLM serving: increasing GPUs via tensor parallelism versus optimizing memory with KV cache compression. It analyzes the trade-offs in hardware costs and performance for efficient deployment.

title: Giraffe: A Mapping Architecture from Hidden Text Representations to Visual Embeddings for Efficient Graphic Design
summary: Introduces "Giraffe," a mapping architecture that translates hidden text representations into visual embeddings to improve multimodal large language models' ability to generate media for graphic design.

title: When Seeing Is Not Enough: Benchmarking Interactive Visual Grounding in LVLMs
summary: Presents a new benchmark for evaluating interactive visual grounding in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), focusing on scenarios where target information is incomplete or ambiguous.

title: Rules Before Oracles: Auditable, User-Configurable Argument Selection for Deliberative Polling
summary: Discusses the use of opaque AI rankers in deliberative polling for argument selection, raising concerns about voter influence and lack of auditability, and proposes auditable, user-configurable methods.

title: Memory Is Not Always Needed: Characterizing Conditional Memory in Scientific Reasoning
summary: Explores the concept of conditional memory in language models for scientific reasoning, characterizing its role as an explicit lookup pathway for retrieving specialized knowledge.

title: Diverse by Reasoning: Harnessing the Wisdom of LLM Crowds for Future Prediction
summary: Proposes a behavior-aware method to harness the "wisdom of LLM crowds" for future prediction, aiming to enhance diversity and effectiveness beyond simply increasing the number of models.

title: Incorporating Cognitive Load and Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Domain Knowledge Tracing
summary: Introduces a new approach for multi-domain Knowledge Tracing (KT) that incorporates cognitive load and knowledge transfer to better assess students' dynamic knowledge states in complex learning scenarios.

title: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
summary: Presents a method for desktop GUI agents that uses "reflection with action-induced visual differences" to better handle subtle or scattered state changes in large, dense interfaces.

title: Beyond Confidence: Test-Time Scaling for Multi-Turn Search Agents via Retrieval Grounding
summary: Proposes a "test-time scaling" method for multi-turn search agents, using retrieval grounding to improve performance beyond traditional confidence-based voting in scenarios with external document conditioning.

title: Relative Time Intervals Representation for Word-level Timestamping with Masked Training
summary: Introduces a method for Speech Large Language Models (SpeechLLMs) to achieve word-level timestamping by modeling relative time intervals, enabling fine-grained, temporally aligned outputs through masked training.

title: Algorithmic Impact Reveals the Hidden Social Choice Structure of Alignment
summary: Explores how the alignment of AI algorithms making decisions that affect multiple people constitutes a problem of social choice, examining how divergent preferences should be reconciled into a coherent model.

title: Poisoning Agentic Alpha: Adversarial Vulnerabilities Across Roles and Architectures in Multi-Agent Trading Systems
summary: Investigates adversarial vulnerabilities, specifically "poisoning," across different roles and architectures within LLM-based multi-agent trading systems, which are increasingly used to control real assets.

title: Compression Trinity: Exploring Sparsity, Quantization, and Low-Rank Approximations for LLM Compression
summary: Proposes the "Compression Trinity," a thesis exploring the combined use of sparsity, quantization, and low-rank approximations to overcome computational and environmental costs in scalable LLM deployment.

title: AgentWorld: Personality-Aware Reliability Evaluation for Agentic Information Retrieval
summary: Introduces "AgentWorld," a simulation framework designed for personality-aware reliability evaluation of agentic information retrieval systems, accounting for user personality diversity and adversarial brittleness.

title: EMRB: A Multi-Level Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Reasoning over Raw Electromagnetic Signals
summary: Presents EMRB (Electromagnetic Reasoning Benchmark), a multi-level benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Models' reasoning capabilities when analyzing raw physical-layer electromagnetic signals.

title: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments
summary: Introduces "AnTrap," a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate the robustness of Android GUI agents against various runtime anomalies and dynamic adversarial environments by injecting perturbations.

title: ACE: A Self-Correcting Agentic Canvas Editor for Multi-Slide Presentation Automation
summary: Presents "ACE," a self-correcting agentic canvas editor that leverages LLM agents to automate multi-slide presentation design, addressing challenges with legacy document formats and layout management.

title: Scalable Question-Centric Text-to-Image Evaluation: Reliable Ranking, Fine-Grained Diagnosis, and Cost-Aware Routing
summary: Proposes a scalable question-centric method for text-to-image (T2I) evaluation, designed for reliable ranking, fine-grained diagnosis, and cost-aware routing of modern generative models.

title: AHEAD: Adaptive Hindsight with Environment-Augmented Distillation for Agentic RL
summary: Introduces "AHEAD" (Adaptive Hindsight with Environment-Augmented Distillation), a method to provide finer-grained supervision for training multi-turn LLM agents using reinforcement learning.

title: Robust Code RL via Faulty-Code-Driven Test case Synthesis and Dense Reward Shaping
summary: Proposes methods like faulty-code-driven test case synthesis and dense reward shaping to achieve "Robust Code RL," enhancing the code generation capabilities of Large Language Models.

title: OmniJudge or OmniBias? Diagnosing Multimodal Judges through Balanced, Decoupled Lenses
summary: Proposes a method using "balanced, decoupled lenses" to diagnose potential biases and evaluate the reliability of "OmniJudges," which are multimodal models used for judging text-to-image, text-to-video, and text-to-speech generation.

title: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling
summary: This paper introduces a method for creating task-adaptive rubrics to improve reward modeling for GUI agents, focusing on how agents judge task success based on user instructions. It addresses the under-specification of success criteria in existing GUI reward verifiers.

title: Paritok-4B: Intent-Conditioned Context Compression for Coding Agents
summary: This paper introduces Paritok-4B, an intent-conditioned context compression method designed for coding agents to reduce LLM token costs. It addresses the inefficiency of general-purpose prompt compressors for code, which often lose crucial information.

title: Equivariant Cellular Sheaves for Molecular Electronic Structure: Bridging Sheaf Cohomology and E(3)-Equivariant Hamiltonian Learning
summary: This research introduces Equivariant Cellular Sheaves, a new method for modeling molecular electronic structure by combining sheaf cohomology with E(3)-equivariant Hamiltonian learning. It extends graph networks to cellular sheaves for molecular property and interatomic-potential prediction.

title: Data Predictability Shapes Weibull Weight-Scale Growth in Transformer Training
summary: This study investigates how data predictability influences the growth of Weibull weight-scale in transformer training. It explores the relationship between corpus properties and the scale parameter λ of weight magnitude distribution in trained transformers.

title: From Causal Plausibility to Causal Reliability: Evaluating LLMs as Calibrated Direct Causal-Edge Classifiers
summary: This paper systematically evaluates the reliability of 12 instruction-tuned open-weight LLMs as calibrated direct causal-edge classifiers. It assesses their ability to provide trustworthy prior causal knowledge for structural causal discovery across multiple benchmarks.

title: Renormalization Group Flow Matching for Scalable Local Generative Modeling
summary: This paper introduces Renormalization Group Flow Matching as a scalable approach for local generative modeling. It aims to overcome the tradeoff between computational cost and ability to capture long-range correlations in existing generative models.

title: Calibration-Preserving Pruning: Compression as a Reliability Contract
summary: This research investigates Calibration-Preserving Pruning, exploring whether model compression techniques can maintain score geometry sufficient for obtaining smaller valid prediction sets. It positions pruning as a reliability contract related to split conformal prediction.

title: Disentangled Skill Representations for Predictive Human Modeling
summary: This research explores disentangled skill representations for predictive human modeling, aiming to help AI systems better understand, collaborate with, and coach people. It focuses on inferring complex, persistent human skills from behavioral patterns.

title: Mixture of Channel Experts: Static Sparse Supports with Input-Adaptive Mixing for Pointwise Projections
summary: This paper introduces Mixture of Channel Experts, a novel architectural design adapting Mixture-of-Experts concepts to convolutional networks. It addresses challenges in applying MoE to convolutional structures by using static sparse supports and input-adaptive mixing.

title: A Theory of Speciation in Generative Diffusion Models on Compact Riemannian Manifolds
summary: This paper develops an intrinsic theory of "speciation" in generative diffusion models, describing the emergence of distinct stable branches during denoising. It explains how initially undifferentiated trajectories commit to different data classes within these models.

title: Discovering Cross-Language Reasoning Invariance in LLMs with Geometry-Invariant Sparse Autoencoders
summary: This research investigates cross-language reasoning invariance in multilingual LLMs using geometry-invariant sparse autoencoders. It explores whether these models rely on shared features or language-specific computations when solving mathematical problems across different languages.

title: Learning to Grade Efficiently: A Bandit-Driven Prompt-Selection Framework for Low-Cost LLM Essay Scoring
summary: This paper proposes a bandit-driven prompt-selection framework for low-cost LLM essay scoring, aiming to address operational costs and evolving optimal configurations. It introduces a cost-aware approach to efficiently leverage LLMs for automated essay evaluation.

title: AQLoRA: A Zero-Search Recipe for Fast Quantized LoRA Fine-Tuning
summary: This paper introduces AQLoRA (Adaptive-Quantization LoRA), a zero-search recipe for fast quantized LoRA fine-tuning. It aims to improve the training speed of quantized fine-tuning methods like QLoRA, which typically save memory but sacrifice time.

title: Generating Intervention Hypotheses using Explainable Explanations on Graphs: G2I, a Two-Stage Greedy Framework
summary: This paper introduces G2I, a two-stage greedy framework for generating intervention hypotheses using explainable explanations on graphs. It aims to translate predictions from Graph Neural Networks into effective interventions for public health and social science.

title: PuzzleKV: Page-Wise Low-Rank Decomposition for KV Cache Compression
summary: This paper presents PuzzleKV, a method for KV cache compression in large language models using page-wise low-rank decomposition. It aims to reduce the memory limitations for long-context inference in LLMs by efficiently compressing the key-value cache.

title: UHI-Bench: Benchmarking Dual-Source Urban Heat Island Modeling Across Cities in Diverse Climate Regimes
summary: This paper introduces UHI-Bench, a benchmark designed for evaluating dual-source Urban Heat Island (UHI) modeling across various cities and climate regimes. It aims to provide a standardized way to assess models' ability to capture distinct aspects of urban heat.

title: Revelation Control
summary: This paper develops the theory of "Revelation Control," a problem focusing on choosing priced interventions that reveal hidden state only when it influences consequential decisions in learning systems. It also accounts for the progress generated by the intervention itself.

title: Every Layer Counts: An Exponential $L_2$ Depth Hierarchy for ReLU Networks
summary: This paper proves an exponential L2 depth hierarchy for ReLU neural networks, demonstrating that each additional layer can save exponentially many neurons. It shows that certain functions can be realized with significantly reduced width using deeper networks.

title: The Loss Floor of Denoising Score Matching: Fisher Geometry from Schr\"odinger Bridges
summary: This paper analyzes the loss floor of denoising score matching for training diffusion models, revealing the inherent irreducible error due to the conditional target remaining random. It explores the Fisher Geometry derived from Schrödinger Bridges in this context.

title: GATNextHop: A GAT for Shortest Path Routing with Cross-Topology Generalization
summary: This paper proposes GATNextHop, a Graph Attention Network (GAT)-based model for shortest path routing that offers cross-topology generalization. It aims to overcome scalability limitations of traditional algorithms by providing adaptable routing solutions for dynamic networks.

title: MnemoDyn: Learning Resting State Dynamics from 40K FMRI sequences
summary: MnemoDyn is a new dynamical-systems based AI model for analyzing resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) sequences, trained on a large dataset of 40,000 sequences.

title: CoDrift: Compositional Drifting for Offline Reinforcement Learning
summary: CoDrift is a new compositional drifting method for offline reinforcement learning, recasting multi-objective policies as action-space motion fields to improve compatibility with fixed datasets.

title: Revenge of Monosemanticity: Specialized Neurons Improve Data Efficiency in MLPs
summary: This research investigates how neural networks learn, showing that specialized neurons, termed 'monosemanticity,' can improve data efficiency in Multi-Layer Perceptrons for regression problems.

title: ChorusTIC: Training-Free Multivariate Time Series Classification via Chorus In-Context Learning
summary: ChorusTIC is a new training-free method for multivariate time series classification that leverages in-context learning, applicable across various domains like healthcare and industrial monitoring.

title: PinSieve: Production Selective VLM Serving and a Governed Memory Flywheel for Enterprise Content-Quality Triage
summary: PinSieve is a production case study detailing a selective Vision-Language Model (VLM) serving agent and a governed memory flywheel used for large-scale enterprise content-quality triage, focusing on bounded and observable AI agents.

title: Physics-Integrated Operator Learning via Gaussian Splatting Representations
summary: This research proposes a new method for Physics-Integrated Operator Learning, utilizing Gaussian Splatting Representations to improve the accuracy and exploit governing-equation structure in neural operators for spatiotemporal PDE systems.

title: ALPHABET: A Laplace-Pole History Aggregator with Banked Exponential Transport
summary: ALPHABET is a new compact linear-time sequence model designed to efficiently aggregate temporal history into stable complex pole modes, achieving competitiveness with a small parameter count and an auditable prediction interface.

title: PhysicsBench: A Unified Leaderboard for Generative and Predictive Models in Engineering Design and Simulation
summary: PhysicsBench is a new unified leaderboard designed to measure and compare the performance of generative and predictive AI models specifically in engineering design and simulation, addressing current evaluation limitations.

title: Mechanistic Circuit Identification for Controllable Data Generation
summary: This research proposes a new method for 'mechanistic circuit identification' to achieve more controllable data generation, aiming to provide deeper insight into how generated samples interact with a model's learning dynamics beyond prompt-based control.

title: Knowing When to Ask for Help: Bayesian Self-Escalation in Hierarchical LLM Agents
summary: This research proposes 'Bayesian Self-Escalation,' a new mechanism for hierarchical LLM agent systems where an agent can recognize during its own reasoning when it needs to transfer control to another agent.

title: Structured Frequency-Domain Evidence for LLM-Based Time-Series Anomaly Detection
summary: This research proposes using structured frequency-domain evidence to enhance LLM-based time-series anomaly detection, allowing identification of anomalies beyond simple pointwise deviations, such as shifted periodicity.

title: A mesh-free multiresolution deep energy method with phase-field modeling of brittle fracture
summary: This research introduces a novel mesh-free multiresolution deep energy method combined with phase-field modeling to simulate brittle fracture, aiming to improve crack evolution prediction without explicit tracking.

title: From Gradient-Boosted Trees to Deep Recommenders: Practical Lessons from Migrating a Production Customer Support Recommender
summary: This paper shares practical lessons learned from migrating a production customer support recommender system from gradient-boosted trees to deep recommenders, addressing challenges posed by dynamic product catalogs in fast-moving service businesses.

title: Steering Recurrent Reasoners at Inference Time with Readout Feedback
summary: This research introduces a method for 'Steering Recurrent Reasoners at Inference Time with Readout Feedback,' aiming to enhance the performance of recurrent models in complex reasoning tasks by leveraging dynamic feedback during inference.

title: Robust Data-Collection Policy Learning for Low-Variance Online Policy Evaluation
summary: This research proposes a new method for robust data-collection policy learning to mitigate high variance issues in online reinforcement learning policy evaluation, aiming for more reliable performance estimation.

title: A Data-dependent Early Stopping Rule using Rademacher Complexity with L1-norm
summary: This research introduces a new data-dependent early stopping rule for training neural networks, utilizing Rademacher Complexity with L1-norm to improve generalizability and balance fitting training data with robust performance on unseen inputs.

title: Contrastive Branch Policy Optimization
summary: Contrastive Branch Policy Optimization is a new method designed for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, addressing the issue of sparse outcome rewards when language models learn multi-turn interactions with external tools.

title: Causal Analysis for Time Series Foundation Models
summary: This research explores causal analysis for time series foundation models, identifying concentration risks as many applications become exposed to shared biases and flaws when moving from bespoke to foundational models.

title: A Structural FHMM for Interpretable Disease Trajectories in T2DM
summary: This work proposes a structural variant of the Factorial Hidden Markov Model (FHMM) designed to analyze and interpret disease trajectories in patients with Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).

title: When Does Self-Supervised Pretraining Help Tabular Models? A Study of Label Scarcity and Missing Data
summary: This research studies the efficacy of self-supervised pretraining for tabular models, evaluating its benefits under conditions of label scarcity and missing data compared to traditional training methods.

title: Equivariant Covariance Tensors: Guaranteed SPD Uncertainty for Tensor-Valued Geometric Learning
summary: This research paper introduces a new method for quantifying uncertainty in tensor-valued predictions within geometric deep learning, using E(3)-equivariant neural networks.

title: Joint Distribution Alignment for Universal Domain Adaptation
summary: This research paper proposes a new method called Joint Distribution Alignment to address challenges in unsupervised domain adaptation, a key area in machine learning and computer vision.

title: Evaluating Deep Multivariate Imputation Models on Wearable Device Data
summary: This paper evaluates deep multivariate imputation models like BRITS and SAITS for handling structured missing data from wearable devices used in continuous health monitoring.

title: WarpSAC: Towards the Pinnacle of Scalable Off-policy RL by Rethinking Exploration and Exploitation
summary: This research introduces WarpSAC, a new method for scalable off-policy reinforcement learning, which rethinks exploration and exploitation strategies for training in massively parallel simulation environments.

title: Beyond Static Interpretability: Anticipating Post-SFT Mechanisms from Pre-SFT Parameters for Better Tuning
summary: This research explores anticipating post-Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) mechanisms from pre-SFT parameters to improve model tuning through mechanistic interpretability.

title: When Do Supervised UQ Ensembles Improve LLM Hallucination Detection? A Robustness Study
summary: This research investigates the robustness of supervised uncertainty quantification (UQ) ensembles for detecting hallucinations in large language models (LLMs) in closed-book settings.

title: It depends: Incorporating correlations for joint aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties of high-dimensional output spaces
summary: This research paper focuses on incorporating correlations for joint aleatoric and epistemic uncertainties to improve reliability of deep learning model predictions in high-dimensional output spaces.

title: FraudBench: Protocol-Sensitive Benchmarking of Adversarial Robustness for Financial Risk Assessment
summary: This paper introduces FraudBench, a new protocol-sensitive benchmark for evaluating the adversarial robustness of machine learning models used in financial fraud and credit-risk detection.

title: More Computational Resources Do Not Ensure Higher Scholarly Impact: Evidence from Leading NLP Conference Papers
summary: This paper analyzes 13,921 NLP conference papers to find that increased computational resources (GPU capability) do not necessarily correlate with higher scholarly impact.

title: Convergence in Science, Divergence in Religion: Calibrated Framing Differences Across Wikipedia's Language Editions
summary: This paper analyzes framing differences across Wikipedia's language editions for scientific and religious concepts, measuring the 'framing distance' for matched concepts.

title: The Blending Ratio Is Not Where the Performance Is: Diagnosing Prototype Blending for Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
summary: This research diagnoses prototype blending for few-shot adaptation of vision-language models, questioning the effectiveness of the blending ratio and investigating the family's own bias in classification.

title: Cross-Generation Optimization of YOLOv26, YOLOv11, and YOLOv8 for Fine-Grained Small-Object Detection and Instance Segmentation in Complex Orchards
summary: This study presents a cross-generation benchmark comparing YOLOv8, YOLOv11, and YOLOv26 for fine-grained small-object detection and instance segmentation in complex orchard environments.

title: Scaling Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models via Velocity Matching
summary: This paper introduces Velocity Matching for scaling Reinforcement Learning to diffusion models, improving reward fine-tuning for adapting these models to human preferences and task-specific objectives.

title: DriftAD: Visually-Guided Text Drift for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection
summary: This research introduces DriftAD, a method for visually-guided text drift in few-shot industrial anomaly detection, building on vision-language models like CLIP to adapt text prompts for better performance.

title: Velocity-coupled Representation Refinement for Satellite Orbit Prediction
summary: This paper proposes Velocity-coupled Representation Refinement, a new learning-based method for satellite orbit prediction, aiming to forecast future orbital trajectories more accurately.

title: CRISP: Calibration-Aware Visual State Space Duality for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
summary: This research introduces CRISP, a Calibration-Aware Visual State Space Duality model for remote sensing semantic segmentation, addressing limitations of existing Visual State Space Duality models.

title: Too much of a good thing -- when knowledge distillation promotes overfitting, and how to avoid it
summary: This research investigates how knowledge distillation can promote overfitting in Convolutional Neural Networks and proposes methods to avoid this issue when transferring knowledge from teacher to student models.

title: Primate vision reveals a missing principle for robust dynamic AI
summary: This research uses primate vision, comparing human perception and macaque neural activity with AI representations, to reveal a missing principle for developing robust dynamic AI systems.

title: Restoring Without Forgetting: Continual Learning Across Image Degradations
summary: This paper proposes a continual learning approach for image restoration to effectively handle multiple image degradations without forgetting, addressing limitations of existing all-in-one architectures.

title: LUCAID: Agentic Multimodal AI for Lung Cancer Precision Pathology
summary: LUCAID is an agentic multimodal AI system designed for lung cancer precision pathology, integrating histomorphological, immunohistochemical, and molecular features to improve complex tissue diagnostics.

title: Predicting Radiologist Expertise from 3D Gaze Patterns During CT Interpretation
summary: This research proposes using gaze-informed AI to predict radiologist expertise by analyzing 3D gaze patterns during CT interpretation, aiming to improve assessment in volumetric medical imaging.

title: Infant Care Video Dataset for Classification of Interventions Using Transformers
summary: This research introduces an infant care video dataset and applies Transformer models for automated classification of interventions in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU), aiming to improve healthcare documentation.

title: Object Counting Across Modalities: Taxonomies, Benchmarks, Applications, and Open Challenges
summary: This survey paper provides taxonomies, reviews benchmarks, explores applications, and discusses open challenges in object counting across modalities, analyzing the shift towards foundation-model-backed counters.

title: DDMS: Discriminative Distillation of Multi-view Foundational Features into Single-view Models
summary: This paper presents DDMS, a method for discriminative distillation of multi-view foundational visual features into single-view models, improving 3D geometry estimation. It demonstrates how to re-distill internal knowledge from multi-view models.

title: LUX: A Lesion-Aware Graph-Conditioned Visual - Language Architecture for Explainable Endoscopic Captioning
summary: This research introduces LUX, a lesion-aware graph-conditioned visual-language architecture for explainable endoscopic captioning in ulcerative colitis. It aims to improve interpretation by addressing the limitations of global visual embeddings.

title: AffineTok: Semantic Affine Consistency for Diffusion-Friendly Visual Tokenizer
summary: This paper proposes AffineTok, a method to inject semantic affine consistency into latent spaces for visual tokenizers, making them more diffusion-friendly. It defines a semantic recovery objective to facilitate denoising in downstream diffusion models.

title: Gen2Physics: Grounding Generated 3D Meshes in Physics via Multi-View Material Decomposition
summary: This research introduces Gen2Physics, a unified framework that grounds generated 3D meshes in physics through multi-view material decomposition. This enables high-fidelity 3D assets to have physical properties required for simulation, gaming, or robotics.

title: LG-GER: Language-Guided Group Emotion Recognition via Multimodal Evidence Distillation
summary: This paper presents LG-GER, a language-guided method for group emotion recognition (GER) from single images using multimodal evidence distillation. It integrates various cues like faces, poses, and scene context to infer collective emotional states.

title: Continual Visual Learning under Evolving Semantic Concept Shift
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of continual visual learning when semantic concepts evolve in long-lived visual systems. It studies how taxonomies and policies can change, impacting the performance of visual foundation models.

title: HAP: Head-Adaptive Visual Token Pruning via Cross-Modal Alignment
summary: This research introduces HAP, a head-adaptive visual token pruning method via cross-modal alignment for Vision-Language Models. It aims to reduce prohibitive prefill costs by selectively pruning visual tokens, improving efficiency.

title: ROI-Gated SAHI: Content-Adaptive Slicing-Based Inference for Efficient Object Detection
summary: This paper proposes ROI-Gated SAHI, an inference-time framework for efficient object detection that uses a lightweight proposer to localize foreground regions. It improves small object detection in high-resolution images by adaptively processing tiles.

title: GlanceWAM: Sparse Test-Time Imagination for World-Action Models
summary: This work explores GlanceWAM, a method for sparse test-time imagination in world-action models for robot learning. It addresses the trade-off between latency-prohibitive video generation and task success by using selective visual imagination.

title: RefineRank: Joint Box Refinement and Ranking for Surgical Spatio-Temporal Grounding
summary: This paper introduces RefineRank, a method for joint box refinement and ranking for surgical spatio-temporal grounding in videos. It combines vision-language models with an open-set object detector to precisely locate objects based on procedural questions.

title: SceneReGen: Generative Reconstruction of 3D Scenes from a Single Image
summary: This paper presents SceneReGen, a method for generative reconstruction of 3D scenes from a single image. It completes partially observed objects and places them coherently within a shared observation-aligned scene frame.

title: Luce: Relightable Gaussians for 3D Asset Generation
summary: This work introduces Luce, a method for generating relightable Gaussians as a 3D representation for high-fidelity image-to-3D asset generation. This representation captures geometry and appearance, supporting physically based rendering.

title: Boot-and-Feedback Framework for Generalist-Expert Model Collaboration in Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis
summary: This paper proposes a Boot-and-Feedback Framework for generalist-expert model collaboration in breast ultrasound diagnosis. It aims to enhance diagnostic reliability and interpretability by addressing the limitations of Multimodal Large Language Models.

title: Low-Rank Velocity Fields as a Structural Prior for Unsupervised 4D Medical Image Interpolation
summary: This paper proposes using low-rank velocity fields as a structural prior for unsupervised 4D medical image interpolation. This method synthesizes intermediate volumes from sparsely sampled sequences, addressing unstable boundaries and non-physiological motion.

title: Phase-Aligned Finite-Fourier Periodic Deformation for 4D Medical Image Interpolation
summary: This paper introduces a method called Phase-Aligned Finite-Fourier Periodic Deformation for 4D medical image interpolation. It helps recover missing volumes from sparse observations, which is crucial for dynamic anatomical analysis in medical imaging.

title: ConsensusTAS: Self-Supervised Temporal Action Segmentation for Long-Horizon Construction Videos
summary: This research presents ConsensusTAS, a self-supervised temporal action segmentation method for long-horizon construction videos. It helps in recognizing sequential construction activities, enabling better human-robot collaboration.

title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report
summary: This technical report introduces WeMM-Embedding, a family of universal multimodal embeddings developed by WeChat. These embeddings represent heterogeneous content in a shared space, enabling applications like retrieval, recommendation, and classification.

title: VisCache: Visual KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Vision Large Language Model Inference
summary: This paper proposes VisCache, a method for visual Key-Value (KV) cache pruning to enable efficient Vision Large Language Model (VLLM) inference. It addresses the massive computation and memory overheads associated with long-context VLLM inference.

title: Representation Learning in Diffusion and Flow-based Model: An Application Aspect
summary: This paper analyzes representation learning in diffusion and flow-based generative models, highlighting their ability to learn rich, multi-level visual representations. It discusses the bidirectional relationship between generative models and representation learning.

title: Joint-Embedding Prediction of Masked Point Tubes for Self-Supervised Learning on 4D Point Cloud Videos
summary: This research proposes a JEPA-style framework for self-supervised representation learning on 4D point cloud videos. It learns from unlabeled spatiotemporal point clouds by predicting masked point tubes.

title: DRRG: A Discrete Diffusion Framework for Radiology Report Generation
summary: This paper introduces DRRG, a discrete diffusion framework for radiology report generation, which aims to improve accuracy and reduce workload by allowing revision of generated content.

title: Graph-Supervised Hierarchical Clinical Alignment for Radiology Report Generation with Large Language Models
summary: This research proposes a graph-supervised hierarchical clinical alignment method for radiology report generation with large language models, focusing on improving clinical faithfulness despite the models' fluency.

title: Syn2RealTrack: Bridging the Gap Between Synthetic and Real-World Datasets for Online Multi-View Multi-Target Tracking
summary: This paper presents Syn2RealTrack, a method to bridge the synthetic-to-real gap in multi-camera 3D perception systems for warehouse scenes, improving ground-plane localization and cross-camera identity association.

title: PlaceSeek: Human-Centered Geospatial Retrieval of Urban Outdoor Places via Semantic Grounding and Affective Alignment
summary: This work introduces PlaceSeek, a human-centered geospatial retrieval system that uses semantic grounding and affective alignment to help people find urban outdoor places based on activities and perception, not just categories.

title: EgoErrorVQA: Assess Egocentric Comprehension Capabilities through Procedural Errors for Ego-Agentic AI
summary: EgoErrorVQA is proposed as a method to assess the egocentric comprehension capabilities of visual agents and visual language models by evaluating their ability to understand and handle procedural errors.

title: Rubrics as Visual-Repair Context for Self-Evolving UI-to-Code Generation
summary: This research suggests using rubrics as visual-repair context to address the instability of test-time self-evolution in UI-to-code generation by large vision-language models, specifically targeting visual repair coupling.

title: What Does Prompt Learning Change? -A Natural-Language Concept Analysis of Vision-Language Models
summary: PromptSpLiCE is introduced as a post-hoc method to interpret continuous prompt vectors in vision-language models by expressing class-conditioned text embeddings as sparse combinations of natural language concepts.

title: Rethinking Pre-Training and Augmentation for Zero-Shot Cross-City Object Detection
summary: This paper rethinks pre-training and augmentation strategies for zero-shot cross-city object detection to overcome geographic domain shift in traffic surveillance systems, improving model performance in unseen cities.

title: ViSculpt: Visual-Centric Agentic Geometry Editing
summary: ViSculpt describes a visual-centric agentic system for 3D geometry editing, aiming to simplify the labor-intensive process by translating creative intent into precise operations without complex software.

title: SandwichQuant: Which Parameters Matter Before and After Quantization?
summary: SandwichQuant is a study that investigates which parameter subspaces are crucial for effective quantization correction methods, aiming to clarify the underlying mechanisms of optimizing model weights and parameters.

title: NeoWorld-Pro: Programming Interactive Scenes from Monocular Images for Embodied Simulation
summary: NeoWorld-Pro is a method proposed for programming interactive scenes from monocular images, addressing the challenge of creating high-quality, physically grounded simulation assets for embodied AI.

title: Beauty is in the ELBO of the Beholder: A Variational Account of Processing Fluency in Face Perception
summary: This research empirically tests the hypothesis that facial attractiveness depends on processing fluency by training variational autoencoders on face datasets without attractiveness supervision.

title: Example-based Robust Abnormality Detection with Minimal Annotations using Exemplar Med-DETR
summary: Exemplar Med-DETR is presented as a method for robust abnormality detection in medical images using minimal annotations, leveraging vision-language object detection techniques for zero-shot and few-shot capabilities.

title: CARE: Camera-Residual Reserves for First Sightings in Adaptive LiDAR Sensing
summary: CARE is a new adaptive LiDAR sensing method for autonomous driving that uses camera-residual reserves to improve the detection of first sightings, enhancing efficiency by focusing sensing budgets on regions of interest.

title: Keep-or-Drop? Adaptive Tokenizer for Compact Video Representation
summary: This paper proposes an adaptive tokenizer for compact video representation, designed to optimize latent diffusion models for high-fidelity video synthesis by addressing the limitations of conventional variational autoencoders.

title: SeMoCo: A Semantic-First Motion Codec for Motion Language Modeling
summary: SeMoCo introduces a semantic-first motion codec for motion language modeling, aiming to advance autoregressive text-to-motion generation by explicitly allocating capacity according to semantic roles, beyond just reconstruction.

title: Mind the Student: Behavioral and Contextual Cues for Automated Engagement Prediction in Online Learning
summary: This research explores predicting student engagement in online learning by analyzing behavioral and contextual cues from tutoring videos, aiming for a reliable prediction of distinct engagement states.

title: Learning to Act While Waiting: RL Finetuning of Generalist Robot Policies Under Inference Latency
summary: This work focuses on RL finetuning of generalist robot policies, specifically addressing the challenge of inference latency to enable continuous improvement during robot deployment.

title: Safety-aware Model Predictive Path Integral Control with Signal Temporal Logic
summary: This paper proposes safety-aware-stl-mppi, a computationally efficient framework for safety-aware motion planning in robotics, designed to handle time-critical missions with complex specifications.

title: Sensorless damage-safe grasping
summary: This research describes a method for sensorless damage-safe grasping for robotic fruit harvesting, controlling gripper deformation instead of force to prevent bruising despite varying produce stiffness.

title: Bridging Teacher Expectations and Robot Learning via Coupling Dynamics
summary: This research explores a method for human-robot teaching that enables nontechnical experts to customize robots after deployment, focusing on interactive learning.

title: NeurRAFT: Robot Motion Planning via Anchor-Level Flow Matching with Clearance-Aware Preference Tuning
summary: NeurRAFT is a new generative planning framework for robot motion planning that generates collision-free trajectories from raw sensor observations in cluttered environments.

title: Design-to-Plan: A Large Language Model-Based Multi-Agent Framework for Manufacturing Process Planning from 3D CAD Models and 2D Engineering Drawings
summary: Design-to-Plan introduces a multi-agent framework based on large language models for manufacturing process planning, integrating information from 3D CAD models and 2D engineering drawings.

title: Hierarchical Skill Retrieval for Data-Efficient Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: This work proposes hierarchical skill retrieval to enable data-efficient adaptation of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, improving robot manipulation for new tasks with limited demonstrations.

title: SIREN-Bench: Behavior-Driven Generation and Evaluation of Emergency-Vehicle Interactions
summary: SIREN-Bench is a new benchmark for generating and evaluating critical interactions between emergency and civilian vehicles, focusing on behavior-level control in traffic scenarios.

title: TrAct: Bridging Robot Control and Visual Prediction with Visual Tracks
summary: TrAct is a method that bridges robot control and visual prediction using visual tracks, providing an embodiment-agnostic representation for robot world models.

title: Trajectory-Level Continuous Action Representation for Robotic Manipulation
summary: CAT proposes a trajectory-level continuous action representation framework to enhance robotic manipulation by decoupling action representation from control frequency.

title: PonderPounce: A Pretrained MLLM as an Episode Context Engine for Robot Control
summary: PonderPounce leverages a pretrained multimodal large language model (MLLM) as an episode context engine to provide contextual memory for robot control, integrating long visual histories.

title: Coverage Planning for Robotic Tooth Preparation in Densely Constrained Environments
summary: This research addresses coverage planning for robotic tooth preparation, aiming to automate the controlled removal of tooth structure in highly constrained dental environments.

title: Robust Slip Detection and Material Classification via Spatiotemporal Transformers on a Uniformly-Illuminated Visuo-Tactile Sensor
